News.title: Vets warn of ‘hidden danger’ in summer grass that can cause blindness in dogs – as councils blamed for surge in cases
News.content:
PET OWNERS have been warned of a hidden danger lurking in parks and countryside fields that can cause blindness in dogs.

The UK has seen a surge in cases as the dry summer months continue.

The number of grass seed infections has increased across the country, as vets report more and more pets presenting issues with their ears and eyes.



The seeds, known as foxtail seeds, have a pointed shape and sharp barbs which allows them to work their way into ears, eyes, nostrils, and paws, and remain stuck.



If left untreated, the grassy barbs can damage ear canals, travel to internal organs and even cause blindness.

They are most commonly found in open areas like countryside fields, grassy verges, and parks, where pets can pick up the thorny seeds while sniffing or walking.

This has led to some owners blaming local councils for failing to cut grass and leaving pavements overgrown.



Once inside, a vet is needed to remove the barbs, which in severe cases can even result in surgery, costing thousands of pounds.

As a result, one vet clinic advised owners to regularly check their pets’ ears, paws and furs throughout their walk.

They said: “Grass seeds can cause a lot of pain, irritation and infection if not caught quickly.

“If you notice sudden head shaking, excessive licking, swelling, redness or signs of discomfort, please get in touch with us as soon as possible.”



Foxtail seed cases typically peak around June until September, where dry weather exacerbates the problem.

Owners have also been advised to take walks on freshly cut grass, and avoid unkempt or overgrown areas.

News.title: Boy, 15, in court charged with sex offences against 8 girls over three-year period including raping one aged under 13
News.content:
IN THE DOCK Boy, 15, in court charged with sex offences against 8 girls over three-year period including raping one aged under 13

A SCHOOLBOY has appeared in court charged with a string of sex offences against eight girls including raping one aged under 13.

The 15-year-old is accused of 22 charges in total allegedly carried out between 2022 and 2025.



He appeared at Wellingborough Youth Court today for a brief hearing.

The boy is charged with 12 counts of sexually assaulting a female, three counts of assaulting a girl under 13 by touching and one count of raping a girl under 13.



He is also accused of one count of assaulting a female aged 13 and over by penetration with a part of the body or thing and one count of raping a girl aged 13 to 15.

The teen is further charged with two counts of making an indecent photograph or pseudo-photograph of a child, and one count of possessing a prohibited image of a child.

He faces a further charge of possessing an extreme pornographic image or images.

The court heard the eight girls were aged between 10 and 15 at the time.

The teen, from Northamptonshire, spoke only to confirm his identity.

District Judge Amar Mehta told the boy: “Your case is too serious to be tried in this court. Therefore it’s going to be tried at the crown court at Northampton.



“I’m going to send your case to Northampton Crown Court for another hearing similar to this one.”

The teenager was told to appear at that court on August 18.

He was granted conditional bail instructing him not to contact the alleged victims, to have no unsupervised contact with females under 16, and to engage with the Northamptonshire Youth Justice Service.

News.title: Meet the glam python hunter who bagged $10k prize for catching record-shattering 60 predators in stunning outfits
News.content:
THE glamorous female python hunter who clinched a $10,000 prize for nabbing 60 reptiles is in the running for another huge payday.

Taylor Stanberry was among the crowd of brave handlers combing through south Florida as part of the annual python challenge.



But unlike other participants, she’s turning heads for posing with her blood-curdling catches in a stunning outfit and flashy smile.

Stanberry shocked the entire state in 2025 when she was crowned the first female winner of the competition hosted by wildlife authorities.



Each year, the state government incentivizes brave hunters to take aim at invasive Burmese pythons because they’re considered apex predators.

Although she dominated the competition last year, Stanberry made it clear she was most interested in protecting the land she calls home.

“It’s not about trophy hunting or just killing pythons because it’s fun […] I actually want to save the native wildlife,” she told NBC affiliate WBBH in 2025.

Stanberry starts her nights at around 7pm with her husband Rhett, and they explore some of the deepest corners of the jungle by boat, bike, and foot.

They hunt until 5am, trapping smaller pythons as food for their animals and shipping the larger beasts to leather companies.

This year, she’s vying for the prize again but admitted exhaustion and bad weather have made efforts a bit harder.



“It seems like a tropical storm, and the weather is going down to like 72 degrees,” she told Naples Daily News on Saturday.

Colder weather mean snakes are less likely to move around at night, and lightning means she and her husband can’t take out their boat.

But the resilient hunter refuses to back down and is staying out even later in the night to beat out the rest of the crowd.



“A lot of people seem to get pretty tired and die out by like 2am,” she said.

“There’s a huge rush between 8pm and 2am, so we’re going from midnight to six in the morning.”

While Stanberry hunts for snakes on a daily basis outside of the competition, she said the intense scuffle has made her reconsider entering next year.

Still, she’s working hard for another $10,000 prize which will go into some car repairs and her exotic wildlife sanctuary.

“I feel like we’re just going to put a lot of the money back into the gas, and we need new tires now because we’re running that car like crazy,” she said.



“But, obviously, any amount of money is going to go to the animal sanctuary because any extra money for that is really what I need.”

News.title: Brit dad, 37, charged after son, 2, fell from fourth-floor window of Cyprus hotel and died while on family holiday
News.content:
HOLIDAY HORROR Brit dad, 37, charged after son, 2, fell from fourth-floor window of Cyprus hotel and died while on family holiday

THE Brit dad whose toddler died after falling from a fourth floor window in Cyprus has been charged with causing death by recklessness.

The two-year-old boy fell to his death at a luxury in Cyprus hotel last week, allegedly slipping from his dad’s arms and plunging 33ft to the veranda below.



The dad, 37, was released on bail after being held behind bars for eight days.

He had to pay a £17,000 bail and was compelled to surrender his passport by the Paphos District Court.



He is banned from leaving Cyprus and will next appear in court on July 31.

The young boy, locally reported to be three, but understood by The Sun to be two, was declared dead as he arrived in hospital after the horrifying fall from a fourth- floor window.

His Brit banker dad had begged to be released so that he could explain the tragedy to his young daughter and appeared emotional in court.

The two-year-old’s sister had only been told that her brother was in hospital and did not yet understand that he would never be coming home.

The dad was expected to be let out of police custody on Wednesday but the release was blocked at the last minute.

He then had to tell his daughter the tragic news over Facetime.



The two-year-old was described as “deeply adored” and “a truly special, easy–going little boy who brought so much joy to everyone around him”.

Paphos police said “a quantity of alcohol” had been found in the dad’s blood during testing.

The small quantity of alcohol, reportedly equivalent to one or two drinks, was revealed after cops said the dad’s toxicology report had come back clean.

Investigators believe the boy’s dad and grandad were waiting for a lift to go to dinner when the tragedy occurred.

The dad was holding the child around his waist and swinging him from side to side as they waited, the court heard last week.



He then allegedly fell through his dad’s arms and tumbled through a window to his death from the hotel in Chloraka.

The 4ft wide, 8ft tall window could have been open without the father’s knowledge, investigators said.

If convicted, the dad could face up to four years in prison.

A spokesperson for the Attorney General told the Daily Mail: “The Attorney General ordered criminal prosecution of the father.

“He will be charged with causing death due to recklessness, among other things.



“The father will be released, yet he will be subject to strict restrictive conditions, which will aim to ensure his presence at all future hearings.”

News.title: Inside the deserted UK new-build estate that looks like a scene from the Wild West – as locals blast ‘disgusting’ delays
News.content:
OVER 100 homes are lying empty in a new UK housing estate due to “unfinished wiring”.

Development of the neighbourhood, which includes dozens of homes earmarked for social housing, has reportedly slowed in recent months.



Longshaw Drive in Little Hulton, Salford consists of 177 homes, however, only a dozen are currently occupied.

The estate was supposed to be completed earlier this year, with households ready to move in.



One of the few current residents described the neighbourhood as “a bit creepy”, reports Manchester Evening News.

Visiting the site, the outlet compared the almost empty estate to a “setting of a Western shootout”.



Once praised for being part of Salford council’s “largest social housing project in 50 years”, Longshaw Drive includes 93 council houses, with another 20 set aside for shared ownership, and 42 for private sale.

Dérive Registered Provider is heading the project, with a source telling Manchester Evening News that the delay has lost the local council “up to £1million”.



The company is currently under investigation for mismanagement, however, the town hall has said the empty houses are categorically “not part of the investigation”.

Longshaw Drive saw the first set of homes signed over to Dérive in June 2025, with residents moving in from September.

Since then, progress on the remaining homes appears to have been slowed down.

With more than 4,000 households currently waiting for social housing, locals have shared their frustrations over the delays.

One mum who is currently residing in temporary accommodation told Manchester Evening News: “It’s quite disgusting that they have so many people waiting yet delays like this aren’t being dealt with properly.”



Meanwhile, a source told the outlet that the delays are due to “missing electricity certificates” and “unfinished wiring”.

A spokesperson from Dérive Registered Provider previously said: “We acknowledge that it has taken longer than anticipated to bring a number of properties to market.

“This is for a range of reasons including bespoke adaptations for residents and electrical safety tests, as well as typical construction matters for a project of this scale and complexity.

“But we have and are working through this and are delighted to be letting homes to people.”

The rep added: “In total, 57 social homes have been let in the past six weeks.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“More homes are expected to become available in August once all remaining internal works on the water supplies have been completed, and these will be advertised through the Salford Homesearch website.”

The Sun has reached out to Dérive Registered Provider for comment.

News.title: Cruel owner, 52, who crammed 95 animals in ‘stinking’ shed in ‘worst ever’ conditions slapped with 10-year ban
News.content:
HOUSE OF HORRORS Cruel owner, 52, who crammed 95 animals in ‘stinking’ shed in ‘worst ever’ conditions slapped with 10-year ban

A WOMAN has been banned from keeping animals for 10 years after leaving cats, guinea pigs and chinchillas in horror conditions at her home.

Michelle Ashford, 52, crammed the animals into a “stinking” shed in Stowmarket, Suffolk, filled with flies and a “strong smell of ammonia”.



The cats had suffered wounds from fighting, with many ill and gruesome pictures showing one with heavy discharge around its eyes.

Officers from the RSPCA were appalled to discover over 95 animals – including 73 guinea pigs, 17 cats and five chinchillas – living in squalor in October.



A vet described the disgusting shed as “one of the worst environments, if not possibly the worst, that I have seen”.

They added: “The cats were desperate for attention, vying for affection at the front of the pen wanting to be stroked.

“It was so sad to see them being kept in such an unsuitable fashion.”

Ghastly pictures show dozens of guinea pigs trapped in filthy garden tubs inside a shed.



Another 30 were found free roaming in a different shed by the rescuers with the rest of the poor pets crammed into crates stacked on top of each other.

RSPCA Inspector Shahnaz Ahmad said that one baby “likely not more than a few days old, appeared to be getting trampled on by the bigger guinea pigs” in one of the dreadful cages.

Three of the most sickly guinea pigs had to sadly be euthanised, while two of the survivors each had an eye removed by vets.

Ashford even squished pet chinchillas into tiny cages inside a derelict cupboard in her house.

The exotic animals were found “hunched over, lethargic and depressed while in their cages” by the horrified Ahmad.



She lamented that “the bottom cage was not secure, and the two males escaped into the room after the cupboard door was open.

“I expressed to Ashford that the chinchillas would have no natural light while shut in the cupboard but she did not respond to this”, said Ahmad.

The vet believes that these animals suffered for years under the care of Ashford and that all their misery was avoidable.



They said: “In my opinion all of the suffering experienced by all of the animals is avoidable with correct housing, nutrition and stimulation.

“It is my opinion that the owner has failed to meet the basic needs of every animal removed from her care.

“She has also neglected to seek veterinary treatment for the animals that required treatment, causing animals to be in pain unnecessarily, leading to their suffering.

“All of this was avoidable. The owner is also doing nothing to prevent the situation continuing to escalate by housing entire male and female animals of the same species together allowing further breeding.”

Ashford, now of the Dengie peninsula in Essex, pleaded guilty to failing to meet her animals’ welfare needs on July 8.



This included not providing them with a suitable living environment and failing to prevent their pain and suffering.

She received 18 weeks in custody and a further 12 months suspension as well as 15 Rehabilitation Activity Requirement days.

Appearing at Ipswich Magistrates’ Court earlier this month, Ashford was ordered to pay over £1,200 in fines, including costs and a victim surcharge.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ashford claimed that she is not a bad person and regrets her actions.

She said that she now no longer has any animals other than three dogs.

News.title: Missing pet dog found swimming in San Francisco bay TWO WEEKS after being spooked by July 4 fireworks and running away
News.content:
A MISSING pet dog has been miraculously rescued from San Francisco bay nearly two weeks after being spooked by July 4 fireworks and running away.

The dog, named Prieta, was pulled from the water by firefighters while being pursued by a colony of seagulls.



Drones, trucks and boats were scrambled by the city’s Menlo Park fire department to pull off the action movie-style rescue mission near East Palo Alto.

The tiny female dog had been swimming for 40 minutes before rescuers reached her.



A concerned passer-by had alerted emergency services after they spotted the dog as it “ran into the water and kept swimming”.

The joint rescue effort was managed by local fire crews, police, and animal welfare officers who initially spotted Prieta using binoculars.

Her exact location was then tracked by a drone, before officials carried out the “challenging” water rescue, reaching her around half a mile from the coast.

Prieta was scooped out of the water shivering, startled and was immediately wrapped in a warm jacket before being taken back to land.



East Palo Alto police quipped: “Tiny dog escapes marsh, survives aerial assault by an organised gang of seagulls and is rescued by the Menlo Park fire department. 12/10 action movie.”

The firefighters wrote on social media: “Thank you to everyone who helped reunite this furry friend with its family.”

The dog was then taken to an animal welfare centre, where they used her microchip to track down the owners.



Staff said she arrived “exhausted, scared, and with facial injuries from the ordeal”.

They also treated her for scratches before feeding her and giving her water.

Prieta had gone missing during the Fourth of July celebrations after being spooked by loud fireworks.

Her owners admitted they had begun to lose hope about finding her.

One of them, who decided to remain anonymous, wrote on social media: “I want to thank the entire rescue team from the bottom of my heart.



“These last two weeks were a lot of agony not knowing about my dog.”

The woman said she had searched animal centres around Palo Alto but had no luck until the phone call on July 16.

She continued: “I was very, very depressed not knowing where she was and was even losing hope.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“My heart started beating so hard when I received the call from the SPCA (Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals) team.

“I would never be able to thank you enough for her rescue and for bringing her back to her home. Forever grateful.”

News.title: Dozens of trapped whales threatened with death in defunct theme park begin journey to new home after dramatic rescue
News.content:
DOZENS of trapped whales that were previously facing certain death have dramatically been rescued – as their journey to a new home begins.

Extraordinary images showed the majestic sea creatures being lifted out of a defunct Canadian theme park following two years of abandonment.



Nearly three dozen beluga whales were taken out of Marineland in Niagara Falls, Ontario, and are now headed for the US.

The sea canaries, that weigh up to 1,600kg each, were pictured being hoisted out of the shuttered park pools in huge slings attached to a crane.



One of the whales, named Sierra, looked nonplussed as she was carried away by a soft white sling.

Sierra is set to be joined by Acadia, Osiris and Lilooet at Shedd Aquarium in Chicago.

Meanwhile, Bertie Botts and Frankie are destined to be flown out to SeaWorld in San Antonio, Texas.

The relocation efforts kicked off on Monday, according to Canadian officials.



Canadian Fisheries Minister Joanne Thompson said: “The first wave of the rescue mission at Marineland is underway.”

It comes after years of chaos that left the survival of the gentle animals hanging in the balance.

The whales’ home at Marineland closed down when its owners John and Marie Holer died in 2024.



After their deaths, staff continued to care for the magnificent creatures.

They even faced threat of euthanasia if a suitable home wasn’t found in time.

But luckily, they have been given another chance at life.

Authorities in Canada hammered out deals with US and Spain counterparts over moving the whales last month.

And miraculously, they will now be given a new home.



It comes after tragic pictures showed the abandoned theme park rotting away behind locked gates with hundreds of animals still inside.

Images captured by Canadian outlet CBC showed weeds swallowing cracked parking lots and deer roaming the deserted grounds months after the once-popular attraction shut its doors.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Other haunting images from inside the abandoned attraction also reveal the grim state of its marine enclosures.

Animal rights campaigners have previously expressed fears over the future of the park’s remaining deer and elk.

News.title: Andy Burnham live: New Prime Minister sets challenge to ministers during his first Cabinet meeting
News.content:
Andy Burnham has thrown down the gauntlet, asking MPs to "take that little bit of pressure off people's shoulders" as he sets sights to help ease families facing the cost-of-living crisis

Andy Burnham today chaired his first Cabinet meeting and told his appointed ministers to examine “all possible ways” to help families struggling with high costs.

In a challenge to his top team one their applause had died down, the new Prime Minister said their task was to "take that little bit of pressure off people's shoulders" and show them help was coming so they could have some hope things were improving.

He told the meeting: "That’s the mission that we’ve got to set ourselves together” and asked his colleagues to look into what their department could do to ease cost-of-living pressures, “big and small,” saying: “We need to be a cost-of-living Government, getting that cost of living down, looking at all possible ways of doing that.”

Burnham started today by making good on his promise for “breathing space” for struggling households, a key plinth of his economic plans unveiled in his maiden speech outside No 10 on Monday. The move will see VAT removed from domestic electricity bills from October 1.

Burnham said: “Westminster has not been working for people for too long, with families struggling with the cost of living. That needs to change. I said I wanted to give people breathing space, and that’s what I’m announcing on my second day as Prime Minister. We’re taking immediate action to cut taxes on energy bills, put more money in people’s pockets and bring back hope.”

It is estimated that the change will reduce the annual Ofgem price cap by around £45 from October, with companies expected to pass the reduction onto customers.

Chancellor John Healey said: “For too long, too many people have struggled with the cost of living. Today’s energy tax cut will give families some breathing room on bills, and provide some reassurance this winter". He continued: “This measure is funded this year from cancelling the Digital ID programme, and it will help bring down inflation while supporting households in every postcode.”

The fully priced plan from Mr Healey comes as Burnham continues to pad out his cabinet, with a number of key appointments made since yesterday, including Ed Miliband receiving the FCDO brief, Angela Rayner returning as Housing Secretary, and Shabana Mahmood staying on as Home Secretary.

News.title: Kiena Dawes' mum makes plea for 'domestic abuse-related suicide' law 'before girls have to die to be heard'
News.content:
Kiena Dawes' mum makes plea for 'domestic abuse-related suicide' law 'before girls have to die to be heard'

The mother of Kiena Dawes has thrown her support behind a campaign to create a new offence of domestic abuse-related suicide following her daughter’s death in 2022

View 3 Images Kiena died on a railway line in Lancashire in July 2022 after a two-year relationship with Wellings. (Image: PA)

A grieving mum has backed calls for a new law in her daughter’s name after she took her own life following prolonged domestic abuse.

Angela Dawes is supporting a campaign for “Kiena’s Law” after her 23-year-old daughter died in July 2022 following what a court heard was a prolonged campaign of abuse by her former partner Ryan Wellings. The petition, made by Lancaster Police and Crime Commissioner, Clive Grunshaw has gained almost 19,000 signatures.

The petition is calling for a new criminal offence of domestic abuse-related suicide, recognising cases where prolonged coercive and controlling behaviour contributes to a victim taking their own life. Speaking at an event in Blackpool this month, Angela said the proposed law could help prevent other families suffering the same heartbreak.

View 3 Images The court heeard he regularly physically assaulted Kiena, slapping her, “ragging” her by the hair and subjecting her to verbal and financial abuse. (Image: Lancashire Constabulary / SWNS)

"To have a standalone charge for things like what Kiena went through, I do feel is so important," she said. “Nothing is ever going to bring my baby back, but if we can change things moving forward, I’d hate to see another family go through what we’ve been through. My girl didn’t want to die. My girl wanted to live. But she lived in fear.

"We’ve lost a beautiful, very special, kind young girl who’s missed so much, not just by me but by so many other people. Please make changes before girls have to die to be heard. I can’t personally save any other girls, but I hope I can help by saying this. Please don’t give up, all of you who are working so hard for these changes. Please don’t give up. Let’s stop losing girls in this way.”

Kiena died on a railway line in Lancashire in July 2022 after a two-year relationship with Wellings. During his trial at Preston Crown Court, jurors heard he regularly physically assaulted Kiena, slapping her, “ragging” her by the hair and subjecting her to verbal and financial abuse.

In a note written before her body was found, Kiena said she was "murdered", and said Wellings "killed" her. She wrote that he had "ruined every bit of strength" she had left, and that her "future" was "taken away" from her. Wellings was acquitted of manslaughter but convicted of coercive and controlling behaviour and assault. He was jailed for six-and-a-half years in January 2025.

View 3 Images Wellings was jailed for six-and-a-half years (Image: PA)

Since her daughter’s death, Angela has vowed to campaign in Kiena’s memory and for others who have died in similar circumstances. She said: “Changes need to be made. Girls shouldn’t have to die to be heard, and my daughter had to die to be heard. There was so much victim blaming."

The campaign is also calling for coercive and controlling behaviour to be included within the dangerous offender framework. The campaign is headed by Lancashire Police and Crime Commissioner Clive Grunshaw, who has worked alongside Angela and Advocacy After Fatal Domestic Abuse (AAFDA) to raise awareness of domestic abuse-related suicide and push for changes to the law.

Frank Mullane MBE, chief executive of Advocacy After Fatal Domestic Abuse (AAFDA), said Kiena’s case had “exposed a serious gap in the law”. He said: “Too often, when a victim dies by suicide following prolonged domestic abuse, coercive control and intimidation, the full impact of that abuse is not recognised by the criminal justice system.

"Angela’s courage and determination have helped shine a light on this issue, but this campaign is about much more than one family. Kiena’s Law represents an opportunity to recognise the devastating and sometimes fatal consequences of coercive and controlling behaviour, improve accountability and help prevent future deaths. We owe it to Kiena and to every family affected by domestic abuse-related suicide to make that change.”

Police and Crime Commissioner Clive Grunshaw praised Angela’s determination to secure reform. He said: "Kiena’s story has touched people across Lancashire and beyond".

“We must continue to learn lessons, improve protections for victims and ensure that women and girls are supported when they seek help. I would encourage people to support the petition and help keep this important conversation at the forefront of public and political debate.”

Article continues below

Find out more about the petition here

For mental health support, contact the Samaritans on 116 123, email them at jo@samaritans.org or visit samaritans.org to find your nearest branch.

For confidential support, call the 24-hour National Domestic Abuse Freephone Helpline on 0808 2000 247 or visit womensaid.co.uk. If you or your family have lost a friend or family member through fatal domestic abuse, AAFDA (Advocacy After Fatal Domestic Abuse) can offer specialist and expert support and advocacy. For more info visit** www.aafda.org.uk**.

News.title: Boy, 15, accused of rape and sexual assault against eight victims as young as 10
News.content:
Boy, 15, accused of rape and sexual assault against eight victims as young as 10

Wellingborough Youth Court heard that the boy is accused of rape and sexual assault against eight victims who were aged between 10 and 15 at the time

View Image The case will now be tried at Northampton Crown Court (Image: PA Wire/PA Images)

A 15-year-old boy charged with sexual offences against eight girls, including one who was 10 years old, has appeared in court.

Wellingborough Youth Court heard that the boy is accused of rape and sexual assault against eight victims who were aged between 10 and 15 at the time.

The teenager, who cannot be named because of his age, has been charged with 22 offences relating to alleged incidents between 2023 and 2025.

He was not asked to enter any pleas during the 20-minute hearing on Tuesday. The youth, who was accompanied by his mother, was not asked to enter the dock and took a seat at the back of the court room.

He has been charged with 12 counts of sexually assaulting a female, three counts of assaulting a girl under 13 by touching, and one count of raping a girl under 13.

He is also charged with one count of assaulting a female aged 13 and over by penetration with a part of the body or thing, one count of raping a girl aged 13-15, and two counts of making an indecent photograph or pseudo-photograph of a child.

He faces further a charge of possessing a prohibited image of a child and another of possessing an extreme pornographic image or images.

District Judge Amar Mehta told the boy: "Your case is too serious to be tried in this court. Therefore it’s going to be tried at the crown court at Northampton. I'm going to send your case to Northampton Crown Court for another hearing similar to this one."

Article continues below

The teenager was told to appear at that court on August 18. He was granted conditional bail instructing him not to contact the alleged victims, to have no unsupervised contact with females under 16, and to engage with the Northamptonshire Youth Justice Service.

The boy spoke only to confirm his name, date of birth and address, and to ask the judge what the Youth Justice Service was.

News.title: Reason you feel exhausted in a heatwave as 'hottest day ever' on its way
News.content:
Reason you feel exhausted in a heatwave as 'hottest day ever' on its way

With the hottest day ever predicted to be hitting the UK soon, health experts have shared the reason why you're likely to feel exhausted in a heatwave – and what you can do about it

View Image Many people feel exhausted during a heatwave (stock image) (Image: Getty Images)

The UK has experienced an unprecedented summer when it comes to the hot weather, experiencing three major heatwaves. This year marks the first time in British history that temperatures have breached 35C in three separate months (May, June, and July). As of late July, meteorologists are closely tracking advanced weather models that predict temperatures could potentially soar to 41C, which would eclipse the UK's current absolute record of 40.3C set in July 2022 – making it the hottest day ever in the UK.

‌



With temperatures remaining hot across much of the UK, many people are still very much feeling the effects.

‌



New data from Healthwords.ai reveals heat-related health queries increased by 621% between April and June, as warmer weather prompted a surge in people seeking advice for symptoms including dizziness, fatigue and dehydration.

‌



The most common concerns included dizziness and fainting, excessive sweating - especially at night, lethargy and fatigue and dehydration and electrolyte loss.

Talking about why these ailments might be happening, Dr Tom Maggs, Chief Medical Officer at Healthwords.ai explains: "Many people assume feeling exhausted during a heatwave is simply because it’s uncomfortable, but there’s much more happening inside the body.

"When temperatures rise, your body has to work much harder to regulate its core temperature.

‌



"Blood vessels widen to help release heat, your heart works harder to circulate blood, and you lose both water and important electrolytes through sweat."

The doctor added: "“Even mild dehydration can leave you feeling unusually tired, sluggish or lightheaded, and the effects don’t necessarily disappear as soon as the weather cools.

"If you’ve also had several nights of poor sleep because of the heat, that fatigue can build up over several days.”

‌



Dr Maggs says people often underestimate how quickly dehydration can develop. “Thirst is actually a relatively late sign that your body needs fluids," he said.

"If you’re already feeling thirsty, tired or developing a headache, you’re likely already mildly dehydrated. Older adults, young children and anyone exercising outdoors are particularly vulnerable.”

5 ways to recover from heat-related fatigue

Drink water regularly throughout the day rather than waiting until you’re thirsty.

Replenish electrolytes alongside fluids, particularly if you’ve been sweating heavily or spending long periods outdoors. An oral rehydration solution, such as O.R.S Hydration, is specifically formulated to replace both fluids and essential electrolytes.

Prioritise sleep by keeping bedrooms cool, closing curtains during the day and avoiding strenuous activity right before bedtime.

Take regular breaks from the heat and seek cooler, shaded spaces where possible.

Seek medical advice if you experience persistent dizziness, fainting, confusion or vomiting, as these could be signs of heat exhaustion or heatstroke.

‌



Dr Maggs concluded: "Most people recover well with rest, cooling down and proper hydration, but prevention is always easier than recovery.

"Small habits like drinking consistently throughout the day, avoiding the hottest parts of the afternoon and recognising the early signs of dehydration can make a significant difference.”

Healthwords is registered with the UK's Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) as a Class 1 Medical Device, specifically as patient health self-management software.

Article continues below

The platform is a registered digital health tool designed to help you decode basic symptoms, understand self-treatment options, and find over-the-counter products. However, it is not a replacement for a real doctor.

News.title: FIFA told World Cup expansion plans would kill football as Gianni Infantino left red-faced
News.content:
FIFA told World Cup expansion plans would kill football as Gianni Infantino left red-faced

Plans to potentially expand the World Cup to 64 teams in the future have been heavily criticised with the chief of La Liga now taking aim at Gianni Infantino after this summer's tournament

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino has come under fire during the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

The president of La Liga, Javier Tebas, has accused FIFA and Gianni Infantino of trying to 'destroy football' with their plans to increase the number of teams competing at future World Cups to 64.

‌



Spain won the final of this summer's tournament on Sunday, beating Argentina 1-0 in a forgettable final. 48 teams, rather than the usual 32, competed across matches held in the United States, Canada and Mexico as part of expanded format for the first time, but Infantino has already confirmed that adding a further 16 teams will be discussed.

‌



However, Tebas has torn into the plans, claiming they make 'no sense' and that moving ahead with them would be irresponsible.

‌



“Increasing the number of national teams makes no sense,” Tebas told the Italian outlet, La Gazzetta dello Sport.

Argentina star's sister reignites Falklands row with rant after World Cup final READ MORE :

“The football industry is not just the World Cup, which is the most important event. But not everything can revolve around the World Cup. It is national competitions that support this sport.

“They are destroying the football industry, the one that generates tens of thousands of jobs for an event that lasts 40 days and to which the minority of players go.

‌



“We need fewer national teams and more protection for national football, at all levels. They don’t realise, they decide irresponsibly.”

Tebas went on to question Infantino's position following criticism of political interference at the World Cup from the United States President, Donald Trump.

View 2 Images La Liga president Javier Tebas has torn into Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Infantino has been in power for 10 years and is expected to be elected for a fourth term next year. But Tebas wants to see change, even if he believes it is unlikely to happen.

“In my opinion, yes, I think his time is up,” he added. “But he has the support of the system, of the federations, there is not much more to add, right?

“There is no opposition candidate, no one wants to present themselves to lose. This is the system, and it is a system that is sick at the source.

‌



“In these days here in America I have heard many people against Infantino, who do not agree with what he does. They say it, but then they do nothing.

“I don’t know if silence or complicity is worse, because those who are silent are perfectly aware of the damage that football is suffering.”
