The Gunners have been undergoing changes to their academy this season, with Pascal De Maesschalck appointed as academy director.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The club has a history of developing young talent and aims to continue that with De Maesschalck at the helm.



Ten players were released from Arsenal’s youth teams earlier this summer, including Josh Nichols, Colombia youth goalkeeper Alexei Rojas and Egypt Under-20 international Cam’ron Ismail.

Sports.title: Man Utd ‘make ANOTHER transfer enquiry for Ismaila Sarr’ after trying to sign Crystal Palace star TWICE before
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have made an enquiry for Crystal Palace star Ismaila Sarr, according to reports in France.

The Senegalese winger, 28, is said to be on Michael Carrick‘s radar as the Red Devils look to strengthen on the wing.



Although he is not United‘s main target, Sarr has the type of profile being considered by the Old Trafford dlub, according to French publication Foot Mercato.

Their recruitment team will reportedly explore several options before advancing with one.



Sarr, who is a childhood United fan, is likely to be attracted by the proposition of a move, despite Crystal Palace‘s qualification for the Europa League after their Conference League triumph.

He’s reportedly called United his ‘dream club’ in the past.



The winger, who farms cattle with his dad to shun the limelight, was Senegal‘s star during this summer’s World Cup, scoring four goals in the four games they played.

His productive World Cup followed his best ever season at club level, where he scored 21 goals in all competitions and was top scorer in the Conference League.

His exploits in Europe also led to him being named Player of the Tournament.

And while he’s been linked to United in the past, this could be the summer for Sarr, who is entering the prime years of his football career.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

But a switch doesn’t look that simple with Marcus Rashford‘s future is lying in doubt after Barcelona opted for England team-mate Anthony Gordon instead of him.

The signing of a winger may depend on whether United can offload their academy graduate.

Additionally, United have been linked to Dutch star Crysencio Summerville as another option.

However, that could also be difficult as Roma look to be in the driving seat for the West Ham winger, 24, and might be rivalled by Aston Villa, who are reportedly plotting a move of their own.

Sports.title: Ex-Chelsea star who England were ‘desperate’ to call up seals shock free transfer to EFL club after horror spell abroad
Sports.content:
FORMER Chelsea and Brighton speedster Tariq Lamptey has joined QPR on a free.

The right-back, 25, had been unemployed since terminating his Fiorentina contract by mutual consent two and a half months ago.



The Italian side forked out just over £5million to sign Lamptey from Brighton last year.

But the 5ft 4ins wide man endured a torrid time abroad, tearing his ACL after playing just 25 minutes across two appearances, and missing the rest of the season.



Lamptey will now try and get his career back on track in the Championship.

Some fans will have rubbed their eyes upon seeing him holding the blue and white shirt on Tuesday morning.

Lamptey was hot property at Chelsea, making three first-team appearances as a teenager and earning a big move to the Seagulls.

There, he made over 100 Premier League appearances and scored five goals across all competitions.

Two years into his Brighton spell, when Lamptey was at the peak of his powers, the FA was scrapping to keep him committed to England.

He had played up to Under-21 level by that point and was knocking on the door of the senior side, but chose to switch to Ghana.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The FA had been ‘desperate’ to keep him, according to The Athletic.

Lamptey has earned 11 caps for Ghana but his last one came almost two years ago.



After being unveiled by QPR, who finished 15th in the second tier under Julien Stephan last campaign, Lamptey told the club website: “The team have ambitious goals for the season, so I am looking forward to it.

“I know what I am capable of and I set myself high standards. I had a great start to my career, and I’ll keep continuing that.

“My recovery has gone well and I’m not too far away now. I’m looking forward to joining the boys.

“You can’t really predict what’s going to happen, you can only put your best foot forward and prepare as well as possible. And that’s what I try to do.”

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan planned one last St James' Park visit before cancer death to see fans he loved
Sports.content:
Kevin Keegan planned one last St James' Park visit before cancer death to see fans he loved

The England legend was set to be a special guest at next season's opening game against his old club Liverpool at St James' Park on August 23 before he died from cancer

Toon fans pay tribute to Kevin Keegan

Kevin Keegan was planning an emotional return to his beloved Newcastle United before his tragic death from cancer.

‌



"King Kev" was set to be a special guest at next season's opening game against his old club Liverpool at St James' Park on August 23. He told an audience at his last appearance on Tyneside that he 'did not want a statue' like fellow Toon idols Sir Bobby Robson and Alan Shearer. But he intended to see the "Toon army" one last time.

‌



His tragic death from cancer at 75 meant that he never got that chance. Lifelong fan Joe Black wore a Newcastle Utd shirt today which had been signed by Keegan during his personal appearance at the Tyne Theatre in Newcastle in May.

‌



View 7 Images Lifelong Newcastle United fan Joe Black with the shirt signed on his last appearance on Tyneside

He joined a stream of fans today at St James' Park who paid tribute, including his son, also Joe, 34, and his six-year-old grandson Joe. He said: "I am going to wear my shirt for the opening game of the season and then keep it and never wear it again.

"My dad was also called Joe and he was black and white daft. My first game was when I was five years old and I have been coming ever since and I am 69 now. Keegan was a hero, he was something else, and we will never forget him."

‌



Newcastle-born Carolyn Ridley, 63, also a lifelong fan, came to pay tribute and 'share stories' with supporters. He said: "He brought such great times, I still get goosebumps thinking about it. He lifted everything when he was a player and manager.

View 7 Images Kevin Keegan tributes at St James' Park (Image: Mirrorpix)

"We will never forget the excitement of his teams, he nearly won the league. But his football was just brilliant; I think he got the Geordies, and we got him and loved him. Every time you came here you knew you were going to see goals; he will be remembered for that and of course that TV rant."

‌



Keegan himself joked that people would remember his 'perm, his crash on TV's Superstars and his rant at Man Utd." Sir Alex Ferguson, the man famously on the other end of Keegan's "I'd love it, absolutely love it, if we beat them" tirade, said: "I had the utmost respect for him.

View 7 Images Newcastle United fan Carolyn Ridley came to pay her respects at St James' Park (Image: Mirrorpix)

"We had many duels when he was manager of Newcastle, but I have to say the job he did at Newcastle was fantastic. He re-energised that club and brought that enthusiasm and fanaticism that great supporters can give. That's the job he did.

‌



"And he also brought three great players to the club: David Ginola, Faustino Asprilla, and Philippe Albert. I must say the challenges we had at that time were huge. It gave Newcastle - I think - their best ever team."

Fergie told Track Radio: "The best thing about him was that he held no grudges and I admired him for that." Schoolfriends Ross Hickson, 46, and Steven Porritt, of Gateshead, bumped into each other outside St James' Park.

View 7 Images Alex Ferguson said he had the 'utmost respect' for Kevin Keegan (Image: PA Archive/PA Images)

‌



They shared memories of Keegan's heyday as both a player and manager. "I met him when I was 12 or 13 at the training ground," Steven, a floor layer, recalled.

"I was picking up the footballs and he said to me: 'We are £3m in debt, we can't afford to lose them'. Then he got me a ball which I got signed and took into school. He loved it up here and we loved him. I am 47 years old and could not stop crying when I heard he had died yesterday."

Ross, a courier, added: "For me, he is up there with Sir Bobby Robson as a legend of this club." Fans left floral tributes around the Sir Bobby Robson and Alan Shearer statues at the ground.

‌



View 7 Images Shola Ameobi former Newcastle United player paid his respects to Kevin Keegan (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Former player Shola Ameobi and Newcastle Central MP Dame Chi Onwurah both came to pay their respects. One tribute read: "White roses for the Geordie from Yorkshire. You broke our hearts in 1974 but made up for it."

Another card read: 'Kevin Keegan, Angel of the North'. Others said that whatever tribute was offered 'would never be enough'. Chris Hughton, the former Toon manager, recalled Keegan's wonderful rapport with players.

‌



"He was an incredible coach. He was down to earth, charismatic, and always incredibly honest," he said. Lee Clark, now manager of Hartlepool United, played under Keegan in the 90s.

View 7 Images Fans have left tributes around the grounds of St James' Park in Newcastle (Image: Newcastle Chronicle)

When he first passed his driving test, Keegan told him to take his new sports car back because he did not like the way Clark was driving it. He did the same again with Clark's next car. He said: "He was like the Pied Piper to the Geordie public. They adore him."

‌



The former BBC broadcaster Gary Richardson interviewed Keegan on many occasions. Richardson recalled completing one interview about Keegan's early life before explaining that he was returning to London. Keegan asked him to stay and they chatted for two hours.

"It was one of the greatest days of my life in broadcasting. And that is just because of the way that he was ," he added. Keegan told him that he was a 'lucky man' because all of his dreams had come true - winning the league with Liverpool, playing for England and Newcastle United, and working with the great Bill Shankly.

View 7 Images Keegan made 63 appearances for England, 31 of those as captain (Image: Bob Thomas Sports Photography via Getty Images)

‌



"Three days after joining Liverpool he came up to me and said 'you will play for England son," Keegan recalled. "And I never had any doubt about it because it was Bill Shankly telling me. And he did not mess around."

In a statement on behalf of Keegan's former Liverpool team mate and close friend Terry McDermott, his family said: "We are heartbroken by the loss of our dear friend, Kevin Keegan. Kevin was so much more than a teammate.

Article continues below

"He was a lifelong friend whose warmth, loyalty, humour and passion for football touched so many lives. The memories they shared, both on and off the pitch, will be treasured forever. Although Terry’s dementia means he is no longer able to express his feelings publicly, we know how much Kevin meant to him and how deeply this loss would have affected him.

"Our thoughts and prayers are with Jean, Laura, Sarah and all of Kevin’s family at this incredibly sad time. We hope they find comfort in the love and respect being shown for Kevin by so many people. Kevin was one of football’s true greats, but to Terry he was, above all, a cherished friend. He will be greatly missed and never forgotten."

Sports.title: Lionel Messi sparks conspiracy theories as footage from World Cup final speech leaked
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi sparks conspiracy theories as footage from World Cup final speech leaked

Lionel Messi's Argentina speech has caused a stir with numerous conspiracy theories emerging after the World Cup final

View 2 Images Lionel Messi hinted at a pre-match issue for Argentina during the speech to his team-mates before the World Cup final (Image: TyC Sports)

Conspiracy theories over a potential issue distracting Argentina players in the World Cup final have been sparked after footage emerged of Lionel Messi's strange pre-match speech.

‌



Lionel Scaloni's side failed to lay a glove on Spain at MetLife Stadium on Sunday and though they defended valiantly, the 2022 champions did not muster a shot until the second half of extra-time. A number of theories have emerged over why their performance was so bad and the latest of those has hinted at a significant problem just before the match started.

‌



Fresh footage from inside the tunnel has supported those claims and also provided more evidence of Scaloni stating that things happened before the final. As the Argentina players emerge from their dressing room, Messi has been captured stating: "Come on, boys, let's forget what happened, as if nothing had happened."

‌



FIFA issue statement on Argentina bust-up and RESCIND World Cup final red card READ MORE :

Leandro Paredes refuses to apologise for World Cup final 'punches' as FIFA overturn red READ MORE :

Lisandro Martinez and Enzo Fernandez are among those in the background of the video appearing visibly upset. The latter was sent off in the final knockings of normal time while Martinez went off injured during the first half.

The X account @arielipillo, which has 80,000 followers, has claimed that they were emotional and distracted because of unannounced anti-doping tests moments before the game started.

However, that post has been hit with a community note which clarifies that FIFA anti-doping controls are carried out after matches and not before.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Cameras also caught comments from Messi and Emiliano Martinez as the players headed back out for the second half.

Via Sport, Argentina's captain said "Come on, lads. Personality, people, personality. We've always had it, so why wouldn't we have it now? We have the personality to play. Martinez added: "With heart, lads. Let's move forward, not backward... Only cowards play backward.

‌



In addition to the strange behaviour, some Argentina players disgraced themselves with their conduct after losing to Spain. Leandro Parades was involved in a brawl with Gavi and Eric Garcia while Nahuel Molina and assistant coach Roberto Ayala appeared to throw punches.

View 2 Images TOPSHOT - Argentina's midfielder #05 Leandro Paredes (top) clashes with Spain's midfielder #09 Gavi during the 2026 World Cup football tournament final match between Spain and Argentina at the New York/New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford on July 19, 2026. (Photo by CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / AFP via Getty Images)

The former was among many to release statements following defeat in the final with Messi's public declaration particularly heartfelt.

‌



He wrote: “The pain is immense, it will take time for this wound to heal. But I also choose to hold on to all the good things, all matches we turned around by giving everything and moments that will remain in our memories forever.

“I will always remember the support of an entire country that, together with the work and effort of this group, brought us back once again among the best teams in the world. I also want to congratulate Spain on winning World Cup.”

“Today, it is difficult to appreciate what we achieved… but this group has really reached two consecutive World Cup finals. Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and every message. Once again, we managed to come together as a country and stand united, sharing the immense pride of being Argentine.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi snubs Argentina parade as he flies home separately from disgraced team-mates
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi snubs Argentina parade as he flies home separately from disgraced team-mates

Argentina's players are still reeling from their World Cup final defeat but that hasn't stopped them from hosting a bus parade which Lionel Messi snubbed

View 3 Images Argentina held a bus parade after their World Cup final defeat but Lionel Messi wasn't there (Image: Getty)

Lionel Messi flew back to Argentina separately from his international team-mates after their 1-0 World Cup final loss to Spain. Most of La Albiceleste's squad embarked on an open-top bus parade in Buenos Aires after landing, but 11 players, including Messi, did not make an appearance.

‌



Argentina's dreams of back-to-back World Cup titles were crushed by Luis de la Fuente's Spain on Sunday evening as La Roja lifted the trophy for just the second time in their history. Yet, the match itself was overshadowed by ill discipline.

‌



Some of Lionel Scaloni's squad were branded disgraceful on the back of their performance, during which Argentina failed to register a shot on target until extra time and Enzo Fernandez was sent off for two egregious bookable offences.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Full list of Argentina's 27 dirty tricks in World Cup final as they ruin greatest match READ MORE :

Argentina star's sister reignites Falklands row with rant after World Cup final READ MORE :

After the final whistle blew, scenes got even uglier, with Leandro Paredes seemingly throwing Spain's Gavi to the floor and Nahuel Molina appearing to punch opposition skipper Rodri. Argentina's players have since flown home, but 11 stars did not join the bulk of the squad in Buenos Aires and Messi embarked on a separate journey to his homeland altogether.

View 3 Images Manager Scaloni and 15 players took part in the greeting (Image: Getty)

‌



In the wake of their heavily criticised appearance in the final, manager Scaloni and 15 of his players landed at Ezeiza International Airport to a hero's welcome on Monday evening, regardless of the 1-0 defeat they had suffered.

After staff disembarked the plane, Argentine Football Association president Chiqui Tapia, manager Scaloni and veteran defender Nicolas Otamendi led the group across a red carpet before they boarded an open-top bus.

This vehicle travelled along major streets towards the AFA training centre in Buenos Aires. The 15 players will soon begin their holidays from the AFA base.

‌



But 11 stars did not travel with their team-mates. Rodrigo De Paul, Cristian Romero, Julian Alvarez, Geronimo Rulli, Juan Musso, Nico Paz, Giuliano Simeone, Lautaro Martinez, Molina and Fernandez remained in the United States.

It is likely they will embark on vacations from the US. Messi was the 11th player not to travel, though he did fly to Argentina. At 6:28am local time on Tuesday, he arrived at Islas Malvinas International Airport before heading to his home in Rosario.

View 3 Images Messi was emotional after defeat in New Jersey (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

After a stopover in Miami, Messi landed in his home country from New York and will rest with his family in the gated community of Kentucky in Funes. He too was greeted by hordes of fans upon arrival, but opted not to join his team-mates in Buenos Aires.

Messi will jet off to Miami to join his Inter Miami peers after enjoying sufficient rest in Rosario. His parents were unable to attend the World Cup due to his father Jorge's health issues.

Sports.title: Man City to sign youngster from under Arsenal's noses after contract rejection
Sports.content:
Man City to sign youngster from under Arsenal's noses after contract rejection

Manchester City have agreed to sign Arsenal teenager Mishel Nduka, after the youngster rejected a new deal that would've kept him at the Emirates

View 2 Images Man City have secured a deal to land one of Arsenal's teenage stars

Manchester City have reached an agreement to land Arsenal youngster Mishel Nduka, who turned down a new contract in north London.

‌



The young midfielder is expected to undergo a medical imminently before joining City on scholarship terms, which is likely to lead to a professional deal. Nduka is an England youth international and tipped for a big future.

‌



Nduka moved to Arsenal from Charlton Athletic in 2025 and played for Arsenal’s Under-18s. He also ran out for the club’s under-21 side in Premier League 2 but, despite the offer of a competitive long-term deal, he has chosen to move to Manchester, reports the Athletic.

‌



Nduka’s likely move to City comes after they completed the signing of 17-year-old Jeremy Monga from Leicester City this month. Arsenal were also keen but backed out when they believed the price being quoted was too high. City secured a deal which is worth £12.5m in total - £10m plus £2.5m in potential contingencies.

Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer READ MORE :

City's greatest academy success has been Phil Foden, who continued to blossom under Pep Guardiola before eventually being named the PFA Player of the Year in 2024. Last season was a breakout campaign for Nico O'Reilly, who established himself as the team's first choice left-back.

Rico Lewis was another player to become a fixture in the first-team environment. Enzo Maresca has now come in to replace Guardiola and will be tasked with making use of the club's young talent, with Nduka now among those available to him.

‌



Nduka is not the only youth prospect that Arsenal have lost in recent years with Ayden Heaven moving to Manchester United last year. The centre-half went straight into the first-team squad at Old Trafford and played 18 times for the Red Devils last term.

View 2 Images Ayden Heaven left Arsenal for Man United last year (Image: (James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images))

He had been on Arsenal's books since he was 13 and had made his senior debut in a Carabao Cup game, but Sky Sports claimed that he felt a route into the first-team was blocked off. Several players were ahead of him in the pecking order and the Gunners continued to sign players, forcing him into moving.

Article continues below

Heaven became the second young player to join United from Arsenal during that season after striker Chido Obi-Martin moved north in October.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez 'should've been sent off twice' as FIFA receive new referee verdict
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez 'should've been sent off twice' as FIFA receive new referee verdict

Enzo Fernandez has been handed a stark verdict following his sending off in the World Cup final

View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez became the first player to get sent off in a World Cup final since 2010 (Image: Bob Kupbens/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Enzo Fernandez has been told he should have been sent off before eventually getting his marching orders in the World Cup final. That is the opinion of former PGMOL chief and ex-FIFA referee, Keith Hackett, who said the Chelsea star was lucky not to receive an earlier sending off for dissent.

‌



Argentina failed to defend their crown in Sunday's final, losing 1-0 to Spain in extra-time. The South American side had to play the 30 minutes of added time without the Blues talisman, who was shown a red in the 93rd minute.

‌



The 25-year-old first received a yellow in the 82nd minute after screaming at referee Slavko Vincic, who declined to award a foul in Argentina's favour. Fernandez was noticeably miffed by the decision and sarcastically applauded Vincic when being handed the booking.

‌



Fernandez's reaction would have resulted in an immediate second yellow in the Premier League but the midfielder remained on the pitch. However, moments before the full-time whistle blew, Fernandez aggressively clattered into Pau Cubarsi and was then shown a second yellow, and subsequently a red card.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Hackett said Vincic's lenient decision to not send off Fernandez for dissent saved the Argentina star from an earlier shower. He said: "I think that he was fortunate, but I think that there's always, in a final, a reluctance to some degree to issue a red card.

FIFA issue statement on Argentina bust-up and RESCIND World Cup final red card READ MORE :

Cristian Romero issues statement after World Cup final loss and vile Argentina scenes READ MORE :

"And I think that we saw that this referee was in those opening stages and right up to this fairly lenient with his approach. What was said was pretty robust, which caused the reaction of the referee, who was clearly, with his body language, very unhappy with what he said.

‌



"So on that first point, I wondered if that in itself, what was said to the referee, was sufficient to warrant a reaction and the possibility of a red card? I think it's likely that the referee didn't see the player applauding because I think he was concerned about getting the game restarted.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez was eventually given his marching orders in the 93rd minute (Image: Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

‌



"From a VAR point of view, they were right not to come in. So, I think generally in a final of this nature, this player was fortunate." Hackett placed blame on Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni for failing to rein in Fernandez's discipline.

He added: "I would say the manager, if he's seen that, has a choice. A choice to get a message to that player to improve his discipline. And a choice for the captain of the team to do likewise.

View 3 Images Argentina manager Lionel Scaloni was also blamed (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

Article continues below

"They didn't. Had he done that, there might have been consideration of substituting him to prevent the red card." Unfortunately for Scaloni, he had already used all five of his substitutions. Playing with a man down throughout extra time, Argentina ultimately fell 1–0 to Spain following a second-period extra-time goal by Ferran Torres.

Fernández became only the sixth player in men's World Cup history - and the third from Argentina - to be sent off in a final.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson reveals meeting Kevin Keegan in pub just days after 'love it' rant
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson reveals meeting Kevin Keegan in pub just days after 'love it' rant

The Liverpool legend and former Newcastle United and England manager Kevin Keegan was widely regarded as one of the most admired and beloved figures in world football

View 3 Images Kevin Keegan and Sir Alex Ferguson went head to head for the title in the 95/96 season

Sir Alex Ferguson has recalled a heartwarming encounter with Kevin Keegan, just days after former Newcastle United boss delivered one of the most iconic managerial outbursts in Premier League history.

‌



Keegan, one of the most popular figures in English football died aged 75 following a battle with cancer on Monday.

‌



In a statement, his family said: "It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75. The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments.

‌



"Kevin, a double Ballon D'or winner, was a much loved husband, father and grandfather. The family would like to thank Kevin’s incredible medical team for all their support. This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy."

‌



Tributes have poured in from across the football world, and former Manchester United manager Ferguson has reflected on a few memorable moments he shared with Keegan.

One of those encounters came in a pub, just days after Keegan famously declared that he would 'love it' if his side beat United in the 1995/96 title race - a passionate response to Ferguson's trademark mind games that helped define their rivalry.

Recalling their encounter, Ferguson said: "That was Kevin, he was all emotion and he brought that to the team as well. They played for Kevin Keegan, there's no question about that.

‌



"The interesting thing about the outburst from Kevin, two weeks after the season had finished, I was playing golf with some friends and went to a great bar up the road, nice food. We went up there, and who walks in? Kevin Keegan and he spent the rest of the night on the piano."

View 3 Images Ferguson and Keegan during Newcastle United's match against Manchester United

That season, Newcastle surrendered a 12‑point lead to United, but by then, Keegan had long put the collapse behind him.

‌



Ferguson added: "The best thing about him is he held no grudges, that was a fantastic quality he had. We had a great night, he would always say - whatever happened in previous weeks, that was soon forgotten.

"I really respected him for that."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



View 3 Images Tributes to Kevin Keegan outside St James' Park

Keegan died after being diagnosed with cancer, but was still active in the final months of his life. The former England boss is survived by his wife, Jean, and their children, Laura Jane and Sarah Marie.

'King Kev' remains one of the finest players England has ever produced, and his international career - both as a player and later as manager was unforgettable.

‌



A two‑time Ballon d'Or winner, he enjoyed spells with Scunthorpe United, Liverpool, Hamburg, Southampton, Newcastle and Blacktown City.

He hung up his boots in 1985 and took charge of Newcastle in 1992. From there, the Liverpool icon went on to manage Fulham, England and Manchester City before returning to St James' Park for a second spell in 2008.

Sports.title: Argentina star's sister reignites Falklands row with rant after World Cup final
Sports.content:
Argentina star's sister reignites Falklands row with rant after World Cup final

The Falklands controversy between England and Argentina is back in the headlines following a declaration from a family member of one player

View 2 Images Leandro Parades' sister has reignited the Falklands controversy (Image: La Nacion)

Barbara Parades, the sister of Argentina star Leandro, has brought the Falklands row back into the spotlight after controversially claiming they have the Islands. The dispute over which of Argentina or England owns the South Atlantic Island was a trending topic surrounding their semi-final clash at the World Cup.

‌



In the immediate aftermath of their 2-1 win over the Three Lions, Argentina players celebrated in front of their fans and later revealed a white banner that had the phrase "Las Malvinas Son Argentinas", written on it. In English, that translates to: "The Falklands belong to Argentina".

‌



A FIFA investigation was demanded ahead of their participation in the final, but that went ahead on Sunday without any intervention or punishment. The 2022 world champions took on Spain and were outclassed at MetLife Stadium, with their post-match behaviour drawing much-deserved criticism after punches were thrown.

‌



FIFA issue statement on Argentina bust-up and RESCIND World Cup final red card READ MORE :

Leandro Paredes refuses to apologise for World Cup final 'punches' as FIFA overturn red READ MORE :

Despite that, Barbara's reflection on their campaign was one of pride, largely due to beating England. She told reporters: "Getting this far and beating England along the way meant everything to us. We might not have the fourth star, but we have the Falklands for ourselves."

The Falklands had been a huge topic in the build-up to England's semi-final defeat and rumbled on for days afterwards, following uproar over the banner held up by Argentina players. The UK government even weighed in, saying: "The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands definitely are."

Argentina's Premier League stars could theoretically have their UK work visas revoked if their conduct is considered "not conducive to the public good", with the Home Office holding the legal authority to do so. Nevertheless, legal expert Asma Bashir has described such an outcome as "highly unlikely".

‌



Such suggestions only emerged following quite an outburst from Nile Gardiner, a former aide to Margaret Thatcher, who had deployed troops to reclaim the Island in 1982. The dispute dates back to the early 19th century, with both nations laying claim to the South Atlantic Island. The conflict lasted 74 days and claimed the lives of over 900 people.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

FIFA have yet to sanction Argentina for that incident, though they could face retrospective punishment over the post-match scenes against Spain, with an investigation now underway.

‌



Paredes was amongst those involved in a brawl with Eric Garcia and Gavi, in which he appeared to throw punches, yet escaped without a red card.

Despite his behaviour, Paredes focused solely on their tournament campaign in his statement following Sunday's final. It read: "Thank you, Argentina! I love you today and always. Today, I write with a heavy heart, having been unable to bring our country the joy it so richly deserves.

"But with a chest full of pride for having given everything we had and for flying our flag at the very top once again! Thank you to everyone who was part of this national team. To this group of players who gave their all to represent this jersey, fighting for it until the very last second of every match! It was an honour to be part of the best Argentine national team in history."

‌



View 2 Images Leandro Paredes tried to fight Spain players after Argentina lost the World Cup final

Paredes' mum, Myriam Benitez, also spoke out on the controversy while talking to journalists awaiting Argentina's arrival at the Ezeiza airport in Buenos Aires. She said: "We never disrespect anyone. Respect always, I think that's everything that motivates us and gets us to where we really want to go. I know what the Argentine National Team means to my son."

The 32-year-old is currently turning out for Boca Juniors in his homeland following stints in France and Italy. A number of the Argentina squad actually ply their trade in Spain, with Nahuel Molina amongst those on Atletico Madrid's books.

Article continues below

He was another player embroiled in an altercation as he furiously squared up to Spain midfielder Rodri after seemingly striking him in the stomach. Dani Olmo also found himself on the wrong end of a blow, with Argentina coach Roberto Ayala swinging his arm towards the Barcelona star's face.

Sports.title: 'Biggest moment of my career' - Emotional Menzies reflects on Humphries win
Sports.content:
An emotional Cameron Menzies dubbed his win against Luke Humphries "the biggest moment of my darts career" after his dramatic upset secured his place in the next round of the World Matchplay Darts.

Menzies pulled out an incredible Big Fish checkout to beat world No 2 Humphries 10-7 in his first-ever triumph at Winter Gardens.

The monumental victory was a full-circle moment for the Scot, and represents a remarkable turnaround in fortune just eight months after he required surgery for punching a table during his first-round defeat to Josh Manby at the World Championship.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cameron Menzies lands the Big Fish finish to stun Luke Humphries at the World Matchplay.

"I don't know how to explain that [victory]. I did believe in my heart that I could maybe cause an upset but I would have to play it out of my skin," Menzies said.

"I wouldn't say I played it out of my skin, but I played really well. I did say before the game started, to beat Luke, I need to take every chance that he gives me.

"It's not like Luke to give a lot of chances away but obviously I'm going to take it. A lot went in. I was happy. I stole a few legs to win but it's made the best moment of my darts career."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cameron Menzies hits a HUGE double-double finish against Luke Humphries!

The Scot revealed in February that he considered giving up darts altogether, but reflected on his greatest ever win after a "terrible" start to 2026, which also included the death of his uncle:

"It's up there because I didn't think I was going to qualify for this.

"The start of the year, I was terrible. I was just really bad. I had a really poor start to the year but I went through a lot.

"I'm in a better place mentally and physically. I'm enjoying darts again."

Mardle: Menzies knows he can handle anything now

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hear from Cameron Menzies and Wayne Mardle after the Scotsman claimed a famous win over Luke Humphries at the World Matchplay.

Sky Sports Darts' Wayne Mardle:

"It's his best ever win, and he mentioned that.

"With Cameron Menzies, everyone mentions his emotions, but it's the way he had to win that game.

"Nothing went according to plan. He was broken back early twice, that's up and down emotions. The high of breaking to being broken back.

Image: Menzies' win against Humphries was his first at Winter Gardens

"Then he went on a run, and got pegged back.

"There was a lot happening in that game, but he held it all together beautifully.

"Humphries had an amazing spell of four legs, but then Menzies found a level again, and that's something we don't see enough.

"What he should take away from tonight was the way he handled this situation. It was like he was there a million times before.

"He knows he can handle anything now."

What's happening at the World Matchplay on Tuesday?

Image: Luke Littler, World Matchplay Darts 2026

The 2026 Betfred World Matchplay continues at the iconic Winter Gardens from July 18-26, as a 32-player field compete for the prestigious Phil Taylor Trophy.

Two-time world champion Luke Littler takes on Nathan Aspinall in a blockbuster clash after opening his defence of the Phil Taylor Trophy with a sensational 10-6 win over Niko Springer on Day One in Blackpool.

Stephen Bunting takes on Josh Rock after winning through a Winter Gardens classic against debutant Niels Zonneveld, surviving three match darts to edge past the Dutchman 13-12.

Three-time World Matchplay winner Michael van Gerwen faces fellow Dutchman Dirk van Duijvenbode, while Gary Anderson - the 2018 champion - goes up against 2023 runner-up Jonny Clayton having recorded the eighth-highest average in World Matchplay history, averaging 109.96 in his 10-2 demolition of Ryan Joyce.

Sports.title: 'We know a lot of what's going on' - Rahm tight-lipped on LIV future
Sports.content:
Jon Rahm has remained tight-lipped about his LIV Golf future for 2027, saying "we know a lot of what's going on" but he is not in a position to share details.

The future of the breakaway golf league beyond the end of this season remains in doubt after the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund confirmed in April it is ending its funding for the series.

As one of the league's highest-profile players, Rahm's future beyond this season has been the subject of speculation amid LIV's bid to seek alternative investment.

LIV is in the UK this week for its event at the JCB Golf and Country Club in Staffordshire, its first tournament since the start of June.

Asked in Tuesday's pre-event press conference whether he had any clarity about LIV's future heading into 2027, Rahm said: "Yes. Well, we're in contact with them.

"We know a lot of what's going on, yeah.

"Not that I can share with you guys right now."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment New Zealand's Ryan Fox won The Open with a 12ft birdie putt on the 18th hole at Royal Birkdale

Put to him that he seemed optimistic, the Spaniard said: "I'm always optimistic.

"I play a game for a living. I can't really be too upset about how things are going in life. Even though I'm very frustrated on the course very often, off the course I'm very different to what a lot of people think."

Rahm, who joined the league from the start of 2024, was then asked directly whether he expected to be playing on LIV next year.

"I'm not going to share anything that I can't share with you guys right now," he replied.

Rahm wants clarity over code of conduct warnings

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jon Rahm received a code of conduct warning at The Open after throwing his club following his tee shot on the par-three 15th at Royal Birkdale

Rahm returns to LIV action after finishing tied 46th at The Open last week after shooting four-over for his final round.

The Spaniard received a code of conduct warning from Friday's second round at Royal Birkdale last week after throwing his club following his tee shot on the par-three 15th.

Asked whether he had sufficient clarity on what actions constitute a warning or a two-shot penalty under the new-for-2026 major code of conduct rules, Rahm said: "I personally have no idea what the line is. No clue."

He added: "I think you can all kind of understand what it may or may not be. I completely forgot about it until it happened. I know they issued multiple warnings over the course of the week.

"Yeah, it would be nice to have some clarity."

Asian Tour announces partnership with PGA and DP World Tours

Image: David Puig of Spain played on the LIV sponsored 'international series', organised by the Asian Tour

The Spaniard was speaking on the same day that the Asian Tour announced a new deal with the DP World Tour and PGA Tour, simultaneously threatening their ties with LIV, with whom they have shared a lucrative partnership with since 2022.

The PGA Tour and DP World Tour have a separate alliance that has yet to be renewed, which includes 10 top European Tour players earning PGA Tour cards, but the alliance with the Asian Tour - along with the PGA Tour's involvement with the Australian Open - is seen as progress on a new deal.

LIV - who will see the announcement as a blow - invested $300m in the Asian Tour to create the "International Series" with purses of up to $2m. They have been won by LIV players such as Peter Uihlein, Carlos Ortiz and David Puig.

"We feel the time is now right to collaborate with the DP World Tour and PGA Tour to enhance the Asian Tour for our members, fans and partners," said Cho Minn Thant, commissioner and CEO of the Asian Tour.

"Bringing the three tours together under one partnership will increase the bandwidth of the professional game in Asia.

"Not only will co-sanctioning events see our members competing regularly on the global stage, but we are excited to welcome players from the other Tours to our pinnacle events."

Sports.title: Charges and challenges - the scale of the task facing Maresca at Man City
Sports.content:
Plenty of the Premier League's top clubs have rolled the managerial dice ahead of next season. Manchester City are one of those starting a new era, turning to Enzo Maresca in the wake of Pep Guardiola's decision to depart.

Maresca is returning for his third stint at the club, having been an academy coach in 2020-21 and then Guardiola's assistant in 2022-23 - the famous Premier League-Champions League-FA Cup treble-winning campaign.

He is familiar with the pursuit of silverware, but is yet to be the one to deliver it at such scale. So, how well positioned is he to lead Man City to glory in 2026-27?

Sky Sports' Ben Ransom and Laura Hunter explore Maresca's chances of success in year one - and whether trophies are the only barometer by which he will be judged in the wake of Guardiola's seismic exit.

Sympathetic start gives Maresca breathing room

Maresca has been given a kind start to his term, meeting Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Coventry City in his first three outings - a generous run to be able to establish some early rhythm. It also gives Man City's World Cup warriors, those in battle until the very last, a chance to ease back in.

Rodri played nearly every minute of Spain's triumphant campaign and is the most susceptible to breaking down with fatigue. Given those first three fixtures will still heavily favour Man City without him, he should benefit from a phased return.

Maresca will, however, be under pressure to deliver given how winnable those fixtures are on paper. He cannot afford to cede ground early, especially as City face Man Utd and Liverpool in two of the next three in September. Clearly both of those rival bouts hold significance beyond the result.

As the Italian acknowledged when joining, he is in a "dream situation", inheriting a well-balanced squad with incredible talent and depth, built by Guardiola. "It provides the consistency I need to do my job effectively," he said.

The demands will therefore be the same as what were placed on Guardiola, without necessarily having the unique job security the Spaniard was afforded. Guardiola always managed on his own terms. Maresca has a strong bond with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak, but won't necessarily get the same privilege.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports football journalist Laura Hunter says Enzo Maresca won't be afforded time to excel as Manchester City boss

How much time will players need to adapt?

In terms of style, it's not quite rinse and repeat but there are plenty of similarities between Maresca and Guardiola's preferred way of playing.

Both are rooted in possessing the ball, favouring control, and pressing aggressively. Maresca is arguably more expansive, though, wanting to stretch the pitch with wingers that play high and wide.

Image: Chelsea's stats in their only full season under Enzo Maresca

City's wingers have been coached more recently to play a style where they tuck inside and rotate to create central overloads. Most of the play revolves around Rodri, but it's fluid.

Watching City under Guardiola often meant seeing defenders step into midfield, midfielders become forwards, or even drop into full-back. Maresca's more rigid 4-2-3-1 structure will likely make for more traditional roles.

It also requires a high-functioning No 10 to link play. At Chelsea, that was Cole Palmer. Maresca has got Phil Foden or Rayan Cherki to choose between, should he wish to adopt the same setup here.

How is the squad shaping up?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Ben Ransom explains why Manchester City decided to sign Elliot Anderson for £116m, making him the most expensive British player in history

There has been a concerted effort over the past two or three transfer windows under Hugo Viana to lower the average age of the squad. It's dropped from 29 to just over 25, albeit a leadership void has appeared following the departures of Bernardo Silva and John Stones this summer - and Kevin de Bruyne before them.

Rodri and Ruben Dias are important, while last season saw City lean further into a leadership role for Erling Haaland. Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol are also experienced, stable figures, plus Mateo Kovacic. The spine of the team remains incredibly strong.

Business to date has been costly but smart. Elliot Anderson, signed for mega money from Nottingham Forest, has been bought to add robustness and future-proof midfield and young Jeremy Monga has been poached from Leicester.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With Rodri linked with a move away from Manchester City, Sky Sports News reporter Ben Ransom discusses whether Ayyoub Bouaddi could be brought in to replace the midfielder

The wish list also includes a right-back and a winger, while keeping tabs on Lille teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi, who excelled at the World Cup for Morocco. Arsenal are also admirers of him.

Depending on potential suitors meeting the club's valuation, outgoings might comprise a selection of: Savinho, Omar Marmoush, Nico Gonzalez, Jack Grealish, Tijjani Reijnders and Rico Lewis. Transfer activity is expected to accelerate now the World Cup has concluded.

What are Maresca's main challenges?

This is the first time since the Abu Dhabi takeover that the plan is uncertain. 10 years ago, all preparation went into building a club to lure Guardiola to the Premier League. That vision has been and gone, so where now?

City have forged a culture geared towards winning silverware, anything less is unlikely to be tolerated for a sustained period. Fans arrive at the Etihad expecting to be entertained, but above all, demanding to win. Balancing both is where Maresca's Chelsea failed.

The 46-year-old does have the benefit of not being the only managerial newbie at one of the top clubs, though, making for a changeable Premier League landscape as the natural order figures itself out. At City, that is being viewed as an opportunity to take advantage of.

Andoni Iraola at Liverpool, Xabi Alonso at Chelsea and, perhaps to a lesser extent, Michael Carrick at Man Utd, all hold question marks. This era of unknowns is fertile ground for anyone with ambition to make a mark. Very much sink or swim.

What about the 115 charges?

115 Premier League charges still cloud the club. Maresca will have to field difficult questions from the media over it.

Guardiola was the master of public-facing confrontation, having had to handle media glare at some of Europe's biggest clubs all his career. He knew the City press pack well and how to shut down any exchanges he wished not to speak on.

Maresca came under fire at Chelsea at times but mainly over football matters. How he handles this situation will likely impact his first 12 months - assuming a verdict is reached within that timeframe.

Man City have denied all of the charges.

Maresca is due to give his first Man City press conference on Friday, July 24. You can follow everything that is said in our dedicated live blog here.

Sports.title: 'Fery can improve but that's exciting' - Henman optimistic as Brit eyes US Open run
Sports.content:
British No 1 Arthur Fery will head into the American hard-court swing with areas he can improve ahead of the US Open - but that's "exciting", says Tim Henman.

The wild card's surprise run to the Wimbledon semi-finals has injected a much-needed shot of positivity and given British fans a new name to follow in the Grand Slams - starting at the US Open in New York - live on Sky Sports Tennis from August 30.

The challenge for the 24-year-old now is to acclimatise to his new standing in the game and the loss of anonymity and the freedom that brings with it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arthur Fery reflects on his Wimbledon experience, his massive climb up the world rankings and the tournaments he's planning to play next

The 23-year-old, who has soared to 36 in the world from No 114, was the last player standing in what was an otherwise dismal tournament for the host nation, but he became only the fifth British man this century to reach the second week at the All England Club.

Fery has earned direct entry to a Masters event for the first time in Cincinnati - 13-23 August - before appearing at the Winston-Salem Open from 23-29 August ahead of his debut at Flushing Meadows.

Speaking at Royal Birkdale ahead of The Open, Henman called Fery's dream run at the All England Club "amazing" and "transformational for his career and his life".

The former British No 1 said: "He started the year at 185 in the world, qualified in Melbourne and then has continued to improve his ranking - then getting a wild card at Wimbledon ranked 114 and winning five matches getting to the semi-finals it was an incredible performance - and I think it also shows the fine margins between these top players.

"If you're in the top 250 in the world you're an extremely good player and on your day you've got a chance of beating anyone, so huge for him to be 36 in the world now getting to the other Grand Slams and Masters 1000, so he's got an opportunity to really plan his schedule moving forward."

Sports.title: Hamilton tells himself to 'step it up' after Spa setbacks
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says he needs to "step it up" at this weekend's Hungarian Grand Prix after admitting "can't afford" to repeat the crash that compromised his weekend in Belgium amid Ferrari's competitive form.

Hamilton finished fourth last Sunday at Spa-Francorchamps but felt he could have challenged for the win had he crashed at the end of final practice on Saturday in an accident that required a host of parts to be replaced on his car ahead of qualifying.

Team-mate Charles Leclerc qualified and finished ahead of Hamilton for the second race in a row with the Monegasque, while gaining race time through a fortuitously timed Virtual Safety Car, eventually finishing just two seconds behind race winner Kimi Antonelli, the championship leader.

With Ferrari performing better than they had expected relative to Mercedes on the high-speed tracks of Silverstone, where Leclerc won, and now Spa, the Scuderia are being tipped to run particularly strongly at the Hungaroring this weekend, a circuit which will play more to their car's cornering strengths.

Asked by Sky Sports F1 whether he was confident he could gather more momentum over the rest of the season, Hamilton said: "I think so. This weekend was a bit unfortunate and Silverstone [was] again.

"It's really great to see the performance that we are bringing and we are improving the car constantly. I think we have got more stuff coming in the pipeline to try and close that gap down.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Despite being given a five-second penalty for an opening-lap collision with George Russell, Lewis Hamilton was left more frustrated with his performance over the weekend as he finished fourth in Belgium

"But to be here and have that pace generally that we did as a team is really encouraging.

"There's still a long, long way to go.

"Can't afford weekends like this in a sense of my performance [on Saturday] so I'm going to step it up in terms of focus level for next week."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Karun Chandhok was at the SkyPad to analyse whether Lewis Hamilton should have been awarded a five-second penalty for his collision with George Russell on the opening lap

Although he finished off the podium for just the second time in six races, Hamilton moved back ahead of George Russell into second place in the Drivers' Championship after the former team-mates made contact and the Mercedes driver spun out on the first lap.

Hamilton, who received a five-second penalty from stewards for the incident, is 45 points behind Antonelli.

The seven-time world champion has won a record eight times in Hungary, while the circuit was also the scene of his most-recent Grand Prix pole position in 2023.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ted Kravitz explains why he thinks Ferrari have the best chance to challenge Mercedes at the Hungarian Grand Prix

Leclerc encouraged but 'not yet' at level he wants to be

The races at Silverstone and Spa also confirmed an overdue return to form for Leclerc, who had been struggling to tailor his driving style to the demands of the 2026 cars and had endured a difficult run of results.

Leclerc remains cautious about agreeing with suggestions he has made an absolute breakthrough but is encouraged by his recent rate of improvement.

"I'm confident in saying that I made a step forward. Whether I'm at the level where I want to perform, not yet," said Leclerc.

"There are still things in the car that I need to drive around. I cannot drive completely naturally, and that is slowing me down in some parts of the race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix

"So, there are still things that I've got to work on in order to be better. But surely it was a step forward, and for that I'm happy.

"I'll continue with the one-race-at-a-time approach because, with these cars, it's very difficult to be confident that if one race weekend goes well, the other one will, because it relies on such small details.

"With what you do with your driving, it's never a given that you get the same deployment from one lap to the other, and that's maybe the frustrating bit about these cars."

Sports.content:

Bournemouth have made Scott a number of offers since discussions began towards the end of the season - but it is believed the midfielder has indicated he is not currently willing to agree new terms.

The Cherries do not want to sell the talented midfielder, who has entered the final two years of his current contract, and have already knocked back inquiries from the Premier League trio.

Sports.title: Arsenal most impacted? The clubs hit hardest by World Cup
Sports.content:
The World Cup is over but could Premier League clubs feel the effects of the tournament as they prepare for the new season?

The World Cup spanned six weeks and ended in success for Spain, who beat Argentina 1-0 in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

There were more than 150 Premier League players at the tournament, so how could their involvement impact their clubs?

Man City had most players

Manchester City were the best represented Premier League club, with 16 of their players featuring at the tournament.

That total included Spain captain Rodri, who started every game and won player of the tournament, as well as Marc Guehi, Nico O'Reilly, new signing Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki, all of whom reached the last four.

Arsenal had the next-highest number of players feature at the tournament, with 13, including Spain trio Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi as well England quartet Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke.

Spurs, Sunderland, Aston Villa, Crystal Palace and Manchester United were next on the list having all hit double figures for players who featured at the tournament.

Manchester City topped the list in terms of minutes played too, with a combined total of 5,595 putting them well ahead of next-highest Arsenal, who totalled 4,224, with Spurs third on 3,318.

The Premier League player who played the most was actually Aston Villa's Emi Martinez, who played every minute for Argentina, including four chunks of extra-time, totalling 810 minutes.

His Argentina team-mate Alexis Mac Allister, of Liverpool, played the next most minutes, on 749, ahead of Rodri on 726.

How long players remained at the tournament is significant because FIFA have mandated a minimum of three weeks off for players before the new season, meaning those who went deep at the tournament will be reporting for pre-season much later than the rest.

The Premier League season begins in just over four weeks on Friday August 21, when Arsenal face Coventry live on Sky Sports.

Injuries bite

While Manchester City players played the most minutes at the World Cup, they mostly remained free of injury.

The same can't be said of some of their Premier League rivals.

Aston Villa lost Amadou Onana to an anterior cruciate ligament injury, which typically means a player misses between six and nine months.

Image: Belgium's Amadou Onana suffered an ACL injury

Arsenal's William Saliba picked up a back injury in France's semi-final defeat to Spain, while Saka and Rice also experienced fitness issues during the tournament.

Youri Tielemans, who has moved from Aston Villa to Manchester United, suffered a hamstring injury which caused him to miss Belgium's quarter-final loss to Spain.

Tielemans' new Manchester United team-mate Manuel Ugarte sustained a similar injury to Onana before Uruguay's group-stage exit.

Arsenal most impacted overall

When combining factors including minutes played, players used, injuries, potential injury durations and recency of appearances in an overall impact index, Arsenal come out as the most impacted club.

Aston Villa, Manchester United and Spurs are next on the list, with Manchester City only fifth, despite having had more players feature at the tournament than any other side.

Those sides are now facing disrupted pre-season campaigns.

At the other end of the scale, the least impacted club was Coventry, who did not have a single player who featured at the World Cup, meaning Frank Lampard effectively has a full squad to work with in pre-season.

The other newly-promoted teams, Hull and Ipswich, were lightly affected, while Bournemouth, Nottingham Forest and Brighton also feature at the lower end of the overall impact index.

Sports.title: ‘The utmost respect for him’: Alex Ferguson pays tribute to Kevin Keegan
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson has saluted Kevin Keegan for building Newcastle’s “greatest team”. Keegan, who had cancer, died on Monday at the age of 75 and Ferguson has joined the tributes for one of football’s most endearing characters.

Ferguson and Keegan were involved a fierce battle for Premier League supremacy, with Ferguson’s Manchester United pipping Newcastle to the title in 1996. “I had the utmost respect for him,” Ferguson told Track Radio. “We had many duels when he was manager of Newcastle, but the job he did at Newcastle was fantastic. He re-energised that club and he brought that enthusiasm and fanaticism great supporters can give.

“And he also brought three great players to the club – [David] Ginola, [Faustino] Asprilla, Philippe Albert – and added a bit of class to the team. The challenges we had with Newcastle at that time were huge.”

Keegan, frustrated by Ferguson’s comments in the media towards the end of the tense title fight, memorably ranted at the Scot in a television interview. Despite that, Ferguson remained friendly with the former Liverpool and England striker and admired Keegan’s impressive rebuilding job at Newcastle.

The club were in danger of relegation to the third tier when Keegan took over, but he saved them from that fate and then won promotion to the Premier League in 1993. Keegan made Newcastle so dynamic they were referred to as “the entertainers”.

Ferguson believes the title runners-up were the best team in the club’s history. “Kevin carried the love of the game on his sleeve, there’s no question about that, and that carried right on to the fans, to the players,” he said. “That period at Newcastle was of emotion, it was excitement. They brought these great players to the club and they added to it, and it gave Newcastle – I think – their best ever team.”

View image in fullscreen Tributes at St James’ Park for Kevin Keegan, who died on Monday Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PA

Ferguson said he and Keegan had bumped into each other at a pub near Wentworth golf club a few weeks after that season. They spent the night around a piano with all thoughts of the rivalry forgotten. “The great thing about him, he held no grudges,” Ferguson said. “That was a fantastic quality he had and we had a great night.

“All aside whatever happened in previous weeks, that was soon forgotten. I really respected him for that.”

Sports.title: La Liga chief claims Fifa is ‘destroying football industry’ and calls for Infantino to quit
Sports.content:
La Liga’s president, Javier Tebas, has accused Fifa of “destroying the football industry” and called for its president, Gianni Infantino, to quit. Tebas spoke out as the dust settled on the 2026 World Cup with suggestions that the 2030 tournament could be increased from 48 to 64 teams.

“Increasing the number of national teams makes no sense,” Tebas said in an interview with the Italian newspaper La Gazzetta dello Sport. “The football industry is not just the World Cup, which is the most important event. Not everything can revolve around the World Cup. It is national competitions that support this sport.

“They are destroying the football industry, which generates tens of thousands of jobs, for an event that lasts 40 days and involves a minority of players. We need fewer national teams and more protection for national football, at all levels. They don’t realise, they are making irresponsible decisions.”

Tebas said Infantino should leave his position. “His time is up. However, he has the support of the system, of the federations, so there is not much more to add, is there?

“There is no opposition candidate, nobody wants to stand just to lose. This is the system and it is a system rotten at its core.

“These past few days here in America I have heard many people who are against Infantino, who disagree with what he does. They say it, but then they do nothing. I don’t know if silence or complicity is worse, because those who are silent are perfectly aware of the damage football is suffering.”

Infantino has been a controversial figure during his 10 years as Fifa president. He is poised to be re-elected for a fourth term in Fifa’s March 2027 congress, although Tebas believes Infantino might have been brought down by the Folarin Balogun affair if the USA had beaten Belgium in their World Cup last-16 tie.

Scandal-proof: why Infantino's Fifa power can't be touched – video

The USA striker’s one-match ban was suspended by Fifa’s disciplinary committee, allowing him to play against Belgium, after a phone call to Infantino from Donald Trump. Infantino said the decision to revoke Balogun’s ban was taken independently by the disciplinary committee “based on the applicable regulations and the specific facts”.

Tebas said: “The suspension of the American player’s ban was absolutely serious; they were lucky Belgium eliminated the USA because a case could have arisen that might have cost Infantino his job. Since Belgium won, they managed to bury the matter.

“But these things are just the tip of the iceberg. Fifa arranges things as it wants, for what it wants, for its own interests, certainly not for football. So, if they need a 27-minute half-time break, they’ll have it.

“Hydration breaks are a lie. We have them in La Liga, but when it’s genuinely hot. Here, the pitches in Dallas, Los Angeles, Atlanta had air conditioning; I had to put on a jumper in the stands. It was a lie, a break for advertising.”

Fifa has been approached for comment.
