Sports.title: Argentina players face bans as Fifa opens investigation into World Cup final brawls
Sports.content:
Fifa has opened an investigation into the violent scenes that followed Spain’s World Cup final win on Sunday, with several Argentina players facing bans.

Nahuel Molina appeared to strike Spain’s captain Rodri in the stomach as he ran on to the pitch following the final whistle, while there was also a large melee on the halfway line, where Leandro Paredes appeared to grab Eric García by the throat before throwing Gavi to the ground.

Parades was subsequently shown a red card by the referee, Slavko Vincic, who had also sent off Enzo Fernández towards the end of normal time, as well as booking three other Argentina players and the head coach, Lionel Scaloni.

“Following an assessment of the relevant match reports for the Fifa World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, and in line with article 36 of the Fifa Disciplinary Code (FDC), the Fifa Disciplinary Committee has appointed a Disciplinary and Ethics Prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of the FDC with regard to the post-match incidents,” Fifa said in a statement.

Fifa is also investigating Argentina’s conduct after their semi-final win over England, when their players celebrated with a banner proclaiming “Las Malvinas son Argentinas”, which was smuggled into the Atlanta Stadium by supporters.

Fifa prohibits players or teams making political statements, so those involved could be banned.

Sports.title: Gaza celebrates World Cup victory of Spanish team they took into their hearts
Sports.content:
The Spanish football team’s World Cup win has been celebrated in the streets of Gaza, where Spain’s support for Palestinian rights and Israel’s backing for the Argentinian team turned the competition into more than a football showdown.

Gathered at cafes and outdoor screenings, Palestinians defied the risk of Israeli attacks to cheer on a team they had taken to their hearts.

Many waving Spanish flags paid tribute to teenage star Lamine Yamal, who brought a Palestinian flag to celebrations for Barcelona’s La Liga win in May.

“Whoever raises the Palestinian flag deserves to raise the World Cup,” the Gaza al-Irada amputee football team wrote in a pre-game video message for the Spanish team.

Saadi al-Masri, 40 and captain of the amputee team in Gaza, watched the game with friends in a cafe. “I support Spain because we see it as a country that stands with the Palestinian cause and supports Palestinian rights,” he said.

View image in fullscreen Palestinians defied the risk of Israeli attacks to cheer on Spain. Photograph: Issam Rimawi/Anadolu/Getty Images

Spain has been among Europe’s most vocal critics of Israel’s war on Gaza and state-backed violence in the occupied West Bank. It is pushing for stronger European Union action over human rights violations, including suspension of a broad free trade pact.

When Israel’s defence minister attacked Yamal for raising the Palestinian flag, accusing him of “inciting hatred”, the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, was quick to defend the young player.

“Lamine has only expressed the solidarity with Palestine that is felt by millions of us in Spain. Another reason to be proud of him,” he said in a social media post.

Israeli support for Argentina was led by Netanyahu, who has cultivated close ties with far-right president Javier Milei, and posted a good luck message for the team ahead of the final.

The Palestinian delegation to the United Nations responded with an image of the Spanish team, under the headline “world champions”.

Even keen fans in Gaza have struggled to keep up with matches during the World Cup. Most of the 2 million Palestinians in the territory live in tent camps after Israeli attacks destroyed their homes, with little access to power or internet connections.

Arkan al-Walaida, 23, went to internet cafes to seek out match highlights each morning during the tournament, looking for short videos on TikTok or Fifa’s official YouTube and Instagram pages.

When she found out on Monday that Spain had won, she was overwhelmed. “Honestly, I felt like I was about to cry from happiness,” she said. “We see their support as a sign of humanity.”

Al-Masri watched the match at a cafe, packed with an excited crowd. “We were very happy when the final whistle confirmed Spain’s victory,” he said, but fear of Israeli airstrikes meant there were no late-night parties.

In early July, an Israeli bomb killed Mohamed al-Wahidi, a Palestinian aid worker who organised screenings of World Cup matches in Gaza.

The strike, just before the game between Egypt and Argentina, also killed brothers aged eight and 10, and a second man. The Israeli military confirmed the attack but said it had not targeted al-Wahidi.

Sports.title: A big red speaker, Louis Vuitton trophy trunks and a tattoo bet – how Spain celebrated World Cup win
Sports.content:
On the night that Spain won their first World Cup in 2010, Rodrigo Hernández was on camp somewhere lost in the woods of Connecticut. He had been canoeing when the selección beat Germany in the semi-final, upset to have missed it, and for the final he convinced one of the supervisors to let him watch, alone, on a mini-laptop in the hut where the staff slept. When Andrés Iniesta scored the winning goal in the 116th minute, he ran off screaming, doing laps of the lake. He was 14.

On the night that Spain won their second World Cup 16 years later, Rodrigo Hernández was back in the US, not so far from there. When Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in the 106th minute, he ran off screaming in a straighter line and accompanied this time: towards the corner where his other family were. And then, when it ended, when the fighting finished too, he collected the trophy, pausing just long enough for Donald Trump to leave centre stage before lifting it, his timing perfect even here.

It wasn’t the only trophy he had, but those could be handed over and this could not. By the time Rodri departed at 9.38pm eastern time, the last man out of the dressing room at the New Jersey New York Stadium, he couldn’t carry them all: walking with him, just ahead, Ladis had to lend a hand. A football team is never just the players, nor even just the coaches. When he departed the dressing room nine minutes earlier, the same happened for Pau Cubarsí. Nuria helped him, their boy: just 19, looking like a kid down here in the stadium in real life but not on the pitch where he’s a leader. Luis de la Fuente was accompanied by Paloma.

Rodri came with the trophy for the tournament’s best player too. Cubarsí had the young player award, Unai Simón the Golden Glove. They also had two World Cups, every Spain player did: a replica of their own in a black Louis Vuitton trophy trunk, not easy to fit under an arm, and another in Lego. Rodri had three: both of those and the cup. They departed laden down, great big plastic bags full, pieces of the history they made. Shirts, in red and yellow and blue and white. Balls, boots. They had cut the net and taken pieces of that too. They had been given rings, NBA style.

View image in fullscreen Mikel Merino holds a replica of the trophy in the dressing room after Spain’s triumph. Photograph: Alex Pantling/Fifa/Getty Images

Before the final began, Marc Cucurella had sneaked off towards the touchline and buried a coin in the pitch, like that other left-back Joan Capdevila had done in 2010. Iniesta had been out there, his name chanted, as he showed the cup to the stands. After it, Sergio Ramos brought it back again. Dashing out, excitedly kissing it, he placed it on the plinth for this new generation, achieving the impossible in emulating them, to go and collect. One by one they passed, Borja Iglesias and Lamine Yamal among the most evasive in shaking Trump’s hand, until Rodri took the trophy and lifted it to the sky.

Nico Williams went to find his mum in the front row and handed over his medal. Lamine Yamal had made his way across to Lionel Messi, who was sitting but who stood for him, embracing the boy in the bath, the successor: a rite of passage, an image that will be for ever. The actor Javier Bardem was hugging Iglesias, his new friend and idol. Ferran Torres was talking about a “great liberation”: he had suffered, felt how cruel this game could be, how people could be too, but he said: “Destiny is written: God gives to those who deserve.” And Keyne was, well, Keyne. In the dressing room – the same one, Cucurella noted, where he had been at last year’s Club World Cup – the champagne was cracked open.

It was brief – the flight to Spain was scheduled for 11pm and they wanted to get back – and soon they were on their way again. Behind the screen, along the corridor they came, way down in the depths and the half-light of the stadium. The president, the staff, all the players; the many, many people who made this so. Iglesias carried a bag so big it was like he was a student taking his washing home, and he was struggling to stop that box slipping. In the other hand he wheeled a big red speaker. Now playing: Dirty Cash (Money Talks) by PAWSA & Adventures of Stevie V. Lamine Yamal came, via the anti-doping room, in orange sunglasses, four chains, black cap on backwards. He didn’t wear his medal, but most did, thick discs round their necks. And commemorative shirts, ordered up in case.

View image in fullscreen Spain’s Lamine Yamal and Argentina’s Lionel Messi embrace after the match. Photograph: Jeenah Moon/Reuters

Back in Dallas, at a celebration after the semi-final victory, someone had joked to the federation president, Rafael Louzán, that the shirts should say world champions on one side and Finalissima winners on the other, two trophies in one. Tempting, but these bore just the one trophy, “Spain 26” on the back. The war in the Middle East had prevented the Finalissima from going ahead in Doha as scheduled in March and every time another option was offered, Argentina said no, the impression that of a team, a federation, running scared. “Good job we didn’t play,” Emi Martínez had said then, after they scraped past Mauritania in a hastily arranged friendly that filled the hole. “If we had played [Spain] like this …”

Something like this might have happened. Not just because Argentina played like this but because Spain made them play like this. “We gave them a battering,” came the verdict from one of those heading out of the dressing room. This wasn’t just a win; this was more. Has a 1-0 ever been as dominant? There was a moment late in the game, still at 0-0, when the Spain fans chanted: “Look at them! Look at them! How they shit themselves!” and they weren’t wrong. Argentina could not get out all game; as Spain turned the screw, still less, the goal seemingly inevitable; the surprise was that it hadn’t come yet, that there would be just one. When it did it came as a liberation but also an act of irresistible logic.

View image in fullscreen Ferran Torres scores the only goal of the World Cup final. Photograph: Jewel Samad/AFP/Getty Images

Torres’s shot was Spain’s 20th. Argentina didn’t manage one until the 115th minute. They didn’t manage any on target, all game. Across 900 World Cup games for which Opta has the stats, it is only the third time that a team has failed to shoot. And this in the final. They had done to Argentina what they did to France and to everyone, choking them. For the whole tournament Spain had an xG against of 0.3 per game. “If my gloves could talk, they would say they didn’t have much work to do,” Simón said. “Many teams depend too much on the back line,” Aymeric Laporte said, but not Spain.

This was the triumph of a collective, of a group; it ended in New York, but it was built in Chattanooga and beyond, over 51 days. It is the triumph of an idea, a conviction and of a coach too: a victory for De la Fuente and the system he leads and the system that made him. He began his coaching career at Deportivo Alavés in the third tier, where he lasted just 11 games. It was November 2011 when he left and he has not had a club job since. For months, no one returned his calls. He was on the dole for a year and a half until he saw an advert for a job: the Spanish federation was looking for a coach for the youth system. He started in the under-17s. He won the European Championship with the under-19s and the under-21s. Then he won it with the senior side; now he has won the World Cup.

“They asked me what there is left to win; we said the next game in September because they’re insatiable,” he insisted afterwards. Simón said: “The manager is outstanding; he has been our leader.” Cucurella, meanwhile, was in trouble. He had promised that if Spain won the World Cup, he would get a tattoo of De la Fuente’s face and now he had to decide where to put it to minimise the damage, the flight home an opportunity to think. Not least to think what a fool he had been.

View image in fullscreen Marc Cucurella is to have a tattoo of Luis de la Fuente’s face after Spain’s win. Photograph: Lisi Niesner/Reuters

“I said: ‘You made a bad mistake’,” the coach joked. “But it’s not like I am so horrendously ugly that you have to put it somewhere it can’t be seen. And they are men of their word.” For all the laughs, that final line really mattered, and he knows: 10 of them played with him at junior level. The first title he ever won was the Under-19 Euros in 2015. In the middle of his midfield that day was Rodrigo Hernández.

Eleven years on, 16 since he watched Spain’s first World Cup win, motivation sought and identification found in what they achieved, Rodri was back in the US. The embodiment of that idea, a player who approached perfection here, no one played more passes nor made more tackles than him. No one had his weight either, the captain leading Spain out and leading them back too. Like so many of his teammates at a tournament that was an expression of justice and vindication too, he had suffered for this, a torn cruciate ligament overcome.

“It doesn’t matter if you fall, there’s always a reason to get up again,” he said and now he had it right here in his hands. It was 9.40pm when he boarded the bus bound for the airport, carrying the actual World Cup.

Sports.title: Neuer to Neymar: 11 World Cup players who retired from international football
Sports.content:
Manuel Neuer (Germany, 40)

First participated in the World Cup in 2010 before winning the trophy four years later. Germany have had little success since and their penalty shootout defeat by Paraguay marked the end of Neuer’s international career. He initially retired after Euro 2024 but reversed that decision a few weeks before this tournament. “Despite the bitter end, I don’t regret this decision,” he said after his 23rd and final World Cup appearance. The former Germany defender Robert Huth criticised the decision to bring Neuer out of retirement: “I think the big one that really unsettles the squad was the Neuer inclusion. I think [it was] really unexpected, he came late to the table.”

Patrik Schick (Czechia, 30)

Made his World Cup debut this summer having left an impression at Euro 2020. Schick failed to score as Czechia went winless and were eliminated in the group stage. The striker announced his international retirement hours after the final group game. “Today, my national team chapter is coming to an end,” he said. The official Czechia statement paid tribute: “Thank you for every match, every goal, and the pride with which you represented the Czech Republic.”

Guillermo Ochoa (Mexico, 41)

Cemented himself as a fans’ favourite in 2014 when he kept a famous clean sheet against the World Cup hosts, Brazil. His playing time was limited this summer, but he got 12 minutes against Czechia, where he was celebrated by teammates. After full time the manager, Javier Aguirre, said: “The moment he stepped on to the pitch, it overshadowed everything else. He is a world-class legend, and I am incredibly proud of him.” Ochoa later posted: “It was the greatest privilege of my life. Thank you for believing, for always accompanying us. I love you Mexico.”

View image in fullscreen Guillermo Ochoa shows his emotions after Mexico’s exit against England. Photograph: Álex Cruz/EPA

Riyad Mahrez (Algeria, 35)

Having made one appearance at the 2014 finals, Mahrez had to wait 12 years to add to his tally. He scored two goals against Austria before Algeria were eliminated in the last 32 by Switzerland in his final game. Mahrez said: “Representing Algeria has been a dream of mine ever since I was young, to play for my country. It’s been an immense honour and a great source of pride.” A Confederation of African Football’s statement said: “You gave us memories that time can never take away. Thank you, Riyad Mahrez.”

Enner Valencia (Ecuador, 36)

The forward got six goals in as many matches across the 2014 and 2022 finals but was unable to add to that tally for an Ecuador team who lost to Mexico in the last 32. “I’ve played my last match with the national team,” he said in the tunnel after. Ecuador’s official X account showed appreciation to their record scorer: “The GOAT. Super Enner. Thank you for giving yourself to the country and representing it in the best way.”

Nicolás Otamendi (Argentina, 38)

The uncompromising defender played every minute as Argentina triumphed in Qatar, having made his World Cup debut in 2010. Playing time was harder to come by in North America, though he featured in every game bar one, having revealed his intention to retire in March. “It’s my last World Cup, from there I’ll be a fan,” he said. Otamendi’s final home match became a tribute, with Lionel Messi letting him score a penalty at La Bombonera.

Marko Arnautovic (Austria, 37)

This was the striker’s first and last World Cup. He scored twice as Austria reached the last 32, where they were defeated 3–0 by Spain. Arnautovic revealed his departure in an emotional post-match interview, saying: “Playing for Austria was the biggest highlight. It hits me that from now on I won’t see my second family any more.” In a social media post, the Austrian Football Association said: “What a career. What a character. Thank you for everything.”

Sadio Mané (Senegal, 34)

Participated in 2018 but injury ruled him out four years later. Following Senegal’s capitulation against Belgium, Mané released a statement regarding retirement via Senegalese outlet Le Quotidien – although there have been questions about its authenticity – saying: “Know that I sacrificed everything for this flag. I gave the very best of myself and I always fought fiercely for our homeland.” Pape Thiaw was asked about Mané’s retirement in January and replied: “We want to keep him as long as possible … when we say it’s his decision, it doesn’t just belong to him, he belongs to the people of Senegal, and they want to see him carry on.”

View image in fullscreen Sadio Mané has called time on his international career with Senegal. Photograph: Jared C Tilton/FIFA/Getty Images

Craig Gordon (Scotland, 43)

The goalkeeper amassed 84 caps, making his debut in 2004, but did not get off the bench at his first World Cup. “I’ve never wanted it to end, but it must,” Gordon said, calling time on his club and international career. Gordon’s spell was described as “a career unlike any other” by the Scotland national team’s social media account.

Jean Michaël Seri (Côte d’Ivoire, 35)

Made his World Cup debut in his side’s 2–0 victory over Curaçao, his 64th cap. In a social media post, the former Fulham midfielder later said: “After 11 years in the national team, and one World Cup played, I announce the end of my international career today.” Seri received a wealth of tributes below his post. “Congratulations on all that you’ve accomplished with the national team,” replied the captain, Franck Kessié. “Thank you for all these moments shared under our colors.”

Neymar (Brazil, 34)

Announced himself on the World Cup stage with two goals on debut in 2014. Restricted by injury at the current tournament, he managed 55 minutes before Brazil’s exit against Norway and announced his international retirement shortly after full time. “It started here at MetLife Stadium,” he said, referring to his debut against the US in August 2010, “and I finished here. It is now over.” Zlatan Ibrahimovic, working as a pundit for US television, said: “An amazing player, and the skill set he had was just crazy. So, sad moment for Brazilian football.”

Sports.title: Spurs break their women’s transfer record to sign Alice Sombath from Lyonnes
Sports.content:
Tottenham have signed the France defender Alice Sombath from Lyonnes for a club record fee. The price paid for the 22-year-old has not been disclosed but the previous club record, paid for Signe Gaupset in January, was reportedly more than £375,000.

“The league is very competitive, every game is a tough game and that’s what I’m most excited about,” said Sombath. “I saw that Spurs had a very good season last year. My qualities can bring something to the team, even though I know they already have a lot.”

Sombath spent six years at Lyonnes, the eight-time European champions, joining the club after she was signed from Paris Saint-Germain in 2020.

She won the Champions League in her second season, featuring twice and being on the bench in the final, and won five league titles and two Coupe de France titles.

Tottenham’s head coach, Martin Ho, said the defender “fits the profile of what we’re building”. She has already shown real maturity in her performances and we believe she has all the qualities to continue developing into a top player within our environment.

“Alice is an aggressive defender who is comfortable in possession, competitive in her duels and has the ambition to keep improving every day. Those characteristics are really important to us and we’re excited to help her take the next step in her career while strengthening the squad.”

Sombath is Spurs’s sixth signing of the summer, after Shekiera Martinez, Kirsty Hanson, Victoria Pelova, Caitlin Dijkstra and Selma Panengstuen.

The club are delighted to have got these deals done early, allowing for a full pre-season, and that Sombath’s recruitment means they have secured the services of their six priority targets.

Sports.title: New Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa tipped to be sacked this season: ‘Could easily go wrong’
Sports.content:
New Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa tipped to be sacked this season: ‘Could easily go wrong’

Alvaro Arbeloa could fail to last a year in charge of Fulham - he arrives at Craven Cottage with huge pressure.

That's the view of ex-Aston Villa forward Gabby Agbonlahor, who believes the Spaniard has big shoes to fill having replaced Marco Silva.

2 Arbeloa won 18 of his 28 games at Real Madrid during his interim spell in the 2025/26 season Credit: Getty

Arbeloa was appointed by the Cottagers earlier this month on a three-year deal.

It's an immediate return to the dugout for the 43-year-old, who was replaced by Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid in June.

And it's also a move back to England for the 2010 World Cup winner, having enjoyed two separate stints playing in the Premier League.

A seven-year stretch at the Bernabeu was sandwiched between spells at Liverpool and West Ham, with the former right-back retiring after his ill-fated stay at the London Stadium.

But he is hoping for better days in the English capital this time around.

Managerial merry-go-round

Arbeloa is one of eight new managers brought in by Premier League clubs ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.

That is the most amount of changes made in a summer in Premier League history.

Enzo Maresca has taken over Manchester City, Liverpool have brought in Andoni Iraola, Chelsea moved for Xabi Alonso with Olivier Glasner switching to Nottingham Forest.

Elsewhere, Bournemouth have appointed Marco Rose, Crystal Palace now have Pierre Sage in charge with Gary O'Neil joining Ipswich.

But it is the future of Arbeloa that Agbonlahor is worrying about, as he commented on their depleted squad.

2 Arbeloa will be looking to guide Fulham to a top half finish for the first time since 2023 Credit: Getty

Fulham have already seen Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez depart as free agents, while defender Issa Diop is set to sign for Ipswich in an £8.5million deal.

Speaking on the talkSPORT Breakfast show, co-host Jeff Stelling commented on teams that have a new manager at the helm.

Interjecting, Agbonlahor then stated: "Arbeloa, there's pressure on him."

To which Stelling replied by saying: "There's big pressure on Arbeloa, that is a punt, isn't it?"

Agbonlahor continued: "That could easily go wrong we'll see won't we this season.

"We talk about Pep [Guardiola], what did he get out of then Man City players, can Maresca do it?

"What did Marco Silva get out of those players at Fulham?

"Diop's leaving, Wilson's gone, more players might leave Fulham.

"Don't be surprised if Arbeloa doesn't last a season."

Fulham's recent Premier League history

Since winning the Championship in the 2021/22 term, Fulham haven't finished below 13th in each of their last four seasons in the top-flight.

Silva guided the club to tenth spot in the 2022/23 campaign, with Fulham ending in 13th the next season, followed by two consecutive 11th-placed finishes.

Despite finishing outside the top ten in May, the Cottagers were just one point off a Conference League spot in eighth - and two behind a Europa League place in seventh.

Sports.title: Uncapped teenager tipped to earn England call-up and be big player for Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
Uncapped teenager tipped to earn England call-up and be big player for Thomas Tuchel

Fulham starlet Josh King has been backed to force his way into Thomas Tuchel's England plans.

Following the Three Lions' heartbreaking World Cup semi-final exit against Argentina, the conversation has already shifted onto who could star for the national team at future major tournaments.

5 Josh King became a regular fixture in Fulham's starting XI in the 2025/26 campaign Credit: Getty

England now have a two-year wait until their next shot at glory at Euro 2028, which will be hosted on home soil in the UK and Ireland.

Beyond this, there are of course four more years until Tuchel's side can avenge this summer's World Cup heartache, as Spain, Morocco and Portugal host the 2030 edition.

And the Three Lions could have a much-changed starting XI by the time either tournament rolls around, with a number of England's crop set to be well into their thirties by then.

Captain Harry Kane turns 33 this month, and will be nearly 37 in 2030, while key players John Stones and Jordan Pickford will both be 36.

Meanwhile, there is also potential for young players on the periphery of the England squad to stake their claim for a senior call-up, as they look to become key players at future major tournaments.

King of the options

talkSPORT pundit and Aston Villa legend Agbonlahor focused on the latter on Tuesday's Breakfast Show, and he believes Fulham midfielder King is among the top prospects here.

The 19-year-old enjoyed a breakthrough season last term, forcing his way into Marco Silva's starting XI to make 15 Premier League starts.

An England Under-21 international, King's impressive displays were rewarded in the summer, as he was then selected as one of five extra players travelling with the England squad to their pre-World Cup training camp.

Outlining King's qualities, Agbonlahor said: “Before the World Cup there were a few players that were part of the squad that didn't quite make it, but they were training with the squad.

“And one of the players that stands out for me - who I really, really enjoyed watching last season - was Josh King.

5 King is already known to England boss Tuchel after joining his team's training camp in Florida ahead of the World Cup Credit: Getty

“He's 19 years of age, made 32 appearances last season in the Premier League, but he only got one goal and two assists.

“Whenever I watched him play, and every time he got into that number 10 position, he always finds space - like top players do.

"The amount of times he received that ball in that position and created his own space, but maybe the end product, or it's a pass or it's a finish, wasn't at the level.

“But that's what you expect of a 19-year-old. It's a big season for him and I just loved watching him."

Agbonlahor then insisted that Tuchel will no doubt be keeping tabs on the youngster going forward, who he believes could add to England's existing quality in attacking areas.

He added: "He's one that I'm sure Thomas Tuchel will have his eye on - very good player.”

“He kept Emile Smith-Rowe - who’s a talented player - on the bench most of the season, and forced himself into Marco Silva's plans.”

5 King has been capped six times by England at Under-21 level, scoring once Credit: Getty

He will now have a new manager to impress in Alvaro Arbeloa, who replaced Silva this summer.

'What we need'

It wasn't just King who Agbonlahor tipped to break into the England squad in the near future.

He also named Liverpool starlet Rio Ngumoha and Arsenal teenage duo Ethan Nwaneri and Max Dowman as those who should be targeting call-ups.

Alongside King, Ngumoha and Nwaneri was also selected among the Three Lions training players at their pre-World Cup camp, with the former dazzling on his international debut in a friendly win over New Zealand.

On Ngumoha, Agbonlahor began: “Put him in, 100 per cent, and I feel like someone like Noni Madueke who didn't perform [at the World Cup], if you look at Nwaneri, look at Dowman [instead].

“I mean Nwaneri is 19 years of age, went on loan to Marseille - maybe it didn't work out as well as he thought it would be.

“It's a massive season for 16-year-old Max Dowman. These players are going to be so hungry to play. Go out there and play their football and break into Thomas Tuchel's ideas.

5 Aged just 17, Rio Ngumoha impressed off the bench in England's pre-World Cup friendly against New Zealand, which was his senior debut Credit: Getty

5 Max Dowman has followed in Ethan Nwaneri's footsteps by becoming a first-team regular at Arsenal whilst still a teenager Credit: Getty

“Rio Ngumoha? I think he will get a lot more game time under Andoni Iraola [at Liverpool].

"I love the way he plays. Direct, doesn't care, will get the ball and go at you again. Relentless, that's what we need."

England are next in action against World Cup winners Spain on September 26 in a Nations League clash.

During the extended international break across September and October, Tuchel's side will also face Czech Republic twice and Croatia.

Sports.title: UEFA tipped to ‘soft launch’ World Cup feature that football fans hate
Sports.content:
Former England goalkeeper Ben Foster fears hydration breaks will slowly make their way into the Premier League and Champions League.

FIFA's decision to introduce three-minute breaks midway through each half of the World Cup faced heavy backlash from football fans.



3 Multiple professionals of the game called out how hydration breaks can affect a match Credit: AFP

The interruptions caused a disruption to the momentum of matches and were criticised by both coaches and players alike.

"I don’t like it. I only like it when the conditions are extreme. But when the conditions are good, it is unnecessary," said USMNT boss Mauricio Pochettino.

TV broadcasters in America capitalised on the breaks and used them as prime advertising space.



On average, a 30-second World Cup commercial slot on Fox Sports costs between $200,000 and $300,000 (£150,000-£224,000), with prices soaring to around $750,000 (£560,000) during the final stages of the tournament.

Additionally, the final featured a Super Bowl-style half-time show on Sunday night, causing FIFA to breach the Laws of the Game.



The interval during the biggest game in world football was stretched to 27 minutes, exceeding the maximum 15 allowed.

'Halves are not even 45 minutes'

Foster, who played more than 550 professional games for club and country, spoke exclusively on talkSPORT Drive on how the stoppage in play affects the athletes' physical condition.



He said: "If you’re an older player it does, if you’re about 32 onwards [it will affect you].

"I would like to think they have bikes in the changing room because they will have to get moving pretty quick, because you can stiffen up so quickly."

He added: "The halves are not even 45 minutes anymore, they’re quarters. It would not surprise me if these hydration breaks crept into the Premier League.

"It would not surprise me one little bit. Where there’s money to be made, there’s a way. They will find a reason to justify it."



3 A report claim Europe's top leagues could consider hydration breaks in the future Credit: AFP

Commercial changes

Beyond the extended half-time entertainment, FIFA's hydration breaks - which were deployed even in climate-controlled venues - have effectively split football matches into four distinct segments.

Foster believes the shift is entirely driven by money and warned that domestic leagues, including the Premier League, could be next.

Fans are left feeling powerless as the traditions of the sport are altered for commercial gain.



Reflecting on how football's governing bodies push through major structural changes despite widespread fan disapproval, Foster pointed to the implementation of VAR as the ultimate blueprint.

He said: "There’s nothing we can do as football fans to stop it, they introduced VAR and every single one of us hates it.

"I could do away with VAR tomorrow, but they won’t now because they invested so much money into it.

3 The integrity of the World Cup has been called into question Credit: Getty



"They will do a soft launch in the Champions League, for example, you watch. Clubs will say ‘oh we get an extra million quid'."

The former Manchester United goalkeeper added: "Teams have been approaching games differently because it’s in quarters, so you can break it down into the four parts. But I hate it."

UEFA has already ruled out similar measures, and European football managers have admitted to disliking the stoppages.

England manager Thomas Tuchel previously stated that they 'interrupt and change the identity of a football match'.



Rules continued to be broken

FIFA has been under intense scrutiny throughout the World Cup, facing major controversies on and off the pitch.

USA striker Folarin Balogun had his red card suspended, with President Donald Trump admitting to calling FIFA chief Gianni Infantino and asking him to review the decision.

Throughout the tournament, ticket prices soared and allocation for the final soared up to $2.3million (£1.7million).

Additionally, there was a politicisation of the international competition, with supporters of several nations unable to enter the country due to US immigration travel bans.



This included Somali referee Omar Artan, who was refused entry at Miami Airport.

Sports.title: Aston Villa urged to sign England U21 star who was sold by Roberto De Zerbi
Sports.content:
Aston Villa urged to sign England U21 star who was sold by Roberto De Zerbi

Jonathan Rowe is the exact sort of player Aston Villa should be signing - he's got that spice to him that Unai Emery can handle.

That is the verdict of Villa legend Gabby Agbonlahor, who was wowed by the Bologna winger's performance against his old club last season.

4 Rowe ripped Villa defender Matty Cash 'to shreds' when the two sides faced off in the Europa League Credit: Getty

The 23-year-old could be on his way to English football after a topsy-turvy two-season spell in France and now Italy.

Rowe scored the winning goal for the Young Lions in England's Under-21 Euros final win last summer after completing a permanent move to Marseille following a successful loan the year before.

However, the attacker was told to find a new club by now-Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi after a furious bust-up with Adrien Rabiot.

Rowe made the move to Bologna in Italy, but now could be on the move again despite managing just three goals in 28 Serie A games.

The former Norwich City starlet was a rare shining light for his side in their run to the Europa League quarter-finals last season.

Rowe scored Bologna's only goal across their 7-1 aggregate defeat to eventual tournament winners Villa, who are now hoping to sign him.

And talkSPORT Breakfast presenter Agbonlahor believes he fits the bill, with his old side set to lose £117million Morgan Rogers to Chelsea.

Jonathan Rowe to Aston Villa

On Rowe, talkSPORT's Jeff Stelling said: " Reports are that Chelsea and Villa are interested, which could boost his chances of eventually getting in the England squad.

"We're going to be looking for a number nine. He doesn't score a lot of goals, hasn't scored a lot of goals in Italy.

"But I remember his performances for the England under-21s when he won the Euros, and he was absolutely exceptional."

4 Rowe gave Villa fans a potential taste of what they could expect from him next season Credit: AFP

'A player that I want Aston Villa to get'

Agbonlahor said: "I watched him in the games against Aston Villa, and Matty Cash is a top defender, but he ripped him, ripped him up, Jeff.

"He was direct, stop-start, quick, very sharp. He's a player that I really want Aston Villa to go and get.

"If you look at his appearances last season, he could score more goals, Jeff, only three goals in 28 league games and only four goals in 12 Europa League games.

"Has he got to produce more output in goals and assists? Yes, he does, but if there's a manager to get it out of him, it's Unai Emery.

"If I had my perfect world, I'd love Rowe and [Crysencio] Summerville. Aston Villa need wingers, and I think he fits that bill."

4 Rowe scored the winner to help England claim a fourth U21 Euros title in June 2025 Credit: Getty

4 Rabiot (far left) and Rowe (third from right) were both sold by Marseille after their bust-up Credit: AFP

Rowe has proven he's still got a bit of the red mist that led to his Marseille exit by getting a red card in a friendly match last week.

Bologna's No.11 was sent off for shoving Stefano Russo to the ground after a stiff challenge in a 4-0 pre-season defeat to Arminia Bielefeld.

Agbonlahor added: "[Age] 23, but what he has got, Jeff, he's got that spark to him that maybe some managers will have to calm him down.

"He had the fight with Rabiot at Marseille, and both of them got sold by De Zerbi.

"I had just seen a clip last week of a preseason friendly, and he got caught by a defender, and he ran over, pushed the defender over, [and] had to walk off the pitch in anger.

"So he's got that spice to him that maybe a manager like Unai Emery can calm him down.

"But top, top winger and I'm sure clubs will be looking at him."

Sports.title: Chelsea must let Enzo Fernandez go or risk PR disaster after embarrassing World Cup antics
Sports.content:
Chelsea must let Enzo Fernandez go or risk PR disaster after embarrassing World Cup antics

Argentina did exceptionally well to humiliate themselves during their World Cup defeat to Spain - and that's putting it lightly.

Not only were they outplayed, lacking attacking quality and only able to avoid a thrashing thanks to goalkeeper Emi Martinez, they showcased how not to react to a loss with some senseless thuggery.

5 Argentina were the opposite of gracious in defeat at the World Cup final Credit: Getty

Leandro Paredes was sent off for assaulting Spanish players as they celebrated at full-time, and Nahuel Molina attempted to punch Rodri.

A mass brawl ensued but Spain, who admirably took the moral high ground and didn't stoop to the level of their opponents or let the ugly scenes ruin their second-ever World Cup trophy lift.

The post-match chaos was preceded by a series of calls from referee Slavko Vincic that did little to quash any conspiracies of Argentina having preferential treatment throughout the tournament.

However, alongside manager Lionel Scaloni, they did in fact have five players booked, with Enzo Fernandez going as far as to see yellow on two occasions before being given his marching orders.

Fernandez first went into the book for dissent as he shouted at Vincic after going down far too easily, and was lucky not to pick up another seconds later for seemingly responding with a sarcastic clap.

But it was a moment of madness during four minutes of stoppage time where the 25-year-old made it very clear that he lost all composure, much to the detriment of his country.

Chasing down a loose ball, he clattered into Pau Cubarsi with enough momentum to send him flying and onto the turf in a heap.

Vincic did not hesitate to show him a second yellow and red card, but Fernandez still had the audacity to protest the decision.

Argentina spent extra time with ten men and lost the World Cup final, before resorting to violence at full-time and behaving like spoiled brats by turning their backs to Spain's presentation.

England fans could not help but revel in what they considered to be 'karma' after Fernandez's antics during the Three Lions' semi-final defeat.

Fernandez statement after World Cup defeat Posting on Instagram, he said: "As time goes by, you realize there is something much bigger than just a result. "For years, this group has represented the team in the best possible way. It teaches that competing isn't just about winning; it’s about giving your all for the jersey and never giving up. "It has been a privilege to be part of a group that always stepped up, competed at the highest level, and defended these colors with pride, humility, and commitment. "I want to thank all the Argentine fans. Thank you for always being there, for supporting us in every match, for the affection, for the unconditional support, and for making us feel at home anywhere in the world. "Wearing my country's jersey is the greatest honor of my career, and I will continue to give my all every time I get to defend it."

5 Fernandez's goal against England was met with a prolonged celebration Credit: Getty

After a cringeworthy celebration, the midfielder took to Instagram laughing with his teammates as 'Wonderwall' - England's impromptu World Cup anthem - played.

There is every chance a minority of Chelsea fans boo Fernandez when he plays his next game at Stamford Bridge - especially given the reaction to a tone-deaf social media post from the Blues during the World Cup.

Chelsea were forced to delete a post celebrating Fernandez's equaliser against England after fierce backlash - and they might be wise to avoid another PR disaster by letting him go.

With the dust now settling, Fernandez will likely head on a break and recuperate before preparing for another season at Chelsea, although he seems desperate to leave.

London no longer calling

It was at the 2022 World Cup where Fernandez dazzled with Argentina in their tournament triumph and won the Young Player Award at 21-years-old.

The midfielder became hot property and, after a drawn out transfer saga with his then-employers Benfica, Chelsea spent £106.8million and completed a British record move in February 2023.

5 Fernandez had a day to forget with his red card Credit: Getty

Fernandez has since made 169 appearances for the Blues, and been part of their Club World Cup and Conference League successes across three-and-a-half seasons in west London.

He has worn the armband on various occasions, but it is apparent that his mind is elsewhere ahead of the new campaign.

During the March international break, Fernandez said that he 'really likes Madrid' and that the Spanish capital is 'similar to Buenos Aires', which is where he was born.

This sparked speculation over a summer move to Real Madrid and he was given a two-match suspension by Chelsea, who are understood to be demanding £120m for his signature.

Madrid have stated that they have no intention of signing him, and Fernandez insisted that any talks over his Chelsea future could wait until the World Cup has concluded.

Now that the tournament is over, speculation over where he will be playing next season is only set to increase.

5 Fernandez has not kept quiet on his liking for Madrid

Fernandez would love to join Madrid but, even though Jose Mourinho appreciates the player, they have not yet made formal contact with Chelsea over a move.

talkSPORT also understands that Chelsea would like him to stay and sign a new deal at the club, with his current deal running until 2032.

However, given his desire to move to Madrid and a lack of discipline in front of billions, the club world champions should consider cashing in.

It would be detrimental to the squad under new manager Xabi Alonso to keep a player who has made it clear that he could envisage himself elsewhere.

Yes, Fernandez has been one of Chelsea's top players since signing and produced some key moments, including the equaliser against Real Betis in the Conference League final last year.

Alonso also wants to keep him but if a fee in the region of £120m is attainable, then it would be silly not to sell.

5 Maybe it's time for Chelsea to let one of their statement signings leave Credit: Getty

Whether or not Chelsea would be able to find a suitable replacement is another matter although judging by their summer business so far, they would be willing to spend.

Morgan Rogers is joining from Aston Villa for a British record fee of £117m, they have held talks with Crystal Palace for the £55m-rated Maxence Lacroix, and Marco Palestra joined from Atalanta for £47m.

Chelsea have also generated over £100m in income with the sales of Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Tyrique George, with the £65m-valued Nicolas Jackson also a potential departee.

Moises Caicedo, Romeo Lavia and Dario Essugo would remain as the midfield options if Fernandez was to leave, so a new face would need to come in for squad depth.

But, if Fernandez feels as though he's ready for a new chapter in his career elsewhere, Chelsea should amicably show him the exit door.

Sports.title: World Cup winner ‘sad’ Mexico and Canada were overshadowed by USA – ‘No empathy for them’
Sports.content:
This summer's World Cup was highly commercialised, and Emmanuel Petit believes FIFA is killing the tradition and culture of the sport

World Cup winner ‘sad’ Mexico and Canada were overshadowed by USA – ‘No empathy for them’

World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit believes the United States overshadowed co-hosts Canada and Mexico during the 2026 tournament, and has again expressed worry about the Americanisation of football.

Games took place across 16 cities this summer, with three hosts in Mexico, and two in Canada.

6 Canada and Mexico were overshadowed as World Cup co-hosts, Petit believes Credit: Getty

While the opening fixture unfolded at the historic Azteca Stadium, and Canada played all three of their group games on home turf, matches from the quarterfinals onwards took place solely in the US which had 11 host cities.

The World Cup final, won by Spain over Argentina, was played at MetLife Stadium, a venue on the outskirts of New York which has long been criticised by fans.

With the curtain now drawn, Petit -- who lifted the famous trophy with France in 1998 -- doubled down on his criticism of how the tournament was Americanised, having feared the worst earlier this year.

The former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder told talkSPORT he felt Canada and Mexico had been overshadowed by the madness of a US-centric tournament that debuted much-criticized hydration breaks and an extended half-time show.

Emmanuel Petit hits out at Americanisation of football

"I was sad for Canada and Mexico. Because there was no empathy for them, no messages for them," he told Alex Brooker on the How To Win The World Cup podcast.

"It's like the whole competition was organized in America. You take away everything else. It's always America, America, America, all the time.

"FIFA tried during the whole competition to make soccer an American sport. And I really hate it.

"I hope for the next World Cup, we won't get the cooling breaks anymore. I hope we won't get a 30-minute break during half-time to see this pathetic show.

"For me, it was pathetic. Even those famous people on the pitch, they were not convinced at all of what they were doing. We could see that from outside.

"They tried their best to make the show on the pitch. But come on, this is not the Super Bowl. This is football. So stick with it, keep our tradition and get away from this horrible thing."

6 World Cup winner Petit claims Canada and Mexico were overshadowed by Americanisation of the tournament Credit: AFP

6 He believes the World Cup doesn't need a half-time show like the Super Bowl Credit: AFP

Petit added he was 'worried' for the future of the competition, and noted that England using the Oasis hit Wonderful to celebrate with fans after games was a factor in taking the focus off the sport itself.

FIFA losing 'tradition and culture' of World Cup

Each nation was given a specific goal anthem by FIFA, as well as celebration tracks played after the final whistle.

Petit continued: "I love music… I know that the show is very important, but I think it's going too far, honestly.

"Maybe I'm too old, maybe I'm old-fashioned.

"But the way FIFA is managing the competition now, I'm worried for the future, to be honest with you.

"It's going to lose some tradition, the culture. I think the football I lived in the past, there is no comparison with what's happening actually.

6 England players and fans celebrated to Wonderwall after World Cup wins Credit: Getty

6 Petit believes the World Cup has lost its tradition this year Credit: AFP

"I know that football has to evolve over time, music, everything. But as I said, I think it's going too far. We should come back to where we were sometimes before.

"We should focus only on football, nothing else."

Petit concluded that hydration breaks throughout the tournament, and a half-time show in the final, was 'pathetic' to watch and further illustrates the suggestion that FIFA cares more about making money that protecting players.

"I was thinking yesterday, the half-time break, 30 minutes, the cooling break, the extra time. Can you imagine how long the players stayed on the pitch yesterday for the World Cup final?" he asked.

6 Petit also took aim at the introduction of hydration breaks Credit: AFP

"Do you protect football when you do that? No. Do you only think about money? Yes.

"Do you care about the image of football in the world? Because fans in a stadium, they have a different view on what's going on when they are present.

"But from outside, sometimes I had the feeling it was pathetic to watch."

Sports.title: A feast fit for a (Vi)king! Erling Haaland shows off huge birthday meal on holiday with girlfriend Isabel - as he gears up for Premier League return after Norway's World Cup campaign
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland celebrated turning 26 in style on Tuesday as he showed off his huge birthday feast while holidaying after the World Cup.

The Manchester City star played a key role for Norway at this summer's tournament in the United States, Canada and Mexico, steering his country to their best ever World Cup finish before suffering defeat against England in the quarter-finals.

Haaland, aware that the new Premier League season is only a few weeks away, has opted to take a much-needed holiday after the World Cup, enjoying a relaxing getaway on the waves with his girlfriend Isabel Haugseng Johansen in Sardinia.

Reposting a picture shared to Isabel's Instagram on Tuesday, the birthday boy showed off the incredible feast he was about to tuck into as he celebrated turning 26.

Showing views of the ocean's waves in the background, the photo displayed a table boasting huge portions of barbecued meat on the bone, a mountain of sausages, pancakes, eggs, bagels, fruit and a tower of various cakes and pastries.

He then later posted an image of him relaxing on the waves while wearing a Viking helmet, posting on X: '26 years. Nice.'

Erling Haaland showed off his birthday feast on Tuesday while holidaying after the World Cup

Haaland then posted a picture of himself wearing a Viking helmet on his summer holiday

The Manchester City star pictured with his girlfriend Isabel Haugseng Johansen on Instagram

Haaland is renowned for having one of the most extreme diets in the Premier League, averaging a remarkable 6,000 calories per day to keep up his monstrous physique.

Cow hearts and livers can often be found on the City star's menu, as referenced in Haaland: The Big Decision - the documentary made around his £51m move to the Etihad in 2022.

'You other people don't eat this (heart and liver), but I am concerned with taking care of my body,' Haaland explained in the documentary. 'I think eating quality food that is as local as possible is the most important.

'Or the local cow eating grass right over there? I eat the heart and the liver.'

Regular items on his shopping list - as shown on his access-all-areas YouTube channel - also include gigantic barbecue steaks, raw honey, and milk, lots of milk. Haaland loves the stuff, especially raw milk, and he once described it as his 'magic potion'.

The Norwegian loves pairing his milk with a breakfast of eggs on sourdough and a cup of coffee with maple syrup at his six-bedroom mansion in Alderley Edge, Cheshire, which he shares with Isabel.

During the video, Haaland also showcased his love for fish. He ate a lunch of sea bass, asparagus, and egg fried rice before joining his team-mates on the pitch at the Etihad campus.

The upcoming 2026-27 season will mark Haaland's first season at the Etihad without Pep Guardiola, who decided to call time on his glittering Manchester City career at the end of last campaign.

Haaland's remarkable physique is maintained with a crazy 6,000-calorie-per-day diet

There's also plenty of milk in Haaland's diet, which he has called his 'magic potion' for success

Guardiola's former assistant Enzo Maresca, who parted ways with Chelsea in January, has taken over at the Etihad and will undoubtedly lean on Haaland's prowess in front of goal as he bids to win City a ninth Premier League title.

Since arriving in Manchester, Haaland has scored a staggering 162 goals in 198 games across all competitions, winning two Premier League titles, a Champions League, two FA Cups and a League Cup during that time.

Sports.title: Argentina star praised for defying his team-mates and watching Spain's World Cup trophy lift - amid heavy criticism of national team's disgraceful post-match conduct
Sports.content:
Argentina star Jose Manuel 'Flaco' Lopez has won plaudits for appearing to be the only player to acknowledge Spain's World Cup trophy lift after suffering a 1-0 defeat on Sunday.

The Albiceleste were unable to retain the trophy after their barnstorming victory in 2022 and instead reacted poorly, with many of the players refusing to acknowledge Spain's win.

The team was captured turning their backs on captain Rodri accepting the trophy in a gesture widely deemed bitter by international spectators.

But for Lopez, who plays for Brazilian side Palmeiras, the decision to watch the ceremony unfold and Spain lift the trophy after gaining their second star has seen him singled out as an example to his team-mates.

'To face your defeat head-on, that is what it truly means to be an honourable person,' one commenter said on social media.

Another added: 'Showed character. Congratulations!'

Jose Manuel 'Flaco' Lopez was the only Argentina player to watch Spain lift the World Cup

The Palmeiras star was singled out as an example to his team-mates, many of whom turned their backs on Spain

A third suggested: 'Flaco Lopez all alone showing more class than the entire squad. The others had already vanished before the anthem even started playing.'

'The only one who respects football and his country by not letting them be made a laughingstock,' one social media user said.

Argentina were outplayed in New York after forcing extra time against Luis de la Fuente's side, with Ferran Torres finally grabbing the only goal of the game in the second-half of extra time.

When the final whistle blew, tensions bubbled over, with Leandro Paredes one of Argentina stars embroiled in physical violence, lashing out at Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground.

FIFA have since opened an investigation into Argentina's full-time confrontation, with the roles of other players and officials also set to be scrutinised.

Nahuel Molina hit Rodri in the torso as he was running by, resulting in the midfielder squaring up to his rival.

That saw players from both teams pile into the melee, before Paredes threw punches.

Elsewhere, 53-year-old assistant coach Roberto Ayala was also caught landing a punch on Spain's Dani Olmo at full time.

In the aftermath of the ugly brawl, DAZN Spain claimed Argentina defender Nicolas Otamendi complained to Rodri about La Roja's pre-match comments alluding to officiating concerns ahead of the final.

As well as turning their backs on their opponents some Argentineans descended into violence after the final whistle

The South Americans had benefitted from a series of questionable decisions heading into the showpiece event, with the Manchester City midfielder raising concerns before the final.

'You and (Spain team-mate Aymeric) Laporte. Both of you,' Otamendi said to Rodri.

'You spent the time crying and complaining about the referees, my friend. But you shouldn't have spoken before the match, you know that? Didn't you see what he said this week?'

Argentina's post-match conduct had earlier come under scrutiny in their semi-final against England, when unused substitute Valentin Barco celebrated Enzo Fernandez's equaliser by running towards the Three Lions' backline rather than joining his team-mates.

Barco is later thought to have said something in the direction of Jude Bellingham which prompted the Real Madrid star to smack him on the back of his head.

The Argentine national team later unfurled a banner repeating Argentina's claim to the Falkland Islands, which has also seen FIFA open an investigation into their breach of the tournament's rules around political messaging.

Sports.title: Nicolas Jackson is keen on reuniting with Unai Emery at Aston Villa as Man United, Arsenal and Chelsea target Alex Scott turns down new Bournemouth deal: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Spurs agree to sell Lankshear to Middlesbrough

Tottenham have agreed to sell Will Lankshear to Middlesbrough for £14million potentially rising to £20m with add-ons.

There is also a 20 per cent sell on clause and Spurs have matching rights on any bids from other clubs in the future.

Striker Lankshear, 21, who was on loan at Oxford United last season, is expected for a medical later today.

Nicolas Jackson interested in Aston Villa move

Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson is interested in his potential switch to Aston Villa to work with his former head coach Unai Emery again.

Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson is interested in his potential switch to Aston Villa

Jackson's name came up during conversations between Chelsea and Villa centred on Morgan Rogers, who is set to move to Stamford Bridge for a club-record £117million and sign a six-year deal with the option of an extra year.

Villa have long been admirers of Jackson under Emery, who had the striker at Villarreal. Chelsea have been taking their time to decide on the 25-year-old Senegal international's future.

With Jackson, Liam Delap, Emmanuel Emegha, Marc Guiu and Joao Pedro as Xabi Alonso's striker options currently, there is an acceptance inside of Chelsea that they need to reduce their numbers, especially while facing a season out of Europe.

Joao Pedro is considered untouchable and so not for sale. Delap is keen to have another season to prove himself after a disappointing campaign following his move from Ipswich, while Emegha has only just arrived this summer from their sister side Strasbourg. Guiu is expected to leave either permanently or on loan.

There remains a market for Jackson, who spent the last season on loan at Bayern Munich. Chelsea are believed to value him at £65m.

That is down on the £80m they were understood to be seeking last summer before sanctioning his temporary switch to Bayern. That came at a time when the relationship between Jackson and then-manager Enzo Maresca had broken down.

Chelsea's plan for Jackson was to have him return in pre-season so that Xabi Alonso could take a closer look at the scorer. Alonso said at his unveiling last week that Jackson was due to join them on their tour of Australia and Asia after his post-World Cup break.

However, sources close to Jackson have told Daily Mail Sport that they are seriously considering Villa as an option after his name was discussed during talks about Rogers. Alejandro Garnacho has also been linked with Villa, but the Argentinian is said to be prioritising a move to Italy.

KIERAN GILL

West Ham mulling over Roma's Summerville bid

Roma are awaiting a reply from West Ham on their latest efforts to sign winger Crysencio Summerville.

As reported yesterday, Roma's latest bid of £39million plus add ons is a marginal increase and restructure on their second bid which was rejected.

Aston Villa have also been monitoring developments on the 24-year-old.

Roma are awaiting a reply from West Ham on their latest efforts to sign Crysencio Summerville

West Ham have enquired about Cardiff defender Dylan Lawlor.

Ipswich seal deal for new goalkeeper

Ipswich have completed the signing of goalkeeper Kayne van Oevelen from Volendam.

The fee is £4.25m with an initial £3.4m followed by £850,000 in add-ons.

The 22-year-old, who is seen as one for the future, has signed until 2031.

Ipswich have had a bid rejected for another goalkeeper, Kjell Scherpen from Union Saint-Gilloise.

As reported on Window Watch yesterday, Ipswich are close to sealing a £20m deal for Leicester City winger Abdul Fatawu with a further £3m in add-ons.

Ipswich are overhauling their goalkeeping department and discussing an £8.5m deal for Fulham's Issa Diop (right)

They are discussing an £8.5m deal for Fulham's Issa Diop and are negotiating with Celtic for versatile forward Daizen Maeda and free agent midfielder Hidemasa Morita who is leaving Sporting Lisbon and had been close to joining Leeds United.

PFA free agent squad in action tonight

Former Crystal Palace midfielder Jonny Williams and Egypt international Samy Morsy are in the PFA free agent squad of 21 to face Hednesford Town at Key's Park Stadium at 7.45 pm tonight.

Former Crystal Palace midfielder Jonny Williams and Egypt international Samy Morsy are in the PFA free agent squad of 21 to face Hednesford Town at Key's Park Stadium at 7.45 pm tonight.

Around 48 players have now joined the PFA pre-season camp where they train and play a series of friendlies to showcase their availability to clubs over the summer.

Former Manchester United and Port Vale keeper Ben Amos and ex-Ipswich Town striker Connor Wickham are among a growing band of players looking to earn contracts elsewhere.

Another friendly is planned at Tranmere Rovers on Friday.

The games can be viewed on the PFA's live YouTube stream.

QPR snap up Lamptey

Former Chelsea and Brighton full-back Tariq Lamptey has joined QPR on a permanent deal.

The 25-year-old has signed on a free transfer after leaving Serie A side Fiorentina.

Lamptey said: 'I like to get up and down, a lot of energy, a lot of fun. Hopefully I'll keep the fans on the edge of their seats.

Former Chelsea and Brighton full-back Tariq Lamptey has joined QPR on a permanent deal

'I'm tough tackling, I love one-v-ones, defensive and attacking, I just love playing the game.'

Lamptey's Fiorentina contract was terminated by mutual consent in May after the full-back ruptured his cruciate just three weeks after joining the Italian side from Brighton.

Fiorentina paid £6m for the Ghanaian.

Sheffield United weigh up Matondo move

Sheffield United are continuing to evaluate winger Rabbi Matondo who has impressed during their training camp in Valencia.

The Wales international, who is free to leave SK Brann, is due to play in a behind closed doors friendly against Huddersfield Town today.

Matondo figured in the Blades friendly against Levante last week and Chris Wilder is expected to make a decision this week with the likes of Derby County and Middlesbrough also showing interest.

Sheffield United are weighing up a move for Wales international Rabbi Matondo

Sheffield Wednesday close in on TENTH summer signing

Aston Villa forward Tommi O'Reilly is poised to become Sheffield Wednesday's 10th summer signing.

The 22-year-old, who impressed on loan at Crewe in League Two last season, is due to sign on loan again at Wednesday.

The Owls' young goalkeeper Logan Stretch, 19, has been loaned out to National League North side Buxton, who are managed by former Wednesday youth coach Jordan Broadbent.

Man City teenager joins Northampton

Manchester City striker Matty Warhurst has joined Northampton Town.

The prolific 19-year-old was keen to leave for first team football and had interest from a host of clubs in League One and League Two including Stockport County, Cambridge United, Leyton Orient and Swindon Town.

Warhurst, who turns 20 in September, has scored 61 goals in 97 games for various City sides in the last few seasons, including 36 goals in 41 games for the under-18s before adding 13 goals in 18 Premier League 2 appearances and eight goals in 11 FA Youth Cup games.

Alex Scott turns down new Bournemouth deal

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has turned down a new contract.

Scott has two years remaining on his current deal and was offered fresh terms by the Cherries in March this year.

Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United all hold an interest in the 22-year-old, but Bournemouth's stance is that he is not for sale this summer - regardless of his contract situation.

Daily Mail Sport understands Bournemouth have not put a price or valuation on the Under-21 European Championship winner as they do not consider him for sale.

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has turned down a new contract at the club

Just last week, new Cherries boss Marco Rose told the media he was confident that in-demand Scott and Junior Kroupi would remain on the South Coast for their Europa League campaign.

Bournemouth's policy this summer is to keep hold of their best players for Europe - including Scott, Kroupi and winger Rayan - but it remains to be seen if substantial offers would test their resolve.

Scott played 39 times for Bournemouth last season and was key to securing European football for the first time in the club's history.

Thomas Tuchel awarded Scott his first international call-up last November, although he did not earn a cap.

The midfielder also travelled to the United States with the Three Lions before the World Cup to take part in their tournament preparation camp.

Even if Bournemouth could be persuaded to do business over Scott, it's understood that United would have to sell players to afford the £80m it would be likely to cost to prise him away from the Vitality Stadium.

The club want to sell top-earner Marcus Rashford following his loan spells at Barcelona and Aston Villa, and would listen to offers for Joshua Zirkzee. Manuel Ugarte would also have been available, but the Uruguay midfielder sustained a serious knee injury at the World Cup and will spend much of next season recuperating at Carrington.

As it stands, United will struggle to sign Scott and Roma midfielder Manu Kone appears to be a more realistic option after United held talks with the Frenchman's camp.
