Sports.title: THE ANALYST - Alex Scott: Why Man United and Arsenal are battling for £80m 'diamond' who's refused to sign new Bournemouth deal - how he dominates midfield despite slight frame, the attributes that wowed Mikel Arteta and United's advantage in race
Sports.content:
When it comes to recruitment at the highest level of the game, it is often the intangibles that set players apart. Is he a good trainer? What happens when he is left out? Does he get on well with team-mates? Can he listen and take on board tactical information? How does he manage disappointment? And can he handle pressure? In the case of Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, who has turned down a new contract offer from the club, it’s his intangibles report card, just as much as his passing, dribbling and all-action play on the pitch, that has Manchester United, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur circling with intent this summer, with the player valued around £80million. ‘He’s an absolute diamond off the pitch. He’s really, really good and he's one that you'd just want around the group,’ Ian Foster, who managed Scott with England Under 19s and Under 20s, tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘He's such a good kid, and I think he's still under the radar for me.’ Brian Tinnion chuckles when those comments are put to him. When he was Bristol City technical director he brought Scott to Ashton Gate from Guernsey FC, who play in the Isthmian League. ‘The best thing about him is his attitude,’ Tinnion explains. ‘His attitude to play, the attitude to training, and he was never one bit of bother from the minute he walked in the building until the minute we sold him to Bournemouth. He was the absolute dream young person to work with.’ Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is being chased by Arsenal, Manchester United and Tottenham this summer The former Bristol City man is now valued at around £80million The intangibles weren’t always enough, however, and more concrete hurdles almost killed Scott’s career. His lack of height and physicality as a youngster saw Southampton cast him aside. He had a year at Bournemouth, fell out of love with the game and went back home to Guernsey, where he became their youngest ever player. He decided to take one last swing at making it in England, with a trial at Bristol City. This was likely his last chance, and he had to take it. ‘We organised a friendly game for him against a London academy who wanted to play us,’ Tinnion says. ‘So Alex came across for the week and he scored a perfect hat-trick in 35 minutes – left foot, right foot, header. I'm like, “Wow, who's this lad?”. We'd seen and watched him, but watching him close up like this, he was outstanding.’ He rose to the occasion with England, too. It was Scott’s header, coming off the bench in a semi-final against Italy, that kept the Young Lions on their path to winning the Under 19s Euros in 2022. And it was Scott who started alongside Elliot Anderson in last summer’s Under 21s Euros final, helping to throw Germany completely off their game. So, to answer the questions posed earlier: Is he a good trainer? Among the very best. What happens when he is left out? He often changes games at the highest level from the bench. Does he get on well with team-mates? Nobody has a bad word to say about him. Can he listen and take on board tactical information? Managers spoken to for this piece insist he can take on the most detailed of briefs. What about handling disappointment? Well, after joining Bournemouth in 2023 for £25m, a knee injury restricted him to three games, then a year later he tore his meniscus. He broke his jaw on the eve of the Under 21s Euros, and came off injured and in tears in the final. He bounced back in the season just gone to get Bournemouth into Europe. And though he didn’t quite make this summer’s World Cup squad, he was on Thomas Tuchel’s radar enough to join the Florida training camp. And can he handle pressure? Without any hesitation, yes. Scott and Elliot Anderson, who has completed a £116m move to Man City, were a superb pair in England's Under 21s Euros win last year Scott (left) has impressed Thomas Tuchel to the point he was called up to England's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida Now to Scott’s appeal on the pitch. His versatility makes him an attractive target to many of the game’s elite clubs. Having first been deployed as a wing-back by Bristol City, Scott has moved inside, playing as a deeper-lying No 6, a box-to-box No 8, and an attack-minded No 10 just behind a striker. Where Manchester United are targeting a rhythm-setting defensive midfielder to complement Kobbie Mainoo and Bruno Fernandes, Arsenal are seeking ball-carriers to help get them up the pitch quicker in transition. Deceptively strong, Scott showed last season what an impressive driver of the ball he is, with 21 per cent of his carries deemed to be progressive – stats providers define this as taking the ball at least five metres closer to the opposition goal. That was the fourth-highest mark of any defensive midfielder in Europe’s top five leagues last season. Under Andoni Iraola at Bournemouth and Lee Carsley with England Under 21s, Scott has more recently been tasked with a deeper role, working as a rhythm disruptor. He did that to great effect, particularly alongside Anderson, one of his best friends in football, on international duty.

Your browser does not support iframes.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, who values players who can play in multiple positions such as Mikel Merino, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Kai Havertz and any number of his centre backs who can also play at full back, got a first-hand example of Scott’s class in April, when Bournemouth came to the Emirates Stadium and played the Gunners off the park in a 2-1 victory, with Scott getting the winner. ‘He has played for us as a No 10, a No 8; today as a No 6 and he has added a lot of defensive work and a lot of duel-winning to the ability he has on the ball,’ Iraola explained after that match. ‘I’m very happy, because he is becoming a very, very complete player.’ For Foster, it is important that Scott continues to rotate through the roles he can play, rather than keeping him stuck in one position. ‘Whether it’s 4-3-3 or 4-2-3-1, I wouldn't pigeonhole Alex really in terms of a number on his back,’ he says. ‘I just think he can affect the game really positively. I think he's got really high levels of game understanding and he just knows what's required. ‘He's an old-fashioned all-around midfield player. If you would have asked what Paul Scholes and Roy Keane were, they were central midfield players and I think Alex is that. He can get up and down, he can hold midfield, he can burst into the box, he can score and create. He's an all-round, really, really good midfield player.’ Scott's ability to dribble through the midfield is of particular interest to Arsenal, who need players that can break down opposition defences Scott's defensive ability is a lot better than his slight frame would make you expect This summer transfer window will be defined by the market for central midfielders. Anderson has sealed a British transfer record £116m move to Manchester City, Spurs spent a combined £185m on Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, both Enzo Fernandez (Chelsea) and Bruno Guimaraes (Newcastle) would fetch enormous fees if they were allowed to leave. And the stats show Scott has already vaulted himself into the conversation among the Premier League’s best midfielders, able to turn a match on his own. He ranked third behind Anderson (80) and Guimaraes (75) for fouls won from central midfield last season. He made more clearances than Arsenal pair Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi (both 78) and departed Manchester United anchor Casemiro (73) and ranked third for completed dribbles (29) among central midfielders, again behind Anderson (50) and Morgan Gibbs-White (30). ‘He’s very, very brave, in terms of taking the ball under the pressure,’ Foster adds. ‘He's got the ability as a midfield player to just beat you one-v-one, he's very creative.’ Coaches are also quick to point to Scott’s impact in both boxes, in terms of winning headers and duels at set-pieces, as an area of the game supporters often overlook due to his Jack Grealish-like frame and appearance. But Scott’s situation, in Bournemouth’s view at least, is clear. He’s not for sale. With two years left on his deal, and new boss Marco Rose eager to build his whole project around Scott, Bournemouth have no appetite to sell, and maintain they are desperate to tie him down to a new deal that will increase his price tag - despite the midfielder rejecting fresh terms. Scott scores the winner against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium in April Tuchel is becoming increasingly enamoured with the man once dubbed the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ That is unlikely to deter United, Arsenal or Chelsea. Scott’s step-sister Maya Le Tissier is captain of United’s women’s team. Her role in any pursuit may yet prove crucial. United have already splashed on midfield reinforcements this summer, signing Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa via his £38m release clause alongside adding Andrey Santos in a £50m package from Chelsea. But United remain in the market for a third midfielder and will be encouraged by Scott's decision not to sign a new contract at Bournemouth. That said, United would struggle to make a meaningful offer without a sale. Arsenal, meanwhile, missed out on Morgan Rogers - who is set to join Chelsea in a £117m deal, topping the record Anderson set earlier this month - but are keen on Newcastle's Guimaraes. Crystal Palace, West Ham and Tottenham, the team he grew up supporting, all looked at Scott in January 2023, before passing up and allowing Bournemouth to get him a few months later. Scott is loved by Nigel Pearson, who gave him his debut at Bristol City; loved by Foster, and has a massive fan in Carsley. Iraola is smitten with him, and may yet push him up Liverpool’s shopping list, and Tuchel is becoming increasingly enamoured with the man once dubbed the ‘Guernsey Grealish’. United, Arsenal and Chelsea know those footballing minds can’t all be wrong when it comes to the intangibles. So, let the bidding begin.

Sports.title: Lamine Yamal mocks Argentina brute Leandro Paredes with hilarious sign at Madrid's celebration parade after star's shameful violence at the World Cup final - as red carded villain claims they represented nation 'in best possible way'
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Spain superstar Lamine Yamal mocked Argentina brute Leandro Paredes with a punchy sign at the champions' World Cup celebrations in Madrid.

Two million supporters crowded the streets of the capital to welcome their heroes after they defeated Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final.

But the immediate aftermath of the match was marred by the barbarous antics of Paredes, who attacked two Spain players.

He grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat before shoving over substitute Gavi, causing a large-scale melee in the middle of the pitch - and it's that second act to which Yamal's sign referred.

Yamal held up a sign which read: 'Velada del ano VII: Paredes vs Gavi'. The Velada del Ano is a celebrity boxing event in Spain, not unlike Misfits.

Argentina were widely condemned for their behaviour after losing the final - but they have maintained a siege mentality following the game.

Midfielder Enzo Fernandez, who was sent off in normal time, claimed that they had represented their nation in the 'best way possible'.

Lamine Yamal mocked Argentina's Leandro Paredes at celebrations in Madrid, holding up a sign referring to his altercation with Gavi after the World Cup final

Boca Juniors midfielder Paredes was lambasted after the whistle for punching Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground

He said: 'As time passes, you realize there is something much bigger than a result.

'For years, this group has represented our country in the best possible way.

'It teaches that competing isn’t just about winning, but about giving everything for the shirt and never giving up. Being part of this group, which has always stood up, competed to the very end, and defended these colors with pride, humility, and commitment, is something I’ll always cherish.

'I want to thank all the Argentine fans. Thank you for always being there, for supporting us in every match, for your affection, for your unconditional support, and for making us feel at home no matter where we are in the world.

'Wearing my country’s shirt is the greatest honour of my career, and I will continue to give everything I have every time I’m called upon to defend it.'

Defending the shirt with violence is another matter, though, and the BBC's piundits weren't impressed. Micah Richards said of Argentina's behaviour: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time.

'Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest. Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Joe Hart had a similar opinion, saying: 'Disgusting behaviour. There was one man on that pitch with class and that was Lionel Messi.'

Captain Rodri lifted the World Cup as Spain touched down in Madrid yesterday

Yamal carried his luggage, including an oversized Hermes Birkin bag, off the plane

Wayne Rooney also said: 'It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them.

'If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves.'

Argentina were thuggish throughout the World Cup final, just as they had been against England in the semis.

Chelsea star Fernandez complained against his dismissal for a second yellow but his late foul on Pau Cubarsi, which sent the defender flying, was atrocious.

Boca Juniors midfielder Paredes was also fortunate to not be sent off in regular time for a foul on the edge of the box which presented Yamal with a last-breath free-kick before extra-time.

Argentina only had two shots in the entire match, the first of which came in the 117th minute.

By contrast, they were trigger-happy on the fouls with 24 - though Spain didn't have clean hands themselves, as they gave away 21.

Alan Shearer said: 'There's a way to lose. Too many times we've seen that reaction from them. They were trying to win free-kicks and their reaction after full time was terrible. The best team won. It's a result for football because of the way Spain have played.'

Spain were in high spirits as they celebrated winning the World Cup on their bus home to Madrid in the early hours of yesterday

Festivities in the hotel were limited to a bottle of £1,000 red wine drunk by Marcos Llorente, goalscorer Ferran Torres and Marc Pubill

Marc Cucurella and Gavi posed in front of the team's Airbus as they prepared to go home

The airplane arrived hours later as the city of Madrid readied a welcome home fit for heroes

Aymeric Laporte and Alex Baena both posed with the World Cup trophy onboard their plane

Even Lionel Messi didn't rise above the dark arts. The legendary forward was lambasted by Wayne Rooney after he tried to get Marc Cucurella sent off during the latter stages of the game.

The game descended into chaos when Fernandez received his second yellow card.

This led to a melee between both sets of players and Cucurella was spotted saying something to Messi.

The left-back then put a couple of fingers over his mouth and continued speaking, a move which the Argentine immediately reacted to and waved over the referee.

As per FIFA's rules for this tournament, if a player holds their hand over their mouth in a confrontational situation, they will be sent off.

This was seen with Miguel Almiron for Paraguay in the group stage and Piero Hincapie in the knockout stages for Ecuador.

However, it didn't appear that Cucurella was speaking in a confrontational manner and the referee, nor VAR, decided to intervene.

The BBC pundits were quick to hit out at Messi's behaviour as his team headed into extra time a man down.

Rodri led a bus full of Spanish players in rounds of singing as they headed for Newark airport

Yamal had previously enjoyed a cigar in the lift as he began his journey back to Spain

The prodigious Barcelona star had celebrated earlier on the pitch with his girlfriend Ines Garcia

Hart said: 'Oh wow! Wow! Yeah, I didn't enjoy that at all from Lionel Messi.

'You realise how on top Spain are if even Lionel Messi is reverting to that.'

Richards added: 'We don't want to see people getting sent off in a World Cup final for that.'

Rooney was similarly furious with Messi's behaviour as he said: 'It is desperation.

'Argentina play like that, we know that's what they do.

'But the one thing you want is good sportsmanship and that was sad to see Lionel Messi doing that.'

Ffter lifting the trophy in front of a full house of their adoring fans, La Roja opted not to ring in their victory with a night of partying in the city that never sleeps.

Instead, Golden Ball winner Rodri got the party started in transit, leading a round of singing on the team bus as the jubilant players sped back to their hotel for a team meal, before moving on to Newark Airport.

Back at the hotel, noted wine connoisseur Marcos Llorente enjoyed a bottle of Chateau Rayas Chateauneuf-du-Pape Reserve 2014 - which costs £1,009 to uncork - in his room with team-mates Ferran Torres and Marc Pubil.

The stars then boarded the Airbus A350-941 waiting for them - clad in their team's livery - and took off shortly after 2am local time.

Spain's players landed at Madrid's Barajas Airport at 2.30pm local time, and stepped out onto the tarmac with the World Cup trophy held aloft.

Sports.title: World Cup star Michael Olise's ex and mother of his child makes explosive claims against footballer after she ended romance because he spent 'too much time playing on his PlayStation'
Sports.content:
Michael Olise has been described as 'heartless' by the mother of his secret 20-month-old daughter amid an explosive legal dispute.

The France international, 24, was revealed to have fathered a child with 34-year-old Fatima Zaunbrecher, with Zaunbrecher taking her story public for the first time this week.

Speaking to German outlet BILD, Zaunbrecher alleged that Olise has not spoken to her since his daughter Aaliyah Noor's birth, choosing instead to communicate through lawyers. Zaunbrecher was also unhappy with Olise's offer to financially contribute to her upbringing, describing the proposed amount as 'ridiculous'.

Daily Mail Sport understands that Olise has never refused to meet his daughter, and has offered an acceptable financial sum to support the child.

'How heartless can you be towards your child?' Zaunbrecher questioned in her interview, adding that his 'callousness' had 'devastated her'.

Michael Olise has been accused of not supporting or meeting his 20-month-old daughter

Zaunbrecher is based in Dusseldorf and had been when the former couple started to communicate on Instagram in 2022.

The relationship allegedly began when Olise was playing at Crystal Palace, ahead of his £47.4million move to Bayern Munich.

The woman alleges that messages were exchanged between them for two months before she joined him in south London for their first date, saying that the pair had 'liked each other immediately'.

'He's half Algerian, I'm half Moroccan,' she explained. 'They're neighbouring countries after all. He also dislikes large crowds and parties, just like me.

'When he tried to kiss me on our first date, I stopped him and told him we should get to know each other better. He accepted that. From then on, I flew to London regularly.'

Their relationship eventually became tempestuous, Zaunbrecher added, due to disputes over Olise's frequent habit of playing PlayStation rather than spending time with her, and claims of infidelity on his part.

Zaunbrecher then claimed that two weeks after she had finally broken up with him over a suspected other woman, she discovered she was pregnant.

A paternity test - completed in Munich at Olise's insistence - has since confirmed that he is Aaliyah's father.

Sources close to the footballer have insisted that he had not refused contact with Zaunbrecher or his child.

Olise has an intensely private social media presence and has often seemed to shy away from the spotlight in public too.

But since the revelation in the German press, Olise is believed to have seen his social media comments section overwhelmed with replies, and since switched off the function on Instagram.

Alongside the article, BILD also released what they alleged to be a copy of the document confirming Olise's paternity.

Olise has not yet issued a comment publicly.

Sports.title: Deluded World Cup final villain Enzo Fernandez insists Argentina represented nation in 'best possible way' despite disgraceful behaviour in New York and riling England fans with Falklands flag
Sports.content:
Deluded World Cup final villain Enzo Fernandez insists Argentina represented nation in 'best possible way' despite disgraceful behaviour in New York and riling England fans with Falklands flag

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Argentina's World Cup pantomime villain Enzo Fernandez has claimed he and his team-mates represented the country 'in the best possible way' in a bizarre statement on social media on Tuesday.

The Chelsea star, who goaded England with a mocking celebration after netting Argentina's equaliser in last Wednesday's dismal semi-final defeat, was left with egg on his face in the World Cup final on Sunday as his red card proved crucial to Spain's crowning 1-0 victory.

Fernandez, already booked for dissent, sent Pau Cubarsi flying with a dangerous tackle in stoppage time and left Argentina to defend with 10 men for the entirety of extra time.

Argentina's behaviour throughout the World Cup was heavily criticised after Lionel Scaloni's men used aggressive tackling, timewasting and dirty tactics to aid them en route to the final, before several players attacked Spanish stars after the full-time whistle at MetLife Stadium in deplorable scenes of violence and thuggery.

Despite being under investigation by FIFA over the post-match melees, Fernandez urged that Argentina represented themselves 'in the best possible way' during the tournament.

Enzo Fernandez believes Argentina showcased themselves and the country 'in the best possible way', despite several players attacking Spain's stars after the World Cup final

Fernandez goaded England with a mocking celebration after scoring in Argentina's 2-1 victory

'As time passes, you realise there is something much bigger than a result,' he wrote in a statement on social media platform Instagram. 'For years, this group has represented our country in the best possible way.

'It teaches that competing isn't just about winning, but about giving everything for the shirt and never giving up. Being part of this group, which has always stood up, competed to the very end, and defended these colors with pride, humility, and commitment, is something I'll always cherish.

'I want to thank all the Argentine fans. Thank you for always being there, for supporting us in every match, for your affection, for your unconditional support, and for making us feel at home no matter where we are in the world.

'Wearing my country's shirt is the greatest honor of my career, and I will continue to give everything I have every time I'm called upon to defend it.'

Several Argentina players were involved in ugly post-match clashes with Spain's players immediately after the final whistle, which confirmed the European nation as world champions with a 1-0 victory after extra time.

Spain's captain Rodri was struck by Nahuel Molina as he went to celebrate with his team-mates, before Dani Olmo was punched by Argentina coach Roberto Ayala.

Elsewhere, Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes attacked Eric Garcia by grabbing him by the neck and then, along with team-mate Thiago Almada's help, threw unused Spanish substitute Gavi to the floor in disgraceful scenes.

The Chelsea star was sent off in the final after sending Pau Cubarsi flying with a late tackle

The deplorable post-match incidents came after Spain had dominated the match in terms of possession and chances, while Argentina attempted to stop them in their tracks with tough tackling, timewasting and dirty tactics.

After the final, world football's governing body FIFA swiftly opened an investigation into Argentina's violent post-match conduct, appointing a Disciplinary and Ethics Prosecutor to review footage, referee reports and documentation submitted by match delegates.

According to FIFA's Disciplinary Code, players found guilty of violent conduct should be issued with at least a three-match ban.

The same penalty applies to acts of aggression including punches, kicks, elbows, headbutts or other blows against an opponent.

Fernandez and his team-mates were also at the centre of controversy after celebrating with a banner claiming that the Falkland Islands were Argentine following their late 2-1 win over England last week.

FIFA are also investigating whether to issue a sanction in relation to the political statement, which is against their rules and regulations.

Fernandez played a key role in Argentina's 2022 World Cup triumph in Qatar before moving to Chelsea for a then-British record fee of £106.8million.

Following his behaviour and antics at the 2026 World Cup, Fernandez could receive a hostile reception in the first few weeks of the Premier League season when he returns to Stamford Bridge under new manager Xabi Alonso.

Sports.title: The teenage sweetheart who was Kevin Keegan's rock right until his last moments: Football legend met his wife of 51 years Jean on the waltzers at a Doncaster fair - but modest star told her a white lie
Sports.content:
It was a summer's day in 1970 when Kevin Keegan plucked up the courage to speak with a certain Jean Woodhouse at Doncaster fair.

He was 19, she 16, and the pair had been on the waltzers. The soundtrack of that summer was Mungo Jerry's 'In the Summertime', and were he to take her out for fish and chips, it would've cost 20 to 30 pence.

By this stage Keegan was already making strides in football, an employment which entitled him to around £30 per week. He had spent two years playing for Fourth Division side Scunthorpe United and in eight months he would be off to Liverpool.

But feeling slightly bashful, a young Keegan did not try to woo his new belle with tales from the football pitch. Instead, he pitched himself as a humble steelworker, the job he took in summertime to earn a bit of extra cash. During the off-season, Scunthorpe cut his weekly wages, you see, so he had to supplement that with jobs on the steel and in a psychiatric hospital.

'Telling them I was a footballer would have sounded too flash, even though I was an unknown playing for a small club,' Keegan later recalled. Humility was often his way.

The ruse worked. Woodhouse was charmed - despite the fact she had a crush on Manchester United superstar George Best - and four years later they married at St Peter in Chains Catholic Church in Doncaster. The eager lovers brought the ceremony forward while he was serving a ban.

Kevin Keegan and his wife Jean Woodhouse were married for 51 years from 1974 until he died

The duo, who met on the waltzers at Doncaster fair, kept their private life out of the public eye

Their marriage lasted 51 years until his death on Monday and, despite him being one of the poster boys for English football in that time, little is known of the life they kept away from the pitch. Privacy and the protection of their daughters Laura and Sarah were paramount.

Jean didn't take too much of an interest in the football herself, but with a self-sacrificial spirit, she followed him everywhere.

In May 1971 he moved to Liverpool for £33,000 and was inducted into Bill Shankly's legendary team. Suddenly his basic wage was £50 per week. There, Keegan won three First Division titles and a European Cup, though their Liverpudlian stint started inauspiciously.

Keegan arrived for his debut against Nottingham Forest late because he had misjudged the severity of the traffic on the way to Anfield. That earned him the nickname Andy McDaft, but he silenced any doubters after 12 minutes with a stunning debut goal.

After six remarkable years with the Reds, Jean followed him to Hamburg, Germany, where he would twice win the Ballon d'Or prize for being the world's best player.

Life later took them to Southampton, County Durham, the United States, Spain, and Inverkip in Scotland, and Jean was always by his side - even if she didn't pay much attention to his sporting antics.

'My wife Jean has always taken football with a pinch of salt,' Keegan once told The Guardian.

'She doesn't ever get over-involved in it, not when I'm out of it and not when I'm in it. That is the key. After matches, if you've lost she knows not to say too much for about 24 hours while you get over it and if you've won she knows I might take her out at night.

Jean wasn't overly interested in his footballing antics - and he even hid his career at first!

She and one of their daughters, Laura, joined Keegan as he received his OBE at Buckingham Palace in 1982

'We decided early on that football and family should mix as seldom as possible. In our minds there was football and then there was life.'

Football was talked about so little in the home that his daughters actually thought he was a professional golfer, given how much time he dedicated to it in their seven years in Spain.

The love he and Jean shared was horse riding. She was more adept than himself but, on those rides out, they could share a peace which wasn't afforded to him when out in public.

'To relax, I do horse riding. My wife is keen on horses,' he said in a television interview.

'I can't ride a horse to save my life. If you see me running funny on a Saturday, it's because we've been for a horse ride on the Friday night!

'Once you get on the back of a horse and get up a mountain, it's funny, nobody wants your autograph when you're galloping along. They want to get out of the way!'

He added: 'I just live normal. The terrible thing about the public in a way, and I don't mean terrible in a nasty way... you can go and talk to someone and they'll say: "oh, he talked to me, he's natural."

'Of course I'm natural! I was born the same as they were. I was brought up the same as they were. I'm just the same as they are. I think people tend to think you should be different and if you see it long enough, it could make you different.

Jean pictured outside a romany caravan near their house they shared in north Wales while Keegan was at Liverpool

Liverpool, Newcastle and England legend Keegan has died at the age of 75 after a short battle with illness

Keegan (pictured in 1977 after winning the European Cup with Liverpool) is one of the greatest players English football has ever produced

The sprawling Georgian property that was once home to footballer Kevin Keegan while he was the boss of Newcastle United in the 1990s

The property features a large white kitchen decorated with chandeliers and characterful touches

'I enjoy meeting people very much. I enjoy meeting the fans. I just came down on the train and had half a dozen around me all the way. I'd sooner have them round me than be sat on my own twiddling my thumbs.'

The sense you get is that Kevin and Jean retained their humility even when their circumstances improved.

Keegan's mother Doris was a domestic worker and his father, Joe, was a miner and Newcastle fan. The future England manager grew up in a home with no electricity, bathroom or inside toilet. If he wanted to watch the beautiful game which he so dearly loved, he had to go to a friend's house to sit down in front of the TV.

When he was manager of Newcastle in the 1990s, he and Jean moved into a sprawling country pad.

The grand Georgian property in County Durham is situated on 5.4 acres of gardens in a gated community with 24-hour security and boasts a games room, pool and bar.

This expansive property was extended in Keegan's day and has been extended again since making it now a five-bedroom home of nearly 10,000 sq ft.

It boasts a reception hall, kitchen/breakfast room, lounge, dining room, orangery, study, wine cellar and indoor swimming pool on the ground floor.

Last year it was listed for sale for £2.25million.

That's an example of the type of property they could afford, but they never lost sight of the simple pleasures of life. In the mid-2000s they purchased a house in Inverkip, a village in Scotland's west central Lowlands, and would take driving trips out into nature together. Local business workers knew them as regulars.

As one local recalled: 'I met him a few times with his wife and daughter – he was a very nice man with a nice family, and you could have a laugh with him.'

Keegan died on Monday surrounded by Jean and their two girls, having been diagnosed with stage four stomach cancer in January. In sickness and in health Jean stood by his side - whether at Buckingham Palace to receive his OBE or on a candyfloss-filled summer's day at Doncaster fair.

Sports.title: Grand National-winner’s training partnership to end as ally announces new venture
Sports.content:
Grand National-winner’s training partnership to end as ally announces new venture

After two and a half years together a restructure will result in Dr Richard Newland and Jamie Insole going their separate ways as trainers

View 2 Images Dr Richard Newland and Jamie Insole (left): going their separate ways

One of the most successful training partnerships since their introduction is to split.

‌



Grand National-winning trainer Dr Richard Newland announced two and half years ago that he was expanding his operation into the Flat and he was taking on Jamie Insole to help manage it. Newland tasted Aintree glory with Pineau De Re in 2014, while he also has a Cheltenham Festival winner on his CV thanks to the 2007 Coral Cup success of Burntoakboy.

‌



After starting training with only three horses in 2006 Newland sent out more than 500 winners and nearly 150 after teaming up with Insole at his state of the art yard in Droitwich, Worcestershire.

‌



Aidan O’Brien to run controversial frontrunner Puerto Rico in Bow Echo vs Gstaad rematch READ MORE :

Jockey William Buick banned for eight days after being blamed for causing horse stumble READ MORE :

Together they won the Lennox Stakes at Goodwood last year with Witness Stand while Dividend recorded two wins during the Dubai Carnival.

But from the end of August Insole is to establish a yard in Lambourn with his partner, Racing TV presenter Jess Stafford.

“Following recent reports and the decision to restructure the training operation at Urloxhey, I can confirm that my training partnership with Dr Richard Newland will come to an end next month,” Insole said in a statement.

‌



View 2 Images Hollie Doyle on Witness Stand with Jamie Insole (left): struck in the Lennox Stakes (Image: PA)

“I am immensely proud of what we have achieved over the past two and a half years. From a standing start I established and developed the Flat operation at Urloxhey alongside a fantastic and hardworking team, and together we have enjoyed some memorable successes.”

He continued: “I will always be grateful to Richard for giving me the opportunity to begin my training career within the partnership. Establishing yourself as a trainer in Britain is no easy task, and that opportunity provided an invaluable platform from which to build the Flat string from the ground up.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

“It has always been my ambition to establish my own training business and build an operation that reflects my own vision. Jess and I are now in the advanced stages of finalising a lease on a state-of-the-art yard in Lambourn, with excellent facilities and access to some of the best gallops in the country.

“Although the move to our new Lambourn base has always been planned for later this year, the partnership at Urloxhey will now come to an end beforehand, creating a short term period before I am able to begin training under my own licence.”

Article continues below

He added: “While this transition has arrived sooner than anticipated our focus is firmly on the future.”

Sports.title: Aidan O’Brien to run controversial frontrunner Puerto Rico in Bow Echo vs Gstaad rematch
Sports.content:
Aidan O’Brien to run controversial frontrunner Puerto Rico in Bow Echo vs Gstaad rematch

Christophe Soumillon was found to have ridden Puerto Rico in a way which benefitted stablemate Gstaad at Royal Ascot but an appeal panel was not satisfied it was intentional

View 2 Images Gstaad (left) was able to challenge along the far rail after Puerto Rico (obscured) was switched left early in the straight (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Aidan O’Brien is set to run controversial frontrunner Puerto Rico in next week’s £1.2 million Sussex Stakes rematch between Bow Echo and Gstaad.

‌



After the second clash of the year between the 2,000 Guineas first and second in the St James’s Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot, Bow Echo confirmed his superiority by holding off Gstaad by a short head.

‌



But that wasn’t the whole story as jockey Christophe Soumillon, who was aboard Puerto Rico, received an eight-day ban for ‘riding in a manner to benefit’ stablemate Gstaad. The ten-time French champion took two glances over his shoulder as he moved Puerto Rico towards the middle the course entering the straight, causing slight inteference to another rival, which left space for Gstaad to make his challenge along the far rail.

‌



Jockey William Buick banned for eight days after being blamed for causing horse stumble READ MORE :

He appealed against the verdict but a disciplinary panel was satisfied he rode in a way which gave an advantage to Gstaad, adding, “For the avoidance of doubt, we are not satisfied that the Appellant intended so to do.” However the suspension was cut to five days.

Puerto Rico, a dual Group 1 winner under Soumillon last year, finished sixth at Ascot but is among the Ballydoyle entries for the July 29 showpiece in which the three-year-olds will race against older horses for the first time.

Confirming his plans for the Glorious Goodwood meeting in an interview with the racecourse, O'Brien said he was keen to run both Gstaad and Puerto Rico. He said: “Gstaad came out of Ascot very well and we’re looking forward to going there with him – we always thought it was a race that would suit him.

‌



View 2 Images Bow Echo (right) wins by a short head from Gstaad (Image: Mike Egerton/PA Wire)

“He obviously just failed at Ascot. Things didn’t go perfectly for us at Ascot, and maybe they didn’t for Bow Echo either.

“In the Guineas, we felt we were forced on. We were very forward and had to do our own donkey work, while Bow Echo had lovely cover and everything worked well for him.

‌



“Then we went to Ascot and felt that maybe it didn’t go 100 per cent for us either. Maybe the lads thought it didn’t go perfectly for Bow Echo, either.

“It’s going to be interesting. That’s what I think makes these races great. We’re looking forward to seeing what happens.”

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Of Puerto Rico, O'Brien said: “Obviously, Ascot was a complete mess for him. He went forward, and I think he got taken on for the lead. It just all went out the window.

“We had planned on making the running with him. He won his two Group 1s making the running - it just didn’t work for him on the day.

“There was a snowball effect throughout the whole race when that happened, but that’s racing, and it doesn’t go right all the time.

Article continues below

“We’re very happy with his progress since, and we feel that we will see a different horse this time.”

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua retirement date emerges just days before Tyson Fury warm-up fight
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua retirement date emerges just days before Tyson Fury warm-up fight

The former two-time heavyweight champion will return to the ring this weekend before taking on Tyson Fury in an all-British showdown later this year

View Image Anthony Joshua speaks ahead of his return to the ring (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

Anthony Joshua has got another three years left in him before finally calling it a day.

‌



That is according to Matchroom founder Barry Hearn - who offered a rather glittering take ahead of the British brawler's return to the ring. The former two-time heavyweight champion will take on unknown heavyweight Kristian Prenga over in Saudi Arabia on Saturday night.

‌



Joshua has not fought since knocking out YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul in the sixth round back in December. The 36-year-old had been due to fight again in February, but was forced to postpone his return after he was involved in a horrific car crash just days after his win over Paul.

‌



Many wondered whether Joshua would ever fight again, and even promoter Eddie Hearn had previously suggested that 2026 could be 'AJ's' last year in the ring. But according to Hearn's father, Barry, Joshua seems more motivated than ever.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Anthony Joshua sent brutal warning ahead of boxing comeback READ MORE :

In an interview with Sky Sports, he said: "[Anthony Joshua] is in an amazing place at the moment. Obviously I’ve seen him since 2012, we got very close. He’s like a member of our family really. I don’t think I’ve seen him so motivated for the long term.

"As I say, some of that has been fuelled by that tragic accident, but he’s now talking about the next three years in the ring. It was a year ago we were talking about potentially two fights and then go off to a happy retirement.

"He’s very motivated, he feels good about himself, but boxing is a funny sport. It takes one decent punch from a big lad to knock out anyone in the world."

Article continues below

Barry Hearn gives clear verdict on Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight collapsing READ MORE :

Providing Joshua comes away from his fight this weekend unscathed, he will then take on long-time rival Tyson Fury in November. 'AJ' was ringside for Fury's comeback win over Arslanbek Makhmudov back in April. The 'Gypsy King' quickly called out Joshua merely minutes after the contest, but the latter refused to engage in all of the theatrics.

However, just days later, the pair finally agreed to a fight and settling their decade-long feud. Like Joshua, Fury is also expected to fight this week. The Morecambe scrapper will take on veteran heavyweight Mariusz Wach on Friday night over in Thailand. Fury is putting the fight on for charity and will give the proceeds from the 1,500 tickets to local good causes.

Sports.title: Arsenal make first Bruno Guimaraes transfer approach as £60m plans ripped up
Sports.content:
Arsenal make first Bruno Guimaraes transfer approach as £60m plans ripped up

Arsenal have been heavily linked with signing Newcastle United star Bruno Guimaraes for the majority of the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes is still being linked with a move to Arsenal (Image: Getty )

Arsenal have reportedly stepped up their efforts to sign Newcastle United star Bruno Guimaraes, but may have seemingly changed their previous plans for the transfer.

‌



Guimaraes has been heavily linked with a move to the Gunners all summer and reportedly expressed a wish to leave Newcastle earlier in the window.

‌



The 28-year-old remains under contract at St James’ Park until 2028, and The Times have reported that Arsenal have now opened talks with Newcastle over a deal for the midfielder.

‌



The report claims that Arsenal had previously made it clear they would be prepared to pay up to £60million to sign Guimaraes this summer.

However, Newcastle are seemingly determined to maintain their £75million valuation, meaning Arsenal would need to change their plans in order to meet the Magpies’ valuation.

A separate report from The Telegraph has claimed that Newcastle have been left "mystified" by the reports claiming they have begun talks with Arsenal over a deal for Guimaraes.

‌



It remains to be seen if an agreement will be reached between Arsenal and Newcastle for Guimaraes, who was recently with the Brazil squad for this summer’s World Cup.

Guimaraes was part of the Brazil squad that reached the last-16 stage in North America, before the Selecao were denied a quarter-final spot thanks to a defeat to Norway.

The Newcastle star will now be on a summer break before returning to pre-season duties in the next few weeks, and it remains to be seen if that will be with Arsenal or Newcastle.

‌



The report does suggest, though, that if Arsenal were to make an offer of around £75million, it would give the Magpies something to think about.

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes was recently with the Brazil squad at the World Cup (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The update comes on the back of reports emerging that Arsenal had reached an agreement for an improved sponsorship deal with Emirates, which is believed to be worth around £70million.

Arsenal have been heavily linked with signing a new midfielder this summer as they prepare to defend their Premier League title, which resumes next month.

The Gunners have also been planning to strengthen their forward options, having recently agreed a deal to sell Leandro Trossard to Besiktas for around £17million.

‌



Morgan Rogers was a target for Arsenal this summer, but is now expected to seal a £117million switch to Chelsea instead.

Newcastle will be determined to keep Guimaraes at the club, particularly after already sanctioning two major sales earlier in the window.

Tottenham Hotspur signed Sandro Tonali in a deal worth £100million earlier this summer, while Anthony Gordon moved to Barcelona in a £69million transfer before the start of the World Cup.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes accuses Thomas Tuchel of trying to get sacked after comments on England stars
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes accuses Thomas Tuchel of trying to get sacked after comments on England stars

Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Scholes has questioned England boss Thomas Tuchel's approach following the Three Lions' World Cup exit to Argentina

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel has been criticised for his tactics in England's semi-final defeat to Argentina (Image: Kevin C. Cox, Getty Images)

Paul Scholes has accused Thomas Tuchel of wanting to be sacked by England. The Three Lions boss endured a disappointing end to his first World Cup as his team exited the tournament at the semi-final stage to Argentina with a toothless end.

The German coach's substitutions came under scrutiny following the match, while Tuchel took aim at the DNA of English football and suggested he never tasked his players with sitting deep to defend their lead. Despite England recording their best finish since winning the tournament in 1996, there has been discussion over whether Tuchel remains the figure to lead the side.

The former Chelsea boss is under contract until after the Euros in two years' time, and Tuchel has indicated he intends to stay in position until that time. But Scholes is not convinced that the 52-year-old wants to stay.

"I think his comments since the game have actually made it worse than the performances. Saying it's not in the English DNA. You're part of that DNA now, Thomas," Scholes said on The Good, The Bad & The Football.

"He's gone on the offensive and blamed players a lot," Scholes continued. "That is something our manager would never do.

Leandro Paredes refuses to apologise for World Cup final 'punches' as FIFA overturn red READ MORE :

Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer READ MORE :

"He'd blame us behind closed doors on the training ground and meetings but in public never. I think Thomas Tuchel has a bit of a history with this at football clubs; he blames players and falls out with sporting directors. You just wonder with the way he's been speaking, 'do I want to get sacked'."

"It seems to indicate that [Thomas Tuchel] does want to leave [the England role] from the stuff he was saying because it was quite hard to come back from that," he added. "And I didn't realise until yesterday, when I heard someone talking about it, how much he fell out with people at football clubs he's been at.

"You think about it, he's not been at clubs for very long, has he? PSG, Borussia Dortmund, Bayern Munich. He falls out with people and maybe just engineering his way out."

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel will lead England into the Nations League (Image: Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Nicky Butt also questioned Tuchel's approach. "He's obviously an honest coach, and he says what he thinks, but do you think the PR who works with him, obviously they have a big PR at the FA, do you not think they should be coaching him on what to say? 'If you're going to stay on in this job, Thomas, you need to say this.'"

Scholes said: "I don't think he cares. He's had big jobs, he's not bothered."

"I get that but they should lead him in the right direction," Butt replied. "If he wants to stay on he needs to play the game."

Butt was also frustrated with Tuchel's squad selection. "You look at the squad, he brings defenders on, he's not really got that many attacking options to go on anyway," he said.

"Rashford and for me Watkins should have been brought on. Even that 10 role with Palmer and Foden at home, they must be sat at home thinking 'what am i doing here on holiday with my feet up, I should be trying to win us the World Cup'."

Sports.title: Aston Villa are down familiar transfer path but eventually Unai Emery’s magic won’t be enough
Sports.content:
Aston Villa seem to be on a rinse and repeat summer plan that has them grappling whether to sell their top players and then having to think, and think again, before making major signings.

Off the back of a season that saw Unai Emery lead Villa to fourth, owing to a run that saw them win 12 out of 13 games, and end a 30-year trophy drought by winning the Europa League two of their first moves this summer have been to sell Youri Tielemans and, any day now, Morgan Rogers.

Two of their three goalscorers in their European final victory have sought pastures new, recouping £152million in the process, which eases the financial concerns the club may have had whilst they also prepare for Champions League revenue once more.

It seems only Villa can sanction British-record transfer exits and then have to think about whether they go and land some more marquee names. Already Johan Manzambi has been signed from Freiburg for a club-record £58m and Joao Gomes has moved over from Wolves for £38m, but rather than go again, the consideration seems to be whether they may have to sell more of their first-team regulars.

‌



The Midlands outfit have become the poster boys for the flaws in PSR regulations in recent years. But whilst supporters of the club bemoan a system that isn't working for them, it is worth considering that they are not blameless and the reliance on Emery's magic wand is a ticking time bomb.

Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer READ MORE :

Villa find themselves in a position, the like of which they've probably not been in since the early 1990s when they pushed Manchester United for the Premier League title. Their scope for mistakes, and being able to recover from them, is far less than the established teams who can have a poor year and bounce back with relative ease.

So when the Midlands side get hold of a top player, surely it serves them better to retain him - and case studies back that up. Here are a few genuine, maybe slightly hard to accept, facts.

£100m players just don't move to certain clubs. If you're that good and on the market for that amount of money, there's only a cluster of places you end up. So when Villa sell Rogers for £100m the odds on them getting a similar replacement, probably for similar money, are slim to none.

‌



View 4 Images Morgan Rogers has been invaluable to Aston Villa (Image: Dan Mullan, Getty Images)

Villa sold Jack Grealish for £100m and that money was distributed out on new arrivals. They finished 11th with him and 14th without him, sacking a manager in that time. West Ham sold Declan Rice for £105m, distributed those funds and three years later have been relegated. Newcastle sold Alexander Isak for £125m, signed several frontmen to fill the void, and dropped massively. Go back further and Tottenham reinvested Gareth Bale's then world-record fee on the so-called "Magnificent Seven" - which didn't get them far.

So unless you're Liverpool selling Philippe Countinho for over £100m and buying Virgil van Dijk, a defender wanted by every top Premier League team, the offloading of an elite player for huge sums to reinvest has rarely ended well.

The parallels with Tottenham circa 2015 to 2019 are undeniable. A sleeping giant of sorts that finally cracked a once exclusive club, much of it owing to a sensationally gifted manager in the dugout. Mauricio Pochettino made Tottenham more than the sum of their parts and had them mixing it with the elite.

‌



Emery has done likewise, but like Pochettino, there was always talk of him eventually taking the plunge at a club who could consistently offer him the chance to win titles. When Tottenham lost Pochettino, the fear was they'd fall, and so they did. Its hard to deny that the same wouldn't happen to Villa.

And for all the talk of Emery's commitment, the fact he's found the perfect environment, the fact he's allowed the run of the club. Nothing lasts forever and the Spaniard can only pull so many rabbits out of a hat.

View 4 Images Aston Villa have bought in Johan Manzambi as they look to fill the void left behind

Villa, like Tottenham, are investing in their stadium, albeit to a far lesser degree. The hope is that it will bring more financial income, but what about the impact on the pitch? Villa's is yet to be determined but, for all the talk of needing a slight rebuild and getting good money for players, no team in history, has seen sanctioning first-team player exits on an almost annual basis as a route to success.

‌



The frustration with Tottenham, from a Villa stand point, is how they finished 17th and have since spent £185million on two midfielders, breaking their club-record fee twice in a week to land Mateus Fernandes and then Sandro Tonali.

That will make them infinitely better, but their financial structure ultimately gave them the scope to do so whilst Villa, who finished fourth, can go nowhere near matching those fees.

In the accounts for 2024/25 Villa had the highest wages to revenue ratio in the league, spending 74 percent of it on their player salaries, just over £270m, according to a Deloitte report. In stark contrast Tottenham's own figure was 45 percent - the lowest in the top flight.

The PSR rules that have governed the Premier League state that clubs cannot post losses of more than £105m over a three-year reporting cycle, which is well documented now, as are the punishments for breaching them. Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) system comes in as its replacement from the upcoming season, which means clubs will be allowed to spend a maximum of 85 percent of their revenue on squad costs - which cover player wages, amortised transfers and agents' fees. UEFA's remains at 70 percent.

‌



View 4 Images Unai Emery has continued to mix it with the Premier League's elite, but some will question how long he can keep it up

Villa's willingness to spend so much of their revenue of player wages had actually come down. Go back 12 months to the 2023/24 season and it was more than 90 percent of their revenue. These are decisions ultimately taken by the club, prepared to operate close to the limit, hence why they were fined £19.4m by UEFA this month for a "significant breach" of its squad-cost rule for 2025.

Whether the current financial regulations are fit for purpose is ultimately a debate worth having, but this current set of rules are where we are right now. Plenty of top clubs, and aspiring ones, are managing to operate in an ambitious way within them.

Villa seem to have been hamstrung since the early days of the Emery era, when it did become clear that his managerial prowess was going to cover up for other shortcomings.

‌



Already it looks like a summer where those at Villa Park will, privately at least, bemoan the state of the financial landscape. Emi Martinez is another name being linked with the exit door.

After losing to Everton six months ago Emery himself claimed: "We are not contender to be in the top five. We are still not being contenders. There are other teams with more potential than us."

Whether that was a parting shot at those above him, a genuine reminder of where they are or the harsh reality of managing a club operating at their maximum is anyone's guess.

Sports.title: Chelsea to announce £34m transfer after Jude Bellingham World Cup slap
Sports.content:
Chelsea to announce £34m transfer after Jude Bellingham World Cup slap

Chelsea are expected to announce the signing of Argentina international Valentin Barco

View 2 Images Valentin Barco of Argentina is expected to join Chelsea (Image: Jose Hernandez/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Strasbourg star Valentin Barco is still expected to become a Chelsea player this summer, after the Argentina star had a heated exchange with Jude Bellingham during the World Cup.

‌



Barco was part of the Argentina squad that faced England in the semi-final of the World Cup last week, and is now expected to move to Stamford Bridge in the near future.

‌



Chelsea have already completed the signings of Geovany Quenda and Marco Palestra this summer, and there are growing rumours that more could follow in the days and weeks ahead.

‌



It was reported back in May that Barco would sign for Chelsea after the Londoners agreed a €40million (£34m) deal with Strasbourg.

Leandro Paredes refuses to apologise for World Cup final 'punches' as FIFA overturn red READ MORE :

Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer READ MORE :

The Athletic have now revealed that Chelsea are on the verge of confirming the Barco signing, just days after the midfielder became involved in a fiery confrontation at the World Cup.

Barco was a member of the Argentina squad that battled through to the World Cup final, though he managed just 19 minutes of action across the entire tournament.

‌



It was during the semi-final victory over England that Barco became involved in a tense exchange with Bellingham.

Barco, who remained on the bench throughout the win against the Three Lions, ran past several England players as he celebrated one of Argentina's goals.

View 2 Images Jude Bellingham of England reacts towards Valentín Barco of Argentina (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Following the final whistle, Bellingham was spotted watching on as Argentina's players celebrated, with Barco rushing over to join his jubilant teammates.

The Real Madrid star then noticed Barco and made his way over to the incoming Chelsea star, clipping him around the back of the head before the pair became embroiled in a heated confrontation, with shoving and fierce words exchanged.

‌



Barco will now head off on a summer break having been part of the Argentina squad that reached the World Cup final, with a formal announcement from Chelsea confirming his signing appearing to be just around the corner.

The news surrounding Barco comes as Chelsea seal a deal to bring Morgan Rogers to Stamford Bridge from Aston Villa in a £117million transfer, pipping Arsenal to the England international's signature in the process.

Reports have also surfaced suggesting that England defender John Stones is firmly on the Blues' radar, after the 32-year-old departed Manchester City as a free agent earlier this summer.

Sports.title: Chelsea could ruin Arsenal transfer plans AGAIN as Blues target John Stones
Sports.content:
Chelsea could ruin Arsenal transfer plans AGAIN as Blues target John Stones

John Stones is a free agent after starring for England at the World Cup and his availability has alerted both Chelsea and Arsenal in their search for defensive reinforcements

View 2 Images John Stones is on both Chelsea and Arsenal's radar (Image: Pat Isaacs/NurPhoto)

John Stones is one option being considered by Chelsea in their search for central defensive reinforcements, potentially putting the Blues on another collision course with Arsenal.

‌



Stones is available on a free transfer following the expiry of his contract at Manchester City and, despite a season of limited game time, his stock is high after a strong showing at the World Cup with England. At the age of 32, Stones offers extensive Premier League pedigree following his trophy-laden decade in Manchester and is understood to have suitors both in England and abroad.

‌



It emerged over the weekend that Arsenal are courting Stones amid concerns that William Saliba faces up to five months on the sidelines due to the back injury that plagued him during the World Cup.

‌



However, The Athletic have revealed that Chelsea are also keen on Stones, who would aid their mission to add more 'ready-made' players to their squad.

Chelsea could add two central defenders to their squad this summer depending on exits and are currently in talks with Crystal Palace over a deal for the impressive Maxence Lacroix. A deal for the 26-year-old could cost as much as £55million, though, which is a figure higher than Chelsea's valuation of the Frenchman.

If both Arsenal and Chelsea were to move for Stones in the coming weeks, then he would be the second England World Cup star the London clubs have competed for this summer after Morgan Rogers.

‌



Both Arsenal and Chelsea are long-term admirers of the Aston Villa star, who was always expected to move for big money this summer.

View 2 Images Chelsea have already signed another Arsenal target in Stones' World Cup team-mate, Morgan Rogers (Image: Eddie Keogh/The FA)

But despite Arsenal emerging as the red-hot favourites to land him in recent weeks, it's Chelsea who have won the race for Rogers' signature after shaking hands with Aston Villa on a deal worth £117m.

‌



Arsenal are understood to have valued Rogers at £80m, though it's understood they may have gone to £100m to land a player who amassed 14 goals and 12 assists across 55 games in all competitions last season.

But with Villa's valuation of Rogers increasing in the wake of Elliot Anderson's £116m transfer to Manchester City, Chelsea have put up the money to seal what could well end up being the biggest deal of the summer.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
