World.title: Indian Oil Corp stops loading Iraqi oil amid Hormuz instability
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Sources told Reuters that Indian Oil Corp. (IOC) has stopped loading Iraqi oil from Basrah Oil Terminal due to increasing risk and assaults on vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz.

Around July 23, the state-run IOC planned to transport 2 million barrels of Iraqi oil via the mega-sized crude carrier Lila Jamnagar.

Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd, a different state refiner, has also halted plans to transport oil from Iraq via the Indian-flagged Aframax tanker Desh Gaurav.

Following the resumption of military operations in the Strait of Hormuz, India has advised shipping companies to refrain from assigning Indian seafarers to vessels operating in that region.

Ship captains were also advised to be cautious regarding security in the Arabian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, and surrounding waterways and to continuously check navigational warnings.

Prior to the war, the Strait of Hormuz between Iran and Oman served as the primary transit route for around a fifth of the world’s oil and gas supplies.

Tensions have escalated since the truce between Washington and Tehran was broken in early July. This breakdown has resulted in attacks that have disrupted trade through the crucial waterway.

World.title: Turkish Transport Minister arrives in baghdad to elevate transport ties and Development Road cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Turkish Minister of Transport and Infrastructure Abdulkadir Uraloğlu arrived in Baghdad on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, to conduct high-level talks with Iraqi officials aimed at taking bilateral cooperation in transport, logistics, and telecommunications to a higher level.

Minister Uraloğlu was officially welcomed at Baghdad International Airport by Deputy Minister of Transport Hazem Razi Lafta, before holding bilateral talks with Iraqi Minister of Transport Wahb Al-Hasani at the state guesthouse in Baghdad.

Strategic Focus: The Development Road Project Primary Agenda: Fast-tracking execution phases of the multi-billion-dollar Development Road project, an international rail and highway network linking Grand Faw Port in southern Iraq directly to Turkey and European commercial markets.

Diplomatic Context: The visit serves as a key logistical precursor ahead of Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s upcoming official state visit to Turkey scheduled for July 28, 2026.

The visit underscores the massive economic weight and trade synergy between the two neighboring nations:

Heavy Commercial Volume: Bilateral trade volume between Iraq and Turkey stands at approximately $15 billion to $17 billion annually, with joint diplomatic initiatives aiming to expand total trade to $24 billion.

Key Trading Partner: Iraq consistently ranks among Turkey’s top export destinations globally (exceeding $12 billion in Turkish exports alone), primarily spanning food products, construction materials, machinery, and consumer goods.

Infrastructure Footprint: Turkish construction firms have historically undertaken over 1,100 development projects in Iraq valued at more than $36 billion, making Iraq one of the largest markets for Turkish engineering and infrastructure expertise worldwide.

By coordinating transport routes and cross-border digital networks through the Development Road project, both Baghdad and Ankara aim to secure long-term transit revenue, streamline regional supply chains, and further integrate their high-volume trade partnership.

World.title: National Security Service foils clandestine drone manufacturing cell in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s National Security Service (NSS) announced on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, the successful disruption of a clandestine operation attempting to manufacture unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) inside the capital city of Baghdad.

Executed under the direct supervision of the Judge of the Third Investigative Court, the intelligence-led raid resulted in the arrest of three primary suspects and the seizure of a makeshift production facility.

In an official statement and accompanied by video documentation of the tactical operation, the NSS confirmed that its specialized intelligence units executed judicial arrest and search warrants following precise surveillance.

The security sweep uncovered an active workshop equipped with 25 prefabricated drone airframes, along with specialized carbon fiber sheets, custom molds, and technical assembly tools utilized in the production and fabrication of long-range drones.

Seizure Inventory & Intelligence Breakdown

Arrests: 3 primary suspects apprehended under judicial warrants issued by the Third Investigative Court.

Drone Airframes: 25 completed and semi-completed UAV structural fuselages.

Manufacturing Materials: Industrial-grade carbon fiber panels, custom molds, and precision technical tooling.

Status: Disrupted prior to final assembly and operational deployment.

Ongoing Probe: Investigations are actively expanding to determine potential linkages between the illicit workshop, regional factional networks, or broader national security threats.

The NSS emphasized that the covert operation was completely dismantled before the manufactured drones could reach operational completion or be integrated into regional flight networks.

Legal proceedings have been initiated, and the suspects remain in federal custody as investigators work to identify supply chains and potential organizational ties before referring the perpetrators to the judiciary.

World.title: Iraq receives second batch of equipment for Nasiriyah International Airport
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq has received a second shipment of ground support equipment for Nasiriyah International Airport as building progresses, bringing the long-awaited facility closer to becoming operational.

The Ministry of Transport stated that the equipment arrived following an initial delivery in June and is part of the airport’s ongoing preparations for its opening.

Airport Director Ali Al-Ghurabi stated that the latest shipment includes commercial vehicles and operational equipment required to support aircraft and passenger services once the airport is operational.

The equipment will offer the necessary ground handling and technical support capabilities for international airport operations, assisting in the facility’s preparation for commercial flights, he added.

The airport is one of several transportation infrastructure projects being developed by Iraq as the government seeks to modernize its aviation sector, improve regional connectivity, and spur economic development beyond the country’s oil industry.

Baghdad has increased investment in airports, ports, and trains as part of a larger goal to improve transportation linkages, boost commerce and tourism, and establish Iraq as a regional logistical center linking the Gulf to Europe and Asia.

World.title: Washington approves Iraqi proposal to mediate between US and Iran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US President Donald Trump has approved Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s proposal to mediate between the United States and Iran.

This diplomatic breakthrough is intended to diffuse the current crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, according to local news outlet Channel 8 News.

During their recent meeting in Washington, al-Zaidi asked Trump for approval to establish an official Iraqi mediation effort between the United States and Iran.

Trump authorized al-Zaidi to undertake the plan as part of attempts to address the continuing Strait of Hormuz issue.

According to insiders, the mediation would focus on restoring stability to marine shipping and energy flows across the key canal.

Al-Zaidi informed Trump that, while Pakistan has been involved in political and diplomatic discussions, Iraq plans to lead the economic track of mediation.

The Iraqi effort will look for answers to interruptions in commercial shipping and oil shipments via the Strait of Hormuz, which have led to a broader global energy and economic crisis.

According to reports, al-Zaidi plans to visit Tehran on Thursday for a series of high-level talks. He and the accompanying Iraqi officials are anticipated to return to Baghdad later that day.

World.title: Iraq receives Chinese-built ferries for Arab Gulf routes
World.content:
Basra (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq has received a fleet of Chinese-built passenger boats and ferries to be deployed on new maritime routes connecting the country to Arab Gulf states, as part of Baghdad’s efforts to modernize its transportation network and strengthen regional connectivity.

According to Iraq’s Ministry of Transport, the fleet consists of 15 tourist boats, two passenger ferries capable of transporting 200 people each, and a bigger multi-purpose ferry that can transport 500 passengers and 80 vehicles every journey.

The warships will run maritime routes between Iraq and Arab Gulf nations, simplifying passenger travel while promoting commerce and tourism, according to the government.

The acquisition is part of Iraq’s overall strategy to modernize its maritime transport infrastructure and diversify its economy by expanding regional transportation links beyond its road and air networks.

According to the ministry, the new fleet would boost passenger and vehicle capacity while offering safer and more effective transportation services as regional travel demand increases.

The investment comes after Iraq announced several transportation projects, including the near completion of a new marina on the Shatt al-Arab waterway and continued development of the Grand Faw Port, as Baghdad seeks to strengthen its position as a regional transportation and logistics hub.

World.title: Iraq to open new marina for 50 boats on Shatt al-Arab
World.content:
Basra (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is approaching completion of its biggest marina on the Shatt al-Arab waterway, which the government believes would stimulate tourism and upgrade the country’s waterfront infrastructure.

Ahmed Jassim, Director General of the state-owned General Company for Maritime Transport, said that the marina is under development and would be able to accommodate up to 50 boats once finished.

According to Jassim, the marina would have international-standard tourist and recreational amenities, as well as a helicopter landing pad and associated infrastructure, making it Iraq’s first of its sort.

He described the development as one of the Ministry of Transport’s flagship projects, stating that it will be inaugurated in the coming months.

The marina, located on the Shatt al-Arab in the southern city of Basra, is part of Iraq’s larger attempts to improve transportation and tourist infrastructure, as the government wants to diversify the economy beyond oil and attract private investment in the hospitality and leisure sectors.

The initiative comes as Baghdad ramps up investment in ports, logistics, and waterfront projects to cement Iraq’s position as a regional transportation center while also offering new chances for tourist and economic growth.

World.title: Halliburton wins Iraq contract to develop Bin Umar and Sindbad oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Halliburton has signed a deal with Iraq’s Basra Oil Company (BOC) to assist in the development of the Bin Umar and Sindbad oil and gas fields in southern Iraq, bolstering Baghdad’s efforts to increase crude output and decrease dependency on imported natural gas.

According to the deal, Halliburton will offer integrated field management services, as well as engineering, procurement, and construction management for the two fields.

The project involves field development planning, production optimization, digital technologies, and project management, all with the goal of speeding development and enhancing operational efficiency.

Halliburton announced that it will use its Landmark digital platform to integrate subsurface data, drilling, production operations, and business planning.

According to BOC, the initial five-year phase of the Bin Umar expansion could enhance oil output to over 150,000 barrels per day and collect around 300 million standard cubic feet of associated gas, which would be utilized to help fulfill Iraq’s domestic energy demands.

The project is part of Iraq’s wider aim to increase oil production while capturing associated gas that is now burned, decreasing reliance on gas imports to run the country’s power sector and boosting energy security.

BOC will own and operate both fields, while Halliburton will provide technical expertise and project management in collaboration with the state-owned company.

Halliburton also stated that it intends to collaborate with local resources to support workforce development and national value creation initiatives within Iraq’s Ministry of Oil.

The award is the most recent in a string of energy investments announced by Iraq as it attempts to modernize its oil and gas industry, boost production capacity, and recruit foreign expertise to utilize its huge hydrocarbon resources while enhancing the usage of associated gas.

World.title: Arunachal's draft electoral roll shrinks by nearly 20% after SIR
World.content:
Election Commission

NEW DELHI: Arunachal Pradeshâs electorate has shrunk by almost one-fifth in the draft electoral roll published on Tuesday as part of the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise.Only 80.9% electors in the border state submitted their enumeration forms, while the remaining 19.1% were marked as permanently shifted, absent, dead or enrolled at more than one place.The draft roll of the state â which borders China â published on Tuesday has a total 7.18 lakh electors, as against 8.9 lakh electors on June 2, 2026, when SIR Phase 3 was announced. As many as 78,980 electors (8.9%) were marked as permanently shifted, 54,678 (6.2%) as absent or untraceable, 25,573 as dead (2.9%) and 5,281 (0.6%) as others (not willing to be enrolled for some reason of other).As per the Arunachal chief electoral officer (CEO), genuine electors can still be added back to the rolls during the claims and objection period from July 21 to August 20. These claims/objections will be disposed of by Septmber 18 and the final rolls of the state published on September 22.

World.title: Watch: Rahul Gandhi dragged away, forcibly removed from protest site; pics show nosebleed
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress on Tuesday released videos showing dramatic scenes of detentions of senior party leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra during partyâs âChalo PM Houseâ protest outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence over the NEET issue.

The videos captured the moments when police moved in to clear the protest outside the Prime Minister's residence.

In one video shared by the Congress on its official X handle, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi was seen lying on the road while police personnel attempted to lift him and remove him from the protest site.

Former Congress president appeared to resist being taken away as security officials surrounded him and tried to carry him from the spot.

The party also released photograph showing Gandhi with what appeared to be a nosebleed following the police action.

In a separate video, he can be seen lying down during the protest and talking to reporters, taunting the government by saying, "Democracy in India is happening right now."

Another video released by the party showed Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra standing at the entrance of a police bus and refusing to board it.





Officials are seen pulling her inside the vehicle as she resisted being detained.

The Congress also shared several photographs on its official social media handles showing Rahul Gandhi and other party leaders being removed by police during the protest.

The Congress has presented the videos and photographs as evidence of the manner in which its senior leaders were detained during the protest.

How the protest unfolded

Delhi Police forcibly removed and detained Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and several other opposition leaders after they staged a sit-in outside the Prime Minister's residence.

Rahul Gandhi, along with Congress leaders including the chief ministers of Karnataka and Kerala, began the protest at around 3.30 pm against the police action on students protesting the previous day.

The protest came after Congress leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, met students injured during Monday's clashes linked to the CJP-led march over the NEET issue.

The Congress has been demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and a discussion on the NEET issue in Parliament.

The party has also sought justice for students injured during the police action.

Government's response

Meanwhile, Union minister of state in the Prime Minister's Office Jitendra Singh said he met Rahul Gandhi at the protest site along with Union home secretary Govind Mohan and urged him to end the sit-in.

Singh claimed Rahul Gandhi initially agreed to withdraw the protest if the government allowed a discussion on the NEET issue in Parliament.

He alleged that after the government conveyed its willingness to hold the discussion, Gandhi added a fresh demand seeking the resignation of the education minister. Singh described the Congress leader's conduct as "unfortunate and contrary to every norm of democracy."

Congress leaders, however, have maintained that they were protesting against the alleged police action on students and accused the government of refusing to address the issue in Parliament.

World.title: 'Rahul wanted a confrontation': Jitendra Singh details fallout of talks with Congress leader
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union minister Jitendra Singh accused the opposition leader Rahul Gandhi of shifting his demands during talks over the Congress protest at Lok Kalyan Marg outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence, alleging that the Congress leader was more interested in "confrontation" than resolving the issue through dialogue.

Speaking to news agency ANI, Singh said he and Union home secretary Govind Mohan were deputed by the government to meet senior Congress leaders after they began a sit-in protest at a location that, according to him, was not designated for demonstrations and was causing inconvenience to the public.

"It was learned that Congress Party National President Mallikarjun Kharge and other senior leaders like Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and other had suddenly started a protest.

It was also reported that the place was not very conducive to a sit-in protest. It was causing significant inconvenience to the public," he said.

The minister said the government sent the two officials to persuade the Congress leaders to shift the discussion to Parliament instead of continuing the protest.

According to Singh, Rahul told them he would immediately end the sit-in if the government agreed to hold a discussion in Parliament on the NEET issue and related education matters.





"Discussions were held with the top leadership of the government, and we were told to assure them on behalf of the government that the government has no objection. The government is ready to discuss NEET in Parliament, both related issues and the ongoing protests," Singh said.

However, Singh alleged that Rahul then introduced a new condition, demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

The Union minister said he told the Congress leader that "changing the goalpost" was unfair, but Gandhi maintained that it was his prerogative.

Singh further alleged that despite the government's willingness to discuss the issue, Rahul Gandhi insisted on continuing the protest. He further alleged that despite the government's willingness to discuss the issue, Rahul Gandhi insisted on continuing the protest.

"It's very unfortunate that the LoP behaves this way, changing his stance so quickly. This means he's in a mood of conflict. He doesn't want to cooperate with the government to discuss or advance public interest issues. They've come with the intention of confrontation, conflict, and finding an issue," Singh said.

Congress party launched a protest outside PM's residence demanding education minister's resignation over the NEET paper leak case.

This comes a day after massive 'Sansad Chalo' march by the Cockroach Janta Party. Rahul also called for people to join the protest.

"An attack on students is an attack on every Indian family. Prime Minister Modi thinks he can escape without giving answers, without facing any consequences - he won't be able to, not at all this time. I appeal to every patriotic Indian who believes that our students should get justice - join our dharna in front of the Prime Minister's residence," he said.

"The voice of India's students cannot be ignored. An attack on students is an attack on every Indian family. PM Modi believes he can get away without answers, without consequences. He cannot. Not this time. I ask every patriotic Indian who believes our students deserve justice - join us in dharna in front of the Prime Ministerâs residence. The voice of Indiaâs students will not be ignored," he added.

Meanwhile, the CJP protest continued at the Jantar Mantar with top political leaders like Sharad Pawar, Arvind Kejriwal, Atishi, Supriya Sule joining the protest.

World.title: 70% of electricity consumed during April-June quarter came from thermal energy
World.content:
Representational image

NEW DELHI: Even as the share of renewable energy (RE) in the power mix has steadily increased, thermal power continues to remain the mainstay, with 70% of the electricity consumed in the country during the April-June quarter coming from coal-based plants.During the non-solar peak-demand hours, the share of coal-based generation reached a maximum of 75%, minister of state for power Shripad Yesso Naik informed Rajya Sabha.The share of renewable energy has increased significantly over the last few years, with solar, wind, nuclear and hydro together accounting for over 54% of Indiaâs total installed capacity of 548.8 gigawatts. Wind and solar energy set a record earlier this month, generating more than 100 GW together. While the high penetration of variable RE is a reason to rejoice, it is coal-based thermal power that carries the bulk of the load when solar energy is not available and wind intensity drops.With 230.8 GW of installed capacity, the maximum generation achieved from coal- and lignite-based thermal power plants was about 188.8 GW in the first quarter of FY27. While 9.5 GW of thermal capacity was added in 2025-26, the minister informed that 2.3 GW had been commissioned during the current fiscal.The minister also said that, as on July 12, 42.8 million tonne of coal stock was available at thermal power plants, sufficient for 14 days at an 85% plant load factor. He added that sufficient coal was being received by thermal power plants to meet the daily requirement and that a joint committee of the ministries of power, railways and coal was monitoring supplies on a daily basis.Responding to a separate question, the minister informed Parliament that 11 pumped storage projects with an aggregate installed capacity of 15.8 GW were under construction, while another six, with an aggregate installed capacity of 8.2 GW, had received concurrence from the Central Electricity Authority.

World.content:
Opposition unites for CJP demands

Which political parties are protesting

What govt said

NEW DELHI: Several opposition parties came out in support of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s protest againt paper leak of NEET-UG and other competitive exams and their demand for the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.The central government responded but the talks did not work out. PM and HM must resign for destroying the future of Indiaâs youth," Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X.Aam Aadmi Party chief Arvind Kejriwal and leader Atishi joined the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar.Moreover, NCP(SP) chief Sharad Pawar and Lok Sabha member Supriya Sule also joined the protesters.Trinamool Congress (TMC) chief Mamata Banerjee expressed the willingness to join the protests in Delhi if the need arises while also calling for INDIA bloc unity."We supported CJP from the beginning. If need be, I will visit Delhi and join their protest," ANI quoted her as saying."The time has come to be united under the umbrella of the INDIA Alliance against the BJP. I request all parties of the nation and the entire country, and in Bengal also," she added.Samajwadi Party (SP) MP Dimple Yadav was one of the major political leaders who actively participated in the protest on Monday.Questioning the police action against the protesters, Yadav said: "These children had come all the way to the Parliament building because they wanted to tell the government that your system has fallen ill, it is not working. Those innocent children were beaten with batons, the daughters' clothes were torn."The central government has not responded to the demands of the resignations yet. However, talks were held with the CJP and the opposition to pacify the protests.Union minister Jitendra Singh reached Lok Kalyan Marg and spoke with Rahul Gandhi over Congress's protest.Singh later informed that the Centre had agreed to Rahul's initial demand to hold discussions in the Parliament over NEET irregularities, but the opposition leader later back-tracked from his demand and also demanded for education minister's resignation."Shri Rahul Gandhi put forward the demand that if the government agrees to discuss in Parliament all issues related to NEET and the associated movement, he would immediately end his sit-in. Within a few moments, after taking permission from the government's top leadership, Shri Rahul Gandhi was assured that his demand has been accepted, and the government is ready to discuss in Parliament all issues related to NEET and the associated movement," he said."When this information was conveyed to Shri Rahul Gandhi, he said that he would not agree to this alone but also sought assurance for the resignation of the Union Education Minister. He said that now I have two demands: discussion in Parliament and the resignation of the Union Education Minister. When he was reminded that earlier he had only demanded discussion, he said that now my demands have changed. When an attempt was made to humbly explain to him that for a senior leader like him to backtrack from his word so quickly does not befit him, he said that it is his prerogative. When the Home Secretary tried to explain that this site is not suitable for a sit-in, his response was that it is also his prerogative to sit wherever he wants," he said.Union minister JP Nadda also held talks with the protesters on Monday when the CJP submitted its demands."This morning, for the first time, a proposal came from the protesters to hold talks with the government, and our discussions have been ongoing since 11.50am. The meeting took place in a cordial atmosphere. An initial verbal discussion was held in detail with their delegation, and they submitted a written petition to me around 4pm. I have requested all the protesters to end their sit-in and assist the administration in restoring normalcy," Nadda said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the government acted firmly against those behind the NEET paper leak to safeguard students' futures, urging states to work with the Centre to eliminate the menace in the national interest. The remarks came at a meeting of the NDA MPs on Tuesday."At the same time, the prime minister said, to ensure that students' future was not affected, the NEET re-examination was given priority, conducted successfully, and the results were declared without delay," Union minister Kiren Rijiju said after the meeting.Protests continued at Jantar Mantar as hundreds of students and their supporters returned to Jantar Mantar a day after their march to Parliament, saying the alleged use of force by police had only reinforced their determination to press on with the agitation.The protest site remained crowded through the afternoon, with students, parents and supporters raising slogans over the alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG examination and reiterating their demand for education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.

World.title: CJP removes spokesperson Vijeta Dahiya, condemns 'deeply insensitive actions'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party has removed its spokesperson Vijeta Dahiya after viral videos surfaced showing him during the police crackdown on protesters at Jantar Mantar, calling his conduct "deeply insensitive" and "unacceptable.

"

"We strongly condemn the deeply insensitive actions of our spokesperson Vijeta Dahiya, whose videos surfaced while peaceful protestors and our team were facing brutal police violence. Such conduct is unacceptable, shows a complete lack of judgment, and is wholly inconsistent with the values and principles of our movement," the party said in a statement.

Dahiya has been removed as spokesperson and relieved of all official duties, the party said.

Controversial viral video

The clip, which went viral on social media, showed Dahiya at a burger outlet in a mall near the protest site. A group of people can be heard confronting him and questioning why he wasn't with the protesters, asking: "You were eating a burger while we were protesting?"

The exact timing of the video and the circumstances in which it was recorded could not be independently verified.

In an Instagram video addressing the backlash, Dahiya said he had been working continuously for the movement for around one and a half months and had barely slept for the past two nights.





He questioned why eating a burger had become such a major issue. In the caption, he also made a comment stating that: âBy the way, I didnt eat the burger, because I felt that it has maida and transfats, and maybe I should eat elsewhere.â

"No one pays me to participate in the protest," he said, adding that he was doing what he was doing for the country. "Yes, I will eat the burger," he said.

Before this incident Dahiya had also come under fire on social media for his views on transgender people and stating that most women are 'not political'.

The move comes as the CJP continues its protest at Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged examination irregularities. Police had earlier resorted to a baton charge and detained several protesters during a march to Parliament on Monday.

World.content:
July 21, 2026 12:37

Ensure hospitals remain solely for healthcare, not detention: Safdarjung Hospital RDA writes to President

The Resident Doctors’ Association of Vardhman Mahavir Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital have urged President Droupadi Murmu to safeguard patient rights, citing reports that climate activist Sonam Wangchuk was allegedly not allowed to avail Leave Against Medical Advice (LAMA) despite being a “competent patient”.

In a representation submitted on Monday (July 20, 2026), the Resident Doctors’ Association (RDA) said that if the reports were accurate, they raised serious concerns regarding informed consent, personal liberty and constitutional rights.

It asserted that hospitals are institutions of healing and should not be perceived as places of detention except where restrictions are expressly authorised by law and carried out in accordance with due process.

The association sought the President’s intervention to uphold constitutional rights, medical ethics, patient autonomy and the independence of public healthcare institutions, besides demanding an independent inquiry into the reported events at Jantar Mantar, where Mr. Wangchuk and his supporters were protesting before he was forcefully shifted to Safdarjung Hospital.

The association expressed “deep concern” over Wangchuk’s continued hospitalisation.

“While Wangchuk’s medical condition and the necessity of his continued hospitalisation remain matters of independent clinical judgment, every individual admitted to a hospital is, first and foremost, entitled to be treated as a patient with dignity, compassion, and in accordance with established medical ethics and the Constitution of India,” the representation said.

The RDA also expressed concern over the “extraordinary security arrangements” at Safdarjung Hospital during Wangchuk’s stay.

It referred to reports and publicly available visuals showing restricted access to hospital areas, sealing off portions of the building, deployment of extensive security personnel across multiple floors and restrictions on routine hospital operations.

“If such measures resulted in the disruption of patient care, impeded access to healthcare services, or created an environment in which a hospital appeared to function as an extension of law enforcement rather than a place of healing, the matter warrants independent examination,” it said.

“Hospitals are institutions of healing and must not be perceived as places of detention except where such restriction is expressly authorised by law and carried out in accordance with due process,” it said.

The RDA sought measures to ensure that public hospitals remain dedicated solely to healthcare and not perceived to be utilised for non-medical purposes.

It called for an examination of whether the security arrangements within Safdarjung Hospital were proportionate and whether they adversely affected patient care, hospital functioning and access to medical services.

The association also voiced anguish over reports of the use of force against peaceful demonstrators at Jantar Mantar, saying that such incidents, if established, risk eroding public confidence in constitutional institutions and creating an atmosphere of fear among citizens, including members of the medical fraternity.

It also urged protection for healthcare professionals, faculty members, medical students, resident doctors and citizens exercising their constitutional rights peacefully from intimidation, violence or misuse of authority.

The association concluded by urging steps to restore transparency, institutional independence and public confidence in the healthcare system.

“As resident doctors at one of the nation’s largest public hospitals, we reaffirm our unwavering commitment to our patients and to upholding the constitutional values that govern our Republic,” the representation said.

It expressed hope that the President’s timely intervention would reinforce public confidence in constitutional institutions and reaffirm that hospitals remain places of healing, dignity, compassion and justice.

- PTI

World.title: Arun Nehru draws attention of Centre on problems faced by maize, cotton farmers
World.content:
Perambalur MP Arun Nehru on Tuesday drew the attention of the Central Government in the Lok Sabha regarding the problems faced by farmers cultivating major crops including maize, paddy and cotton in his constituency.

Highlighting the issues, he sought an explanation on whether the government had conducted any studies on them. He also questioned whether any steps have not been taken so far to provide quality seeds, fertilizers, easy credit facilities, technical advice, and solid market opportunities.

In his response, Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Ramnath Thakur said that the Centre was implementing a 100% centrally funded Central Sector Scheme known as the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) across various States and Union Territories to provide concessional interest rates on short-term agricultural loans obtained by farmers through Kisan Credit Cards (KCC) for their working capital requirements.

The Department of Agriculture, Tamil Nadu, had also informed that there were two regulated markets functioning in Perambalur with necessary infrastructure facilities including two storage warehouses with a capacity of 3000 metric tonnes each, one transaction shed and one drying yard. Perambalur Regulated Market had also been integrated with the National Agriculture Market (e-NAM), allowing local farmers, especially of maize and shallots, to bid their produce to a wider network of traders.

The Minister further said that direct procurement centres for paddy and maize were set up by the state government during harvest seasons to ensure Minimum Support Prices (MSP) along with state incentives. For maize, the major maize-producing (surplus) districts had been mapped with nearby grain-based distilleries and poultry feed manufacturing units to strengthen market linkages and facilitate efficient procurement.

Mr. Arun Nehru said that all the government’s schemes to improve the livelihood of Perambalur farmers should be fully implemented on the ground and they should not be just on paper. The Central government should ensure that all the benefits announced to the farmers reach them without delay.

World.title: Telangana TET for in-service teachers to be held in September
World.content:
The Department of School Education has issued an exclusive notification to conduct the Telangana Teachers’ Eligibility Test (TET) for in-service teachers.

Only teachers in all government, local body schools, residential, welfare societies, model schools and government departments are eligible to apply.

The computer-based test will be conducted from September 7 to 11. The applications window for the test is online and will be open from July 22 to 29. The results are proposed to be released by the end of September.

The notification for in-service teachers and other details is available on ‘https://schooledu.telangana.gov.in/’. Additional queries can be cleared from 7093958881 (domain), 7032901383 (technical), and 7093708883 (TGTET office).

World.title: Pudukottai Collector reviews government facilities under ‘Ungalai Thedi, Ungal Ooril’ initiative
World.content:
Pudukkottai District Collector M. Aruna on Tuesday reviewed various government facilities at Thirumayam block as part of the ‘Ungalai Thedi, Ungal Ooril’ initiative.

Ms. Aruna inspected the Chief Minister’s Breakfast Scheme at Chidambaram Chettiar Memorial Higher Secondary School and assessed the quality of food served to students. She also verified attendance records maintained under the scheme.

She later inspected a newly constructed sub-health centre at Kottur, built at a cost of ₹45 lakh under the 15th Finance Commission grant. At the Primary Health Centre in Nachandupatti, she interacted with pregnant women undergoing treatment, enquired about the availability of medical services and medicines, and reviewed the overall functioning and cleanliness of the facility.

As part of the initiative, senior officials from various departments carried out inspections at government offices, schools, hospitals, anganwadi centres, hostels, orphanages and public infrastructure facilities, including drinking water supply, sanitation, solid waste management, roads and street lighting.

Later, Ms. Aruna chaired a review meeting with officials at Thirumayam. During the meeting, officials submitted reports on their field inspections and details of public grievances received during their visits. She instructed officials to upload all public petitions received during the inspections to the Chief Minister’s grievance portal without delay and provide time-bound redressal to the public.

World.title: Panchayats propose single-window forest clearances, insurance cover and AI-based alerts to mitigate human-wildlife conflicts
World.content:
Local bodies in Kerala have urged the State government to develop master plans for mitigating human-wildlife conflicts based on accurate ground-level data.

A single-window system for forest-related permits, joint coordination committees for forest panchayats, and formulating disaster management protocols are also among the key suggestions mooted by panchayat representatives at a joint meeting of local-self government institution members and the Forest department in Thiruvananthapuram to discuss a coordinated strategy to address the growing human-wildlife conflicts across the State.

The participants recommended steps such as fencing, trenching and other physical barriers wherever feasible, besides improving habitat conditions within forests by ensuring adequate water sources and food availability for wildlife.

Highlighting the developmental challenges faced by settlements in and around forests, local body representatives urged the government to expedite approvals for essential infrastructure such as roads, drinking water projects and electricity connections.

Office-bearers of the Kerala Grama Panchayat Association also sought special financial assistance for losses caused by wild animals, including crop damage, attacks on livestock and destruction of houses. They also called for a government-backed insurance scheme covering agriculture, livestock and homes of people residing in forest-fringe regions.

Among the technological interventions proposed were AI- and SMS-based early warning systems to alert residents about potential wildlife threats. The meeting also called for a special integrated development package for panchayats with forest areas, covering residents living inside forests, along forest boundaries and in nearby habitations.

There were also calls to introduce a rehabilitation mechanism under the Rebuild Kerala Initiative for those residing in forest-fringe areas. The government has also been urged to acquire such land, provide compensation, and implement a time-bound rehabilitation programme for consenting families.

World.title: Kumkis to be deployed to reduce elephant-human conflict in Manyam
World.content:
The Andhra Pradesh Forest Department is making arrangements to shift two trained Kumki elephants — Jayanth and Abhimanyu — from the Palamaner camp to the Parvathipuram-Manyam district as part of measures to mitigate the growing human-elephant conflict in the region. The move comes following directions from Deputy Chief Minister and Minister for Forests and Environment K. Pawan Kalyan.

The jumbo Jayanth, has undergone specialised training at the State’s Nanniyal elephant camp, while Abhimanyu, brought from Karnataka, will be relocated from the Musalimadugu camp, near Palamaner, to the Guchchimi camp in Parvathipuram-Manyam district.

According to the Forest Department, both the elephants have extensive experience in controlling wild elephants and have successfully participated in six major operations.

Most recently, Jayanth and Abhimanyu played a key role in capturing a solitary male wild elephant near Palamaner. They have been selected for deployment in the Manyam district based on their coordination and proven operational performance.

Officials said: “The move is intended to provide immediate relief to residents of villages along the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha border, where herds of wild elephants frequently enter into human habitation, damaging crops and property, and posing a threat to local communities.”

Forest officials say that recurring elephant incursions in Parvathipuram-Manyam district to habitat fragmentation, shrinking forest cover, and shortage of food and water in the neighbouring forest areas.

World.title: A.P. unveils White Paper on irrigation; ₹35,555-crore plan to complete 36 projects by 2028
World.content:
Andhra Pradesh Water Resources Minister Nimmala Ramanaidu has released a White Paper on the irrigation sector, outlining the State government’s plan to complete 36 major irrigation projects with an estimated investment of ₹35,555 crore by December 2028.

Addressing the media on Tuesday, the Minister said the government had spent ₹24,611 crore on irrigation over the past two years, including ₹12,484 crore on projects in Rayalaseema.

“An irrigation action calendar has been introduced to accelerate project execution,” he said.

Claiming that the coalition government had inherited a ‘devastated irrigation sector’ and weak finances from the previous YSRCP government, he said that the government has restored momentum through a time-bound implementation strategy.

Describing the Polavaram Project as Andhra Pradesh’s lifeline, the Minister said 72 per cent of the project had been completed during the TDP’s previous tenure and claimed it would have been finished by 2021-22 had the government remained in power.

He alleged the YSRCP government had neglected the project for 17 months after assuming office in 2019, failed to fulfil the commitments made to displaced families and diverted Central funds released for the project.

Mr. Ramanaidu said the ECRF Dam, the project’s most critical component, had achieved 31 per cent completion, while right and left canal connectivity works were progressing round the clock. The coalition government had paid ₹2,250 crore towards rehabilitation and compensation for project-displaced families in the last two years and spent ₹1,050 crore on the Polavaram Left Main Canal, with the aim of supplying water to Anakapalli district by July 2026.

Referring to the Veligonda Project, Mr. Ramanaidu criticised the previous government for dedicating an incomplete project, noting that while it spent ₹981 crore in five years, the present government had already spent ₹1,108.12 crore in two years.

He also announced completion of Phase I and II of the Handri Neeva Sujala Sravanthi Project within 100 days for ₹3,870 crore. “The White Paper reflects the government’s strategy to complete long-pending irrigation projects and improve water availability across Andhra Pradesh,” he said.

World.title: Priests block road in Srirangam
World.content:
Priests, who perform rituals and pujas at the bathing ghat at Amma Mandapam in Srirangam, on Tuesday staged a road roko on Amma Mandapam road, protesting against the reported move to remove them from the facility.

There are about 200 priests, who visit Amma Mandapam daily, to perform rituals on behalf of their clients. The priests perform rituals at their respective bases at the mandapam, which attracts hundreds of devotees across the State and neighbouring States to offer ‘tharpanam’ to their forefathers.

According to sources, the officials of Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple had brought a large number of measurement stones and placed them at the bases of the priests a few days ago. The officials reportedly attempted to measure the area, claiming that it belonged to the temple.

Claiming it was an attempt to dislodge them from the mandapam, the priests staged the road roko. On information, the police arrived at the spot and held a negotiation with the protesters. Since they refused to budge, the police removed them from the spot. The protest disrupted vehicle movements on the road for about 30 minutes.

Important topics and their relevance in UPSC CSE exam for July 21, 2026. If you missed the July 20, 2026 UPSC CSE exam key from the Indian Express, read it here

Front Page

Indus Waters Treaty: Govt focus on Chenab projects, renegotiation

Syllabus:

Preliminary Examination: Current events of national and international importance.

Mains Examination: General Studies II: India and its neighbourhood- relations.



What’s the ongoing story: A year after India put the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) “in abeyance” following the Pahalgam terror attack, it is pushing for speedy development of hydropower projects on the Chenab with a combined capacity of over 5,000 megawatts and renegotiation of the six-decade-old pact, government sources said.

Key Points to Ponder:

• What does keeping the Indus Waters treaty ‘in abeyance’ mean?

• Know the significance of the Indus Waters Treaty in the context of India-Pakistan relations.



• Examine the legal mechanisms provided within the Indus Waters Treaty for dispute resolution.

• Assess the challenges and opportunities that arise from the construction of hydroelectric projects in shared river basins, with specific reference to the Indus River system.

• Since it was signed in 1960, what has the Indus Waters Treaty meant for India?

• What does keeping the Indus Waters treaty ‘in abeyance’ mean?

• When the treaty is renegotiated, what changes should India ask for?

• The Indus originates in Tibet. Should India be concerned about China’s interference while it resolves the river issue with Pakistan?

Key Takeaways:

• According to sources, the government has assessed that the pact has outlived its utility and is ready to renegotiate it with Pakistan to make it more balanced. “IWT, in its present form, cannot function again,” said a top source. Pakistan, sources said, has not shown any signs of ending cross-border terrorism against India — a pre-condition for resuming cooperation under the IWT.

• For any future reactivation of the river water-sharing provisions, the treaty would need to be renegotiated in a modified format — a step that remains contingent on Islamabad permanently halting its support for terrorism directed against India, sources said.

• The Indian Express has learnt that Delhi’s key priority is the speedy completion of hydropower projects on the Chenab — 1,856 MW Sawalkote Hydroelectric Project, 1,000 MW Pakal Dul Project, 850 MW Ratle Project, 624 MW Kiru Project, and 540 MW Kwar Project.

• While the Kiru and Pakal projects are expected to be completed by the end of this year, the remaining are expected to be completed in the next two-three years, sources said.

• These projects are critical for India’s clean energy transition, grid stability and regional development, and will substantially enhance India’s hydropower capacity while enabling the fuller utilisation of its legitimate rights under the Indus basin, said sources.

• “Together with accelerated hydropower development and modern basin management, these initiatives will ensure that India’s legitimate share of the Indus waters is utilised efficiently, sustainably and in accordance with its long-term developmental, water security and clean energy objectives,” sources said.

Do You Know:

• The IWT guides the distribution of the waters of the Indus and its tributaries between India and Pakistan. Now, the IWT itself states that the treaty cannot be altered unilaterally. Article XII of the IWT says that the treaty can only be terminated “by a duly ratified treaty concluded for that purpose between the two Governments”. The article also says that it “may from time to time be modified by a duly ratified treaty concluded for that purpose between the two Governments”.

• The term “hold in abeyance” is not recognised in international law, and it does not find a mention in the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties of 1969 (VCLT), a multilateral treaty which regulates treaties among nations.

• The VCLT recognises circumstances for “termination” or “suspension” of treaties. Article 62 states that “fundamental change of circumstances” may be ground for terminating a treaty under some conditions.

• The Indus treaty has endured for almost 65 years, sharing the waters of the Indus river system — the ‘Eastern Rivers’, namely Sutlej, Beas and Ravi, for India, and the ‘Western Rivers’ of Indus, Jhelum, and Chenab for Pakistan.

• India is constructing two hydroelectric power projects—the Kishenganga HE project on Kishenganga river, a tributary of Jhelum, and the Ratle Hydroelectric project on Chenab river.

• Pakistan has objected to the construction of these two projects. In 2015, Pakistan requested the appointment of a Neutral Expert to examine its technical objections to India’s Kishenganga and Ratle Hydro Electric Projects (HEPs).

• In 2016, Pakistan unilaterally retracted this request and proposed that a Court of Arbitration adjudicate its objections. This unilateral action by Pakistan is in contravention of the graded mechanism of dispute settlement envisaged by Article IX of IWT.

India, Moldova discuss UNSC reforms, fight against terror

Syllabus:

Preliminary Examination: Current events of national and international importance.

Mains Examination: General Studies II: Important International institutions, agencies and fora- their structure, mandate.

What’s the ongoing story: INDIA AND Moldova discussed reforms of multilateral organisations, including the UN Security Council, and cooperation in the fight against terrorism, as President Droupadi Murmu landed in Chisinau on her state visit to the country. Murmu is the first Indian head of state to visit the landlocked Eastern European country since the establishment of diplomatic relations in 1992.

Key Points to Ponder:

• What is the relationship between India and Moldova?

• Know the significance of India’s diplomatic engagement with smaller countries such as Moldova in advancing its agenda on UNSC reforms and counter-terrorism

• Map Work-Moldova

• What is the Security Council?

• Non-permanent members and permanent members-compare and contrast

• Who are the 15 members of the UNSC?

• Is Security Council reform in any way moving forward?

• How does the Security Council determine the existence of any threat to the peace, breach of the peace, or act of aggression?

• Five permanent members ten non-permanent members-know in detail

• How Voting System works in United Nations Security Council

• Do You think that the veto power given to five permanent members of the UNSC should be abolished?

• On what basis was Security Council permanent membership granted?

• How are the non-permanent members of the Security Council selected?

• Are UN resolutions binding?

• Is Security Council reform in any way moving forward?

• What is the process for Security Council reform?

• How does the Security Council determine the existence of any threat to the peace, breach of the peace, or act of aggression?

Key Takeaways:

• The President held bilateral discussions with her Moldovan counterpart Maia Sandu, where the two leaders explored new avenues of cooperation in trade and investment, digital transformation, information technology, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, agriculture, education, culture and capacity building, according to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA).

• Briefing the media, MEA’s Secretary (West) Sibi George said, “They also discussed cooperation in (the) fight against terrorism. Both sides discussed (the) importance of reforms of multilateral organisations, including the UNSC.”

• As a special gesture of friendship, Murmu presented a bust of Mahatma Gandhi to President Sandu. The President laid a wreath at the Monument of Stefan cel Mare si Sfant (Stephen the Great), paying tribute to one of Moldova’s most revered national figures.

• As part of her day-long visit, Murmu met Igor Grosu, speaker of the Moldovan parliament, and interacted with members of the India-Moldova Parliamentary Friendship Group.

• Later, both Presidents jointly addressed the India-Moldova Business Forum, which brought together leading business representatives from both countries to explore fresh opportunities in trade, investment, innovation and technology.

• Both countries are also exploring cooperation in digital public infrastructure, innovation, food processing, logistics and skills development, creating significant potential for mutually beneficial investment, employment and sustainable growth, the MEA official added.

Do You Know:

• India’s outreach to Eastern Europe seeks to diversify its European engagement beyond major Western powers such as France and Germany. Over the next few days, President Murmu will also be visiting North Macedonia and Romania.

• Moldova, is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe. Moldova is bordered by Romania to the west and Ukraine to the north, east, and south. The unrecognised breakaway state of Transnistria lies across the Dniester river on the country’s eastern border with Ukraine. India all set to get its first dengue vaccine

Syllabus:

Preliminary Examination: Current events of national and international importance.

Mains Examination: General Studies II: Issues relating to development and management of Social Sector/Services relating to Health, Education, Human Resources.

What’s the ongoing story: The Drug Controller General of India (DCGI) has approved Japanese company Takeda Biopharmaceuticals India’s dengue vaccine, Qdenga, making it the first such vaccine to be greenlighted in India. It is designed to protect against all four dengue virus strains (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3 and DENV-4) and can be administered regardless of prior dengue exposure. It does not require pre-vaccination testing, the company said.

Key Points to Ponder:

• What is the vaccine about?

• What did clinical trials show?

• What is Dengue?

• Dengue is caused by what?

• What is the public health significance of the approval of India’s first dengue vaccine?

• Why dengue remains a major urban public health challenge in India?

• What is the importance of Integrated Vector Management in dengue prevention?

• Know the significance of the approval of Qdenga for India’s public health system.

Key Takeaways:

• The vaccine is administered subcutaneously. It comes as a two-dose regimen of 0.5 mL each, with doses given three months apart. The price has not been announced yet but since Takeda has entered into a manufacturing partnership with Hyderabad-based Biological E to produce up to 50 million doses annually, costs are expected to be competitive for the Indian market. Pricing will also depend on whether this gets incorporated into government immunisation programmes later.

• The approval comes at a critical time for public health, with reported dengue cases in India increasing 11-fold over the past two decades.

• India continues to account for nearly one-third of the global dengue burden. Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease that poses a significant global public health threat, with prevalence in over 125 countries. India accounts for nearly one-third of the global dengue burden.

• In an official statement issued today, Dr Mahender Nayak, head of Intercontinental Markets, Takeda, said, “Dengue is a growing public health challenge and India needs sustained, evidence-based prevention.” The latest seven-year data for Qdenga show continued protection against dengue infection and hospitalisation across all four serotypes — an important milestone for communities and health systems.” Since its launch in 2022, Qdenga has been approved in 43 countries, with more than 32 million doses distributed globally.

• Dr Goh Choo Beng, Medical Affairs Head, Southeast Asia and India Cluster, said, “India carries a substantial dengue burden, and all four dengue virus serotypes have been documented as co-circulating in several regions. The approval represents an important step in strengthening India’s comprehensive approach to dengue prevention, alongside vector control, surveillance, community awareness and other public health measures.”

Do You Know:

• It is designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It is approved for use in the four to 60 year age group, regardless of previous dengue exposure, without the need for pre-vaccination testing.It is the most extensively studied dengue vaccine, with long-term clinical data demonstrating sustained protection against dengue disease and dengue-related hospitalisation.

• The approval in India is based on results from Takeda’s global clinical development programme, involving 19 Phase 1, 2 and 3 clinical trials with over 28,000 participants in both endemic and non-endemic regions. This included the pivotal Phase III TIDES (DEN-301) trial, which evaluated the vaccine in over 20,000 participants across eight countries over an extended period to evaluate both the long-term safety and efficacy of QDENGA. At 12 months following the second dose, the study met its primary endpoint, demonstrating an overall vaccine efficacy of 80.2% against virologically confirmed dengue (VCD).

• The vaccine has also received WHO prequalification, confirming it meets global standards for quality, safety and efficacy, and enabling eligibility for procurement through international agencies such as UNICEF and PAHO to support wider access.

• In 2025, reported cases exceeded 113,000, but modelling analyses suggest the dengue burden in India appears to be higher than reported, likely representing tens of millions of infections each year.

What’s the ongoing story: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said they ​would impose a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, opening a potential new front against the United States in its war with Iran and raising the threat to global energy supplies and trade beyond the Gulf.

Key Points to Ponder:

• Who are the Houthis?

• Examine the strategic significance of Yemen in the geopolitical landscape of the Middle East

• The ‌escalation comes after one of the deadliest periods in the war for U.S. troops. The Pentagon on Monday identified two U.S. soldiers who were killed when Iran attacked an American base in Jordan on Friday, while they also said they had found unidentified remains that could be those of a third soldier reported as missing in action. Separately, a fourth service member was killed in northern Iraq during the “controlled detonation of unexploded ordnance from a downed Iranian one-way attack drone.”

• After the Houthis announced their blockade, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said in a statement that it would respond to them with force, and also that it began implementing protection measures for its ships moving through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key export route for Saudi oil after the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran’s Foreign Ministry ⁠said mediators had presented “proposals” to Tehran, signalling that diplomatic contacts remain active, but gave no details.

• Iran had been pressing the Houthis to close the Bab el-Mandeb gateway to the Red Sea if the U.S. continued to attack Iranian power infrastructure.

• A full closure of the strait would reduce global oil supply by 7% as it would leave most of Saudi oil exports unable to leave the region. The disruption would add to the huge cut to oil flows from the war in the Gulf, which has already reduced shipments by 10% of global supply.

Do You Know:

• The Iran-backed Houthi rebels who control northern Yemen have accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out airstrikes on the capital’s international airport on Monday, testing the ceasefire between the kingdom and the militant group.

• The government of Yemen said the strikes were carried out in order to prevent an Iranian plane from landing. But Houthis have vowed to retaliate for the strike as the incident marks the first such escalation between Houthis and Riyadh, AP reported.

• A Saudi-led coalition in Yemen has been fighting the Houthis in the north for a long time. Houthi official Brigadier General Yahya Saree said Saudi Arabia launched airstrikes on Monday, ending a period of “de-escalation”, adding that “this aggression will not go unanswered or unpunished.”

• The development comes after tensions flared between the two sides this month when the Houthis accused planes from Saudi Arabia of breaching their airspace to prevent an Iranian plane carrying a Houthi delegation to Tehran for the funeral of Iran’s former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Staging a protest: Rights, restrictions in the law

Syllabus:

Preliminary Examination: Current events of national and international importance.

Mains Examination: General Studies II: Indian Constitution—historical underpinnings, evolution, features, amendments, significant provisions and basic structure.

What’s the ongoing story: The police cracked down on the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and its supporters on Monday as thousands joined the planned march to Parliament. The gates of the Parliament complex have been shut.

Key Points to Ponder:

• Is staging a protest legal in India?

• What forms of protest are allowed

• What is barred?

• Is staging a protest at Parliament allowed?

• Right to protest-what Constitution of India guarantees?

• Under what laws is a protest permitted in India?

• What the SC has said over protests, and the limits on them?

• Who are Cockroach Janta party?

• How did the Cockroach Janta party emerge?

• Why Cockroach Janta party staging protests?

Key Takeaways:

• The government has also reached out to protesters, with CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das posting on X that they had met senior BJP leader JP Nadda and submitted a “written letter with our demands.”

Do You Know:

• The right to stage a protest is protected under the Fundamental Right to Freedom. Under Article 19 (1) (a) and (b), citizens have the right to “freedom of speech and expression”, and to “assemble peaceably and without arms.”

• However, these rights are subject to “reasonable restrictions” in the interests of “the sovereignty and integrity of India, the security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, decency or morality, or in relation to contempt of court, defamation or incitement to an offence.”

• Thus, while citizens have every right to organise a protest, it has to be done keeping the restrictions in mind. The general practice to regulate a protest in India has been to mark designated spots for it, make police permission mandatory, and impose prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (earlier Section 144 of the CrPC).

• At the 47th Session of the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva in 2021, India’s representative had said in a statement, “One cherished and valuable aspect of the inclusive political life in India, the largest democracy of the world, is the tradition to express grievances through peaceful assembly and marches. Organised, non-violent and popular marches by the people of India was the key weapon in the struggle for independence. Naturally the right to peaceful assembly has been recognised as a fundamental right by the Indian Constitution.

• Article 19 of Indian Constitution guarantees to citizens of India the right to assemble, peacefully without arms, and the right to form associations and unions. The Supreme Court has ruled that the Constitution also guarantees the right to peaceful protest.”

What EPFO 3.0 proposes: Pension cover for all, social security for gig workers

Syllabus:

Preliminary Examination: Economic and Social Development

Mains Examination: General Studies III: Indian Economy and issues relating to planning, mobilization, of resources, growth, development and employment.

What’s the ongoing story: A universal pension cover for all workers with option of either annuity or systematic withdrawal plan, first-time social security contributions for unorganised sector workers including gig and platform workers, an upgradation of tech ecosystem to incorporate core banking solution (CBS) — these are some of the key changes being planned by the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) as part of its 3.0 reforms phase.

Key Points to Ponder:

• What is Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO)?

• Employees now get a new set of instructions from the EPFO. What specifically is included in the instruction manual?

• How Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 2026 is different from the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952?

• What is the significance of contributory social security in India’s labour market?

• What is the Code on social security?

• What are the major reforms introduced under the EPF Scheme, 2026?

• How the Code on Social Security, 2020 seeks to modernize India’s labour welfare framework?

• What are the challenges in extending effective social security coverage to contract and informal workers?

• Know the role of provident fund reforms in promoting inclusive economic growth.

Key Takeaways:

• Over the last one year, the retirement fund body has worked on improving access to funds and easier claims settlement under EPFO 2.0, which has now taken shape in the form of a revamped portal with a centralised database merging 123 regional databases ensuring timely interest credit and visibility of eligible balance for withdrawal to members.

• The EPFO is now set to move towards the next phase of reforms through a CBS-enabled tech platform, a shift that has been seen as necessary to help it navigate payments for social security schemes covering the complete range of India’s workforce — over 60 crore workers, out of which over three-quarters are in the unorganised sector, with limited or no pension coverage.

• CBS is a centralised payments software which forms the backbone of banks in India allowing operations like deposits, withdrawals, in real time across all branches.

• The new pension cover will have a defined contribution framework with contributions from multiple sources including workers themselves, employers, government co-contributions for lower-income workers, aggregators in the case of gig and platform workers, and corporate social responsibility (CSR) or third-party funds. This is the first time that the EPFO is considering such forms of contributions or withdrawals at the time of retirement: presently, it only allows advance claims or partial withdrawals for certain categories such as education, illness, housing, and marriage during the membership tenure, or a lumpsum final settlement at the time of retirement.

Do You Know:

• Global models are being studied to incorporate similar features such as that of Singapore, which has a deferred annuity scheme that sets aside savings not just for retirement but also for housing and healthcare.

• Singapore’s social security scheme, Central Provident Fund (CPF), relies not just on individual CPF contributions for the retirement income as apart from a contribution of 20% of the salary to CPF, individual efforts are supplemented by employers, loved ones, and the government, as per the information on the Singapore government website. Unlike pension schemes in other countries, CPF members have a differential interest rate, with members earning an interest of up to 6% for those aged 55 and above, and 5% for those aged below 55.

• As the EPFO expects around 2.5 crore gig workers and building and other construction workers (BOCW) over the next five years, the pension scheme is also being designed keeping in mind their inclusion into social security coverage for the first time. The scheme will incorporate “one-to-many mapping” where one Universal Account Number (UAN) will be registered with multiple employers and aggregators, showing total PF and pension contributions from all sources for these workers while maintaining their employer-wise breakdowns.

• The EPFO system plans to allow third-party contributions like NGOs, individuals, donor organisations, CSR, and track all contributions under each UAN with a configurable upper limit. The new pension initiative would operationalise this through flexible co-contribution models, ensuring inclusion of delivery partners, drivers, and other platform workers.

• The EPFO 3.0 phase will also pave the way for PF contributions for all unorganised sector workers and gig workers, in line with the Code on Social Security that brings gig and platform workers into the social security net for the first time. The Code mandates aggregator contributions of 1-2% of annual turnover for social security, with the total contribution not exceeding 5% of the amount payable by the aggregator.

Hormuz crisis: Crude imports surge 60%; net oil, gas imports up 45%

Syllabus:

Preliminary Examination: Current events of national and international importance.

Mains Examination: General Studies II: Effect of policies and politics of developed and developing countries on India’s interests.

What’s the ongoing story: India’s crude oil import bill surged by over 60% on a year-on-year (y-o-y) basis in the first quarter of the current financial year even as import volumes dipped slightly amid supply tightness and elevated prices due to the West Asia crisis and stifled energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, as per provisional data from the petroleum ministry.

Key Points to Ponder:

• How the Strait of Hormuz has emerged as one of the world’s most critical geopolitical chokepoints in the recent

scenario?

• How the Hormuz crisis demonstrates that supply chain resilience is as important as military preparedness?

• How rising crude oil prices affect the Indian economy.

• What has been India’s energy security strategy in the light of recurring geopolitical conflicts?

• How Strategic Petroleum Reserves can help in ensuring India’s energy security?

• India’s policy of “Strategic Autonomy” in the context of the Hormuz crisis-discuss

• How conflicts in West Asia affect India’s foreign policy and economic security

• ‘India’s dependence on imported fossil fuels remains its biggest strategic vulnerability’-do you agree?

• What are the challenges before India in achieving energy independence by 2047?

• Connect the dots between—Oil prices, Inflation, Exchange rate, Current Account Deficit, Fiscal deficit, GDP Growth

Key Takeaways:

• Liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports and petroleum product exports declined in volume terms, while rising in value.

• Overall, the country’s net oil and gas imports jumped 45% in value from year-ago levels, underscoring the adverse economic impact of the West Asia crisis on energy import-dependent India. The country depends on imports to meet over 88% of its crude oil requirement and about half of its consumption of natural gas, which is imported as LNG, or super-chilled gas. Despite depending on imported oil and gas, India is a net exporter of petroleum products due to its massive oil refining capacity, while it also imports some petroleum products like liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

• Around 40% of India’s crude oil imports, 60% of its LNG imports, and a whopping 90% of its LPG imports came from West Asia through the strait. Apart from grappling with physical supply tightness due to the Strait of Hormuz crisis, the resultant surge in international prices forced India to import oil and gas at extremely high rates, as the country has been prioritising supply security over price considerations.

• The June MoU between the US and Iran brought a sigh of relief for India and the global energy market, but the renewed conflict in the Gulf following the pact’s effective collapse is emerging as a major concern as energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz have crashed again after a short-lived three-week recovery.

India’s oil & gas trade math

• According to latest provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), crude oil imports

in the June quarter rose 61.2% y-o-y to $49.8 billion, even as import volumes declined 4.5% to 59.8 million tonnes, or about 438 million barrels.

• This translates to about $113 per barrel as the average landed price of imported crude oil in the June quarter, up from around $67 per barrel in the corresponding quarter of last year. The PPAC data shows that India’s dependence on imported oil in April-June was 89.1%, flat on a y-o-y basis.

Do You Know:

• Petroleum product imports declined almost 42% in volume terms to 7.1 million tonnes, as supply of major petroleum products that India imports — like LPG — were impacted by the West Asia war. In value terms, the decline in petroleum product imports was relatively lower — down 27.6% to $4.2 billion — due to high international prices.

• India’s petroleum product export volumes declined by a fourth to 11.3 million tonnes in April-June from 15 million tonnes in the corresponding period of last year as domestic fuel supplies took precedence amid the global supply crunch. Nonetheless, the exports surged nearly 40% in value due to the jump in international petroleum fuel prices.

• As India imports 1.8-2 billion barrels of crude oil a year, every $1-per-barrel increase in oil prices bumps up the country’s oil import bill by up to $2 billion on an annualised basis. According to a March report by Nomura, India is among the three most vulnerable Asian economies to high oil prices in terms of import bill and current account balances, the other two being Thailand and South Korea. It said that every 10% oil price increase typically widens India’s current account deficit by 0.4% of the GDP.
